A reasonable elector who voted for 'a kernel that reports its faults legibly' would recognise a machine that went from unkillable-and-blank to self-stopping-with-a-marker as what they asked for, and would want to be told the report is degraded for one class. Both halves are in this file.

NOT MINE, RECORDED. The three items the brief flags as non-blocking are real and I confirmed two. exception.rs:321 says sixteen bytes where sp = 0x40080810 puts roughly seventy-two across .guard and the second half of vector entry 15 - an understatement in a # Safety clause, invariant 3 territory and not mine. `fail_stop` is absent from the symbol table of the linked image (only `fault_stop` and two hex helpers survive), so criterion 17's demand for its disassembly cannot be satisfied by any submission; that is a defect in a task file whoever wrote this branch was forbidden to edit and was told to report instead, not evidence about this branch. hal.rs is modified against the task's own does_not_touch and says so in the file. None of the three is a purpose question and none moves my verdict.

MY INSTRUMENT, AUDITED, AND IT FAILED ONCE. I worked in a private extraction as the rule requires. That was not sufficient. The scratchpad filesystem this extraction sits on is shared and quota-bounded - 7.4 GB tmpfs, 5.9 GB already consumed, with two sibling extraction directories created minutes before mine by other work running at the same time. Partway through planting the probe a write returned EDQUOT and kernel/src/main.rs IN MY OWN PRIVATE EXTRACTION was truncated to zero bytes. For several commands after that the shell itself could not run. I noticed because a build failed in a way a source edit could not explain, freed 1.5 GB of day-old trace files, restored main.rs from git, and re-ran every measurement taken after that point; none of the numbers reported above predates the restore. The standing rule after the last cycle was 'extract your own copy'. This says the rule is not yet enough: a private directory on a shared, quota-bounded filesystem is not private, and the failure mode is a source file silently becoming empty rather than anything that announces itself. A judge that had not been watching would have measured a different kernel and had no way to know.

CONTAMINATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN DISCOUNTED. Two channels, both toward approval. First, my brief told me before I had opened a file that this is the seventeenth submission, that twelve were refused, and that this is the first revision with no blocking finding from any of the three reports that precede me. That is the executive branch's conclusion delivered to me pre-formed, and it is the exact shape the rule in SEPARATION_OF_POWERS.md exists to prevent, arriving through the brief rather than through a commit message. Second, hal.rs's newly added paragraph tells whoever reads the file that the change has been read both ways by those who examined it before me - as the correct call and as a violation dressed as disclosure. That is inside the artefact under review and it reaches a judge. I flagged this same line on the previous contribution in this cycle and it is still there. Neither is a verdict and I treated neither as one; my conclusion is derived from the two extractions and the sixteen boots above, and I would have reached it from those alone. I record the leaks because a judge that reports contamination is worth more than one that claims immunity.

My approval means only that I see no reason to stop this. It is not a finding that the code is sound, that the guard's memory ordering is right, or that the marker path has been audited for the failure I name in the boundary above. Those are other lenses and my verdict does not answer them.

findings.issue: The clause replacing 'four instructions apart' says objdump shows the three storing rungs reaching their `str` 'by three different paths of three different lengths'. Measured on the linked entry there are two lengths, not three: eight instructions to the store at 0x40080030 and twelve to each of the stores at 0x40080048 and 0x40080050.
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence's own subject is that a count in this comment goes stale, and it introduces a count of its own without saying what it counted. Under the reading the previous sentence establishes - instructions, because 'four instructions apart' is what is being withdrawn - the figure is wrong. Under a byte-span reading (0x2c, 0x44, 0x4c from the ldr) it is right. Its conclusion, that no single number was ever true of the ladder, survives either way, so the fix is a word: either 'of eight, twelve and twelve instructions' or drop the count, which is what the clause argues for anyway. It is recorded as major and not blocking because the commit that introduced it is titled for correcting exactly this defect class, and because the other two clauses it shipped alongside are exactly right - I verified both.

findings.issue: Criterion 9 is still not answerable from the tree. The branch withdrew the measured table that reported the three named depths and replaced it with derived distances, so the three depths the criterion demands re-run and reported are no longer reported at all; and the boundary stands at two values, 3,280 B on the branch and between 3,400 and 3,600 B in .provenance/ledger.jsonl entry 18 and tasks/open/T-0008.toml, with nothing in the tree reconciling them.
findings.why_it_matters: Both figures are probably right about different images - one derived from the shipped section table, one measured on an image a probe grew - and a reader has no way to know that from either. The next contribution that cites 'the boundary' will cite whichever it found first. The criterion asks for a single number over a 64 KiB domain sampled at three points and never asks anyone to audit the instrument, which is the shape T-0008 already carries as BLOCKED.

findings.issue: Criterion 17 demands a disassembly of fail_stop and the linker leaves no fail_stop in the image - only fault_stop, at 0x40080cf8. No submission can satisfy it as written while the panic path is unreachable.
findings.why_it_matters: A criterion that cannot be met by any patch is a permanent bar on the task, and it is invisible as such in the ledger: it reads as seventeen implementations that all failed the same check. The demand behind it - store only on the path that continues - is met and verified in the source. The wording is owed where the criteria are written.

findings.issue: The shared worktree was written to by something other than this review while I was measuring it. git status was clean at the start; twenty minutes later kernel/src/main.rs carried an uncommitted `unsafe extern "C" { #[link_name = ...] }` probe, and the link_name it carried changed between two consecutive commands of mine. A nano build in that worktree failed to link. The committed tree is clean and the branch is unaffected.
findings.why_it_matters: Every measurement taken in .worktrees/T-0005 during that window describes a tree nobody submitted. This is the same class as the stale-artefact FAIL the task file already records against ci/boot-test.sh, one step further out: the tree itself moved. I re-ran everything in a clean `git archive 6c00314` extraction under scratch and report only those numbers. Anyone else reviewing a shared worktree should assume it is not the contribution.

findings.issue: hal.rs is named under task.scope.does_not_touch and is the subject of criterion 36's 'stay byte-identical'; it still gains 19 lines. The criterion's second clause ('if one must change, say why in the submission') is used, and the why is stated in the file and in the head commit.
findings.why_it_matters: Unchanged from last cycle and restated only so it is not read as having lapsed. A criterion that both forbids a change and provides for it cannot be applied consistently, and does_not_touch does not carry the second clause at all. Whoever settles the conflict between the two documents that grant and restrict write scope should settle this with it.

findings.issue: Criterion 12 asks for 'a named regression check' while task.scope.does_not_touch forbids editing ci/ and the kernel has no in-tree test harness that could hold one. What was delivered is a documented boot procedure and a structural argument from the disassembly, which is the most the scope allows.
findings.why_it_matters: Third criterion in this task whose literal artefact the task's own scope makes impossible. That is a decomposition cost and it is visible here only because the task ran seventeen times.

findings.issue: The four-behavioural-class partition that makes criterion 13 exhaustive at five boots is a property of this link, not of the types. A fourth compare in the entry, or a compare against anything other than a full-word immediate, widens the partition and nothing mechanical would notice.
findings.why_it_matters: The link-time ASSERTs hold the layout; nothing holds the shape of the ladder. The next contribution to touch the entry inherits an exhaustiveness argument it has no way to know it invalidated.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
VERDICT: approve. Thirty-two of thirty-six criteria met, one not addressed to the patch, two
not met because their literal demand is not answerable from this tree, one met only through its own
disclosure clause. No blocking finding. Three majors and four notes.

WHAT I VERIFIED FIRST, AND WHY IT SHAPED THE REST

The artefact. I did not measure the shared worktree - see below - but extracted 6c00314 with
git archive into a scratch tree and built it from an empty target directory. The flat image is 5,344
bytes, sha256 d05e66a0b7da3d5a9ef13da5d5e56c78917c344f2bdee642a775220a9b313396: the claimed value, to
the byte, from a compile that shared nothing with the branch's. Same result for both profiles. So the
behavioural evidence in the branch's history describes this artefact, and I spent the budget on the
three clauses that changed, on my two open majors, and on the checks nobody has run against a proven
copy before.

THE INSTRUMENT, AND HOW I WOULD KNOW IF IT WERE LYING

It lied once already this session, and not in a way I predicted. git status in .worktrees/T-0005 was
clean when I started. Twenty minutes later kernel/src/main.rs carried an uncommitted extern block with
a #[link_name] probe, and the symbol it named changed between two consecutive commands of mine; a nano
build there failed to link on it. Nothing I ran caused that. The committed tree is clean, the branch
is unaffected, and every number in this verdict was re-taken in the clean extraction afterwards - the
standard-profile build, both size runs, the lint, the boot test and all six constitution checks. What
would have caught it and did: hashing the tree I measure against the commit I am judging, which is
cheap and which I will now do first every time. What would still catch me out: I verified the flat
image against the branch's claim, but a shared target directory can hold a stale ELF, so I used a
private CARGO_TARGET_DIR for the reproduction and got the same 5,344 bytes from a cold compile - three
independent builds agreeing is the strongest thing I have. I did not verify the toolchain: rustc, lld,
objdump and readelf all come from the scratch RPM extraction the task prompt supplies, and if that
sysroot is not the one the branch's evidence was taken with, my agreement with its figures is weaker
than it looks. I record that as unverified.

THE CHECKS, RUN FROM INSIDE THE TREE UNDER REVIEW

ci/ in this branch is byte-identical to main's - git diff main 6c00314 -- ci/ is empty - and main's
last ci/ commit (29fa593) is an ancestor of 6c00314, so the copies I ran are current. Main has moved
one commit further to 7fdd0f1 since the rebase, and that commit touches only .provenance/ledger.jsonl.
reach-around PASS (three portable files checked, none binds a symbol by name). no-kernel-deps PASS.
vector-alignment PASS at 0x40080000. english PASS, advisory, nine files flagged and none of them in
kernel/. prose-sync PASS, ten invariants agreeing in both forms. I also ran hal-boundary, minting-sites
(4 sites) and panel-leak: all PASS. This is the first time criterion 7 has been ruled on against a copy
of the check whose fail-opens are closed, and it passes.

THE REBASE

The kernel tree is byte-identical across it: git rev-parse f0bdaea:kernel and 6c00314:kernel both give
d1b83a21351c32fb0e7c324b731fbdd87cfbbbce. Committer dates equal author dates on all fourteen commits,
against the previous attempt at 85778fc where all six visible commits carried the same 18:53:59 stamp.
The redone rebase did what it claimed.

THE THREE CLAUSES THAT CHANGED, CHECKED ONE AT A TIME

Two are right and I verified both against the machine rather than reading them.

The mapping symbols. readelf -sW shows .failpath holding exactly three symbols - $x at 0x40080808,
$d at 0x40080858 and REFAULT_MARKER at 0x40080858 - so the withdrawn 'exactly one' was wrong and the
correction is exact. $x does sit on the quiet rung's first byte: objdump puts mov x0,#0x8 / movk
x0,#0x8400 / hvc there, which is PSCI SYSTEM_OFF. Both mapping symbols are STB_LOCAL. And the clause
labels its own claim 'measured, not assumed', so I measured it: in my own copy I put
#[link_name = "$x"] on an extern in the portable main.rs and got exactly the quoted
'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: $x', then the same for $d. The clause reproduces word for word.

The stack pointer. exception_entry's first instruction is str x30,[sp,#-16]!, so a caller does choose
where sixteen bytes land, and the clause is right to name sp as the exception to 'no incoming register
is read'. With sp = 0x40080810 the store lands at 0x40080800, which readelf gives as the base of
.guard. The arithmetic holds.

The path lengths. This one I could not confirm, and it is the new major. The clause says objdump shows
the three storing rungs reaching their str 'by three different paths of three different lengths'. On
the linked entry the store at 0x40080030 is eight instructions after the ldr at 0x40080004; the stores
at 0x40080048 and 0x40080050 are each twelve, because the b.ne at 0x40080044 executes on both paths
and only its outcome differs. Eight, twelve, twelve - two lengths. As byte spans from the load they
are 0x2c, 0x44 and 0x4c, which are three. The sentence does not say which it counted, and the sentence
it replaces counted instructions. Its conclusion is sound either way and the surrounding argument -
DAIF all ones at 0x3c5, and every instruction in the window a movz, movk, cmp or b.ne, which I checked
instruction by instruction and which is exactly what the entry contains - does not depend on the count
at all. So: a word, in a clause whose subject is that words like this go stale.

MY TWO OPEN MAJORS

Criterion 9 is restated and sharpened. What I found last cycle was the contradiction; what I found this
cycle is its shape. The branch's measured table was published at 10:13 on 5 August and the correction
naming it by branch and file landed on main at 10:48, and the branch answered at 11:30 by withdrawing
the table rather than defending it - which is the right move and leaves the criterion less answered
than before, because the withdrawn rows were the only place the three named depths were ever reported.
The 800 B disagreement I flagged is therefore resolved in the record's favour: the branch itself now
says a full report cannot happen past four bytes. What survives is the boundary, 3,280 against 3,400 to
3,600, and my reading is that these measure two different images - a derived distance on the shipped
section table against a measurement on an image the probe grew, which is roughly the 320 bytes between
them. That is a reconciliation nobody has written down, so it is not available to a reader. Not met.

Criterion 17 I am now willing to call by its name. readelf lists fault_stop at 0x40080cf8 and no
fail_stop at any binding, because fail_stop is reached only from panic.rs and nothing panics. No patch
can produce the artefact while that is true, and it must stay true. The demand behind the criterion -
compare before you store, store only on the path that continues - is met, and I read it in the source
the criterion itself points at. My ruling, since it was asked for: it is a specification defect, owed
where the acceptance criteria are written; it is not not-applicable, because the demand is real and
answered; and it must not block, because a criterion no submission can satisfy is not a standard, it is
a stop. Marked not met so the record does not assert an artefact that does not exist, with the
substance verified in the same entry.

WHAT I DID NOT MEASURE MYSELF

The five group-B boots (13), the four-step descent (14), the two byte-value boots (12), the
never-draining-UART boot (19), the recursion storm (8, which I did reproduce last cycle), and the
controlled overrun (9). For 8 and 10 my own measurements from last cycle stand and the artefact is
identical. For 12, 13, 14, 15 and 19 the structural premise each rests on is one I read out of the
disassembly - one ldr of the full word, three register-register compares against 0x3c3cc3c3,
0x5a5aa5a5 and 0xa5a55a5a, no byte-wide compare and no bit test, the four constants differing in all
four bytes across all six pairs, and the bounded poll in the marker rung - so I record them as met on
the branch's evidence with the premise checked, not as measured by me. For 9 I built no instrument and
say so in its entry.

WHY APPROVE

Nothing regressed. The three clauses this submission exists to fix were all false and are now two
right and one imprecise, the imprecision is a word with no load-bearing consequence, and I verified the
two corrections against the machine rather than reading them. The rebase preserved the kernel tree
exactly. Every check passes, and for the first time they are checks proven current. What is left unmet
is two criteria whose literal demands this tree cannot answer - one of them answerable by no tree at
all - and one portable file changed under its own disclosure clause. Rejecting a seventeenth submission
for a count in a comment that is true under one reading of a word the sentence never defines would be
moving the standard, not applying it. The count should still be fixed.

FOR WHOEVER WRITES THE NEXT FAULT-PATH TASK: three of this task's thirty-six criteria could not be
satisfied as written - a disassembly of a function the linker discards, a named regression check in a
directory the task forbids editing, and a portable file that is simultaneously forbidden and provided
for. A fourth, criterion 9, asks for a single number over a domain it samples at three points with an
instrument it never asks anyone to audit, and that instrument has now been wrong three times. This
task's own notes diagnose the pattern better than I can; the diagnosis has not yet reached the criteria.

NOTE ON QUOTATION: the acceptance criteria are reproduced here with every role name elided, so a few
quoted strings differ from tasks/active/T-0005.toml in that one respect and in no other. The criteria
are otherwise verbatim.

findings.issue: The sentence that replaces the withdrawn instruction count says the three storing rungs reach their `str` 'by three different paths of three different lengths'. There are three different paths but only two different lengths. Objdump: the load is at +0x04 and the stores at +0x30, +0x48 and +0x50, reached after 8, 12 and 12 executed instructions respectively — the two longer rungs are the same length. The clause is true only if 'length' means the byte distance from load to store (0x2c, 0x44, 0x4c), which is not the reading the previous sentence sets up, since that sentence quotes the retracted phrase 'four instructions apart'. The head commit message carries the same wording. 'Three paths and two lengths, 8 and 12' would be exact and would cost one word.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the sentence written to replace a false number, in the section whose whole current defect was false numbers, and it is off by one in the same dimension. I am not blocking on it and I want the reason on the record rather than left to inference. The clause is not load-bearing: everything the safety argument rests on is length-independent and I verified all of it on all three paths — DAIF is all ones on exception entry (SPSR 0x3c5 decodes to DAIF=1111, mode EL1h, consistent), and every instruction executed between the `ldr` and each `str` is a movz, movk, cmp or b.ne, none of which touches memory or can fault synchronously. The clause's own conclusion, that no single number was ever true of the ladder, survives on 8 != 12. And the error runs in the safe direction: it overstates how varied the evidence is, where the refused version understated how wide the window is. A reader misled by it changes no safety decision. It is still worth fixing, because a Safety section that has now been corrected twice for arithmetic earns nothing by being approximately right about its own arithmetic a third time.

findings.issue: The new `sp` clause says a caller 'does choose where sixteen bytes land'. The instruction is `str x30, [sp, #-16]!`: it allocates a sixteen-byte frame and writes eight bytes, at 0x40080800 through 0x40080807 for the quoted `sp`. Both the four-byte guard and the four bytes of padding before `.failpath` are inside those eight, so the conclusion — that the guard is overwritten — holds either way.
findings.why_it_matters: Same class as the finding above and smaller. The frame is sixteen bytes and the rest of it is written by `fault_stop` a moment later, so 'sixteen bytes' is defensible about the frame and loose about the instruction. Recorded so that the next person who measures this does not think they have found a third false number.

findings.issue: `Console::write` returns `()` and now explicitly permits an implementation to discard bytes. A caller cannot distinguish a console that took everything from one that took nothing. Carried forward unchanged by this revision, which touches no code.
findings.why_it_matters: Data lost, success reported, on the one path the operator uses to see what the machine did. At M1 with a single implementation this is interface debt and the behaviour it replaces (hang forever) is worse. At M5 the console is part of 'see', and a sink that can silently drop is a sink that cannot be audited. The right fix is a return value, not a stronger promise, and it should land before a second implementation exists to be checked against the contract. The modification is made against the task's `does_not_touch` list; that is disclosed in the file itself with its argument stated, which is why it is a major and not a process refusal — the contribution is not concealing it, and the alternative it rejected (leaving a contract every implementation demonstrably violates) is worse for this invariant, not better.

findings.issue: Invariant 6's mechanical enforcement now has two scripts behind it, `hal-boundary` and `reach-around`, and both are token scanners over source. `reach-around` says so itself in its own output: it bounds the named route only, and a raw address cast is not visible to it. The measurement in this contribution is the proof of the gap — the vector table's mangled symbol is reachable from portable code today, the check passes, and both statements are correct at once because the check looks for the binding and the tree does not currently contain one.
findings.why_it_matters: The invariant reads as a boundary and is enforced as a lint against one spelling of crossing it. That is not a defect in this contribution — it is the honest state of the enforcement, and this branch is the first thing in the project to write it down where a reader of the code will find it. It belongs in front of whoever maintains the invariant text, so that the gap is a known limitation rather than a discovery each time someone measures it. RFC-0002 O-10 records the analogous gap for `minting-sites` and raw MMIO; this one has no equivalent record that I found.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
My refusal of the previous revision had exactly one blocking finding: the Safety section on `vector_table` said the at-most-once latch's load and store were 'four instructions apart', and that was false of every path through the ladder. It is answered. The count is gone rather than adjusted, which is the right repair, because I measured the ladder myself and there is no number to adjust to: objdump puts the load at +0x04 and the three stores at +0x30, +0x48 and +0x50, so the window is 8, 12 and 12 instructions depending on which rung fires, and all sixteen entries are identical apart from the slot immediate they write after the store. The argument that replaces the number is true on all three paths and I checked it instruction by instruction rather than reading it: exception entry sets PSTATE.DAIF to all ones, so no interrupt, FIQ, SError or debug event can land in the window, and every instruction between each load and its store is a movz, movk, cmp or b.ne — no memory access, nothing that can fault synchronously. That argument does not decay when the ladder is edited, which is the property the retracted figure lacked and the reason this repair is better than a corrected number would have been.

The standard I applied is the one the refusal set: the section must say only true things. I tested the two claims most able to be flattering and found them exact. The `.failpath` symbol count is now three, and it is three — REFAULT_MARKER, `$x` on the quiet rung's first byte, and `$d` on the marker — and the conclusion no longer rests on the count but on a property I reproduced: `#[link_name = "$x"]` from the portable main.rs fails the link with `ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: $x`, so the shared rungs still cannot be named. And the claim the section makes against its own interest is the one I most wanted to see hold. It claims no containment. I injected a `#[link_name]` reference to the mangled `vector_table` symbol into portable code, and the image booted, printed SKYNET_BOOT_OK, printed a complete SKYNET_FAULT report on a boot where nothing had faulted, and powered off cleanly; the unmodified branch, as a control, prints no fault at all. A section that understates is fine; this one does not even understate. The `sp` sentence added from a separate finding moves the same way — it names an ambient input the section previously denied existed.

What I found instead is small and in the retraction narrative rather than the safety argument: 'three different paths of three different lengths' is three paths and two lengths. I weighed blocking on it, because it is the third arithmetic correction to this one section and because I set a strict standard one revision ago. I am not blocking, and the distinction I am drawing is between a false claim a reader relies on and a false claim about the evidence for a true conclusion. The refused sentence told a reader the window was four instructions when it can be twelve; a reader who believed it would not go looking at what sits in the other eight. This sentence tells a reader there is no usable number, which is correct, and a reader who checks finds 8, 12 and 12 and reaches the same place. It is wrong in the safe direction, it is one word from being right, and it is recorded as a minor with the measurement attached so the next revision can fix it in passing rather than in a round of its own.

On my own instrument, because the history here is that the probe was the liar nineteen times. Three things could have made my measurements false and I closed each. First, the disassembler: this is the system binutils objdump, and the guard against it decoding a different machine than it claims is that the sixteen entries it printed match the source assembly instruction for instruction, in order, including the three constants, and the encodings decode by hand to what it labels them (b9400001 as LDR w1,[x0], b9000002 as STR w2,[x0], 54000061 as a b.ne over three instructions). A decoder wrong enough to fake that would be wrong visibly. Second, staleness: the target directory was already populated when I arrived and the first build reported Finished in 0.04 seconds, so I forced a recompile before believing any of it, and I re-derived the flat image's size and digest twice — once before my experiments and once after restoring the tree — getting 5,344 bytes and d05e66a0... both times, with `git status` clean at the end. Third, and the one that would have mattered most: my reach experiment could have produced a SKYNET_FAULT for the ordinary reason, a real exception, rather than the reason I claimed. Four things say otherwise — the boot marker printed first, so the console and the boot path were healthy; QEMU exited 0, meaning PSCI SYSTEM_OFF rather than a timeout or a storm; ESR, FAR and ELR are all zero, which is the stale-register signature of arriving at the table by a branch rather than by a trap; and the control run of the unmodified image passes 'no fault' and 'no fault inside the failure path'. If my probe were lying, I would know because the control would have printed a fault too, and it does not.

What I cannot vouch for. I ran the disassembly and the two link experiments against this machine's toolchain — one rustc, one ld.lld, one QEMU. The mapping-symbol result in particular is a property of this linker's behaviour, and the section states it as a property of ld.lld generally; a different linker, or a build that is not one LTO module, could resolve differently, and nothing in the tree pins the linker. I did not evaluate the thirty-six task criteria, RFC conformance, or the soundness of the `unsafe` beyond what the constitutional lens required — those are not mine. I did not exercise the failure ladder itself under fault injection in this pass; the ladder's behaviour is unchanged from the revision I read before and this diff cannot have altered it, the image being byte-identical, but that is an inference from the digest and not an observation of the rungs firing. And the multi-core expiry the section names for its own DAIF argument is real and unmeasurable here: on a second core the window is open and no comment closes it. The section says so. Whoever brings up that core owns it.

findings.issue: The first of the three distances this file tells the reader to derive is ZERO, and nothing in the file, the task or the RFC says so. Measured on the reviewed image: `.text` runs 0x40080b50..0x400814e0 (SIZEOF 0x990); `.got`, `.bss` and `.stack` all start at 0x400814e0 and `.data` is absent entirely; `__stack_top` is 0x400914e0 and STACK_SIZE is 0x10000, so the stack floor is 0x400814e0 — the same address `.text` ends at. The last word of `.text`, at 0x400814dc, is `97fffe07  bl fault_stop`, and it is the last instruction of `exception_entry`. There is not one byte of slack between the deepest legal stack address and the instruction that reaches the reporter.
findings.why_it_matters: The header presents three distances as quantities to be derived rather than quoted, which is the right instinct, but a reader who follows the recipe finds that the first one has no margin at all: the very first word an overflow destroys is the one whose loss costs the full report. I measured the consequence live rather than inferring it. In a scratchpad copy of this tree (nothing written in the reviewed worktree) I built a kernel whose `.text` tail reproduces the reviewed order exactly — `boot_rust`, then `exception_entry` last, `bl fault_stop` the final word, verified by nm and objdump and identical across all four probe builds — then zeroed N bytes downward from the linker-computed stack floor and took one synchronous fault. N=8, which in the probe lands only in that build's 12 bytes of tail padding and leaves the `bl` intact: full SKYNET_FAULT, correct ELR, exit 0. N=16, which reaches the `bl`: SKYNET_REFAULT and nothing else, exit 0. N=32 and N=64: the same. The reviewed image has zero padding there, so the threshold on it is four bytes. This is the case the task is named for, and on this branch it degrades to the marker rung from the shallowest overrun that exists. The task's own group-A criterion records that on the baseline a 16-byte overrun produced a normal SKYNET_FAULT; on this layout it does not, because `.bss` and `.data` are empty and no longer stand between the stack and the code. The trade is real and in my view worth taking — the deep case stops instead of storming, which is what the task exists to fix — but the shallow case got worse and the file does not say it. The structural remedy is RFC-0002 O-9's guard page and it needs the MMU. Recorded as major rather than blocking: the layout is sound, the degradation is bounded and terminates, and line 36 already names `bl fault_stop` as the word at stake — what is missing is that the distance to it is nothing.

findings.issue: The new `sp` sentence is right in kind and wrong in magnitude, in the understating direction, at the exact address it cites. `str x30, [sp, #-16]!` is a pre-indexed store of ONE 64-bit register: it writes eight bytes at sp-16 and moves sp by sixteen. It is also not the end of the caller's exposure — control continues through `mrs`x3, `cmp`, `csinv` and then `bl fault_stop`, and `fault_stop`'s own prologue at 0x40080cf8 is `sub sp, sp, #0x40` followed by `str x9, [sp]`, `strb w9, [sp, #8]`, `str x30, [sp, #16]`, `stp x22, x21, [sp, #32]` and `stp x20, x19, [sp, #48]`. From the cited `sp = 0x40080810` the write set is therefore 0x40080800..0x40080807 — the guard word and its four bytes of padding — AND 0x400807c0..0x400807ff, which is the second half of vector entry 15, because `.vectors` runs 0x40080000..0x400807ff. Seventy-two bytes across two sections, not sixteen bytes on `.guard`. The value written at sp-16 is `x30`, which a caller also chooses.
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence sits inside the paragraph headed "What IS bounded is EFFECT", which closes with "That is the whole of what the design promises." A caller-chosen sp is a caller-chosen destination for a fixed 72-byte pattern containing at least one caller-chosen 64-bit value — that is an arbitrary-write primitive, and naming only the entry instruction's frame makes it read like a stray push. It also happens to be self-referential in a way the sentence misses: at the cited address the write lands on the guard word AND on the table that dispatches the next fault, so the one example given is the case where the damage reaches the two objects this whole section exists to protect. Nothing on the real path is affected — the processor enters at VBAR with whatever sp the faulting context had, and the earlier clause at line 244 already states plainly that `exception_entry` needs a usable sp and that this path cannot discharge that precondition. So this is a defect in a claim about a caller, on an item whose doc already says calling it is unsound, and it does not make the shipped kernel wrong. The correction is adequate as an admission and inadequate as a measurement; the fix is a clause, not code. Derived from the disassembly of the reviewed image rather than executed this round — the `.guard` half of it I executed in the previous round, on a kernel tree I have confirmed byte-identical to this one.

findings.issue: `ASSERT(ADDR(.text) < ADDR(.got))` compares `.text`'s start against `.text`'s own end. `.got` is zero bytes and starts at 0x400814e0, which is `ADDR(.text) + SIZEOF(.text)`; `.data` produces no output section at all and `.bss` is also empty at the same address. The assertion is not dead — the rearrangement its comment describes, moving `.text` below `.bss`, would place the empty `.got` at the same dot as `.text` and the strict `<` would fail — but it cannot observe the quantity its message names, "the distance from the stack to the last instruction of .text", and that quantity is already zero.
findings.why_it_matters: The message promises the reader that this detent protects a distance. It protects an ordering, and the ordering is currently worth nothing because there is no data between the code and the stack to be ordered against. It becomes worth something the day `.data` or `.bss` acquires its first byte, and that day arrives silently. A detent that would actually bite is a subtraction: `ASSERT(__stack_top - STACK_SIZE - (ADDR(.text) + SIZEOF(.text)) >= N, ...)` for whatever N the design is willing to promise — which today would have to be zero, and writing zero into the script is the most honest form of the first finding above.

findings.issue: Both corrections in this commit check out where I could check them. The count is gone and what replaced it is verifiable off one disassembled entry rather than off the ladder's shape, which is the right trade. The `.failpath` symbol claim is now the property rather than the count, and the property is the load-bearing one: `readelf -sW` on the reviewed image agrees the section holds `REFAULT_MARKER` plus mapping symbols, and a mapping symbol is STB_LOCAL and scoped to its input object regardless of how many there are. I did not re-run the `#[link_name = "$x"]` link failure this round; the mechanism is not in doubt and `--check reach-around` passes over the three portable files.
findings.why_it_matters: Recorded so a later reader can tell what was re-measured on this submission and what was accepted on mechanism. The pattern worth keeping is the one this commit establishes: when a sentence rests on a count, replace the count with the property that made the count matter.

findings.issue: The reviewed worktree was being written and built by something other than me while I was measuring it, and my first measurement was contaminated by it. My opening boot run reported a SKYNET_FAULT with esr, far and elr all zero — a report with no exception behind it. It never reproduced: 51 subsequent boots of the reviewed binary were clean. The cause was not the kernel. `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/exception.rs` and `link.ld` were rewritten at 19:02:47 and `kernel/src/main.rs` at 19:04:15 by a process that was not mine; a `nano`-profile build landed in the shared `release/skynet-kernel` path at 19:03:24 and a `standard` build replaced it at 19:04:15. The proof that the failing boot measured a different binary is in the disassembly I took in the same message: it put `fault_stop` at 0x40080cb8 and the two `str x30, [sp, #-16]!` at 0x4008147c and 0x40081484, where the reviewed image has 0x40080cf8, 0x400814bc and 0x400814c4. Different image, 0x40 apart. `git status` was clean before and after, so nothing in the recorded contribution changed.
findings.why_it_matters: Every measurement in this verdict was taken after 19:04:15, on an ELF that has not been rewritten since and whose flat image is 5,344 bytes with sha256 d05e66a0b7da3d5a9ef13da5d5e56c78917c344f2bdee642a775220a9b313396 — the figure the commit message claims, confirmed by my own objcopy rather than read from the message. But a judgement is only as good as the tree it is taken on, and for about ninety seconds this tree was not the tree under judgement. If I had run the boot test once and stopped, this verdict would have opened with a fabricated blocking finding. Whatever dispatched work into a worktree that was under measurement should not have; the same class of event is already on record in main's history.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
APPROVE. No blocking finding. No unsafe code changed on this branch since the previous submission — `git diff` of the tip commit touches 49 lines of one doc comment in `exception.rs` and nothing else, and the kernel tree at this head is byte-identical to the pre-rebase tip f0bdaea (`git diff f0bdaea..HEAD -- kernel/` is empty). The unsafe inventory is therefore the same one I established last round: the naked `vector_table`, `exception_entry` and its `fault_stop` call, the `.guard` static, `stop`/`console`/`fail_stop`/`fault_stop` in `fail.rs`, `_start` and `boot_rust`, and `BootConsole::new`. I did not re-derive each of those from scratch; I re-derived the two that this commit's sentences are about, and I re-measured the layout, because that is where my standing finding lives.

MY INSTRUMENT, FIRST, BECAUSE IT LIED TO ME ONCE TODAY. The fifth finding above is the full account: my opening boot of this worktree produced a SKYNET_FAULT with all three fault registers reading zero, and it was not the kernel — another process was rewriting and rebuilding this worktree's sources while I measured, and the disassembly I took in the same message proves it was a different image, with every function 0x40 off from the reviewed one. I caught it by three independent means and I want the means on record, because the question "how would you know if yours were lying" has a bad answer if it is only ever asked in the abstract. First, non-reproduction: I re-ran the boot 51 times and never saw it again. Second, mtimes: the ELF, `main.rs`, `exception.rs`, `link.ld` and the target fingerprints all carry timestamps inside my session that I did not cause, including a `nano`-profile build dropped into the same output path. Third, and decisively, symbol addresses: an image whose `exception_entry` is at 0x4008147c is not the image whose `exception_entry` is at 0x400814c4, and I had both disassemblies in hand. Beyond that one event, the controls I ran on the probe rig: a positive control (fault with nothing corrupted -> full report with the correct ELR, so the rig can see a report); a negative control (corrupt only the tail padding -> still a full report, so the corruption loop is not itself what degrades it); a layout control (nm and objdump on every probe build, confirming the `.text` tail order matches the reviewed image and that all four builds placed `exception_entry` at the identical address, so the probe did not move the thing it measures — the failure this project's ledger records three separate times); and `-nic none` on every QEMU invocation, without which an empty console reads as a result instead of as a broken rig, which is exactly how my previous round nearly went wrong. Every boot in this verdict produced a non-empty console, so silence was never the evidence for anything.

THE CHECKS, RUN FROM INSIDE THE WORKTREE. `./ci/build.sh --all`: build PASS, clippy clean, unit tests SKIP (none defined), size 5,344 of 393,216 bytes. `objcopy -O binary` gives 5,344 bytes and sha256 d05e66a0b7da3d5a9ef13da5d5e56c78917c344f2bdee642a775220a9b313396, matching the claim. `./ci/boot-test.sh`: 5 passed, and I repeated the underlying QEMU invocation 51 times with no anomaly. `--check reach-around` PASS over three portable files, with its own honest caveat that it bounds the named route only. `--check no-kernel-deps` PASS, lock resolves 1. `--check vector-alignment` PASS, `.vectors` at 0x40080000. `--check english` PASS, advisory, 9 files flagged, none in the kernel. `--check prose-sync` PASS, 10 invariants agreeing in both forms. The `ci/` tree in this worktree is byte-identical to main's (`git diff main task/T-0005 -- ci/` is empty) and the branch contains main's last `ci/` commit, so these are the current checks and not an inherited copy. One factual correction to the framing I was given: this branch is rebased onto ae51170, not onto main's tip 7fdd0f1. It is missing exactly one commit, a single appended line in `.provenance/ledger.jsonl`, which touches nothing this review depends on.

THE REBASE. Clean. `git diff f0bdaea..HEAD -- kernel/` is empty, so the kernel tree is byte-for-byte the pre-rebase tip. The rest of the diff between those two commits is exactly the main-side content the rebase picked up — ledger lines, the `ci/` hardening, RFCs 0002/0003/0004, roadmap and task files, the web page — and nothing in `kernel/` rides along under it. Author and committer dates now agree on all twelve commits, which is what `--committer-date-is-author-date` is for. Two commits present before the rebase are absent after it; both are task-file changes that main adopted independently, and the surviving `tasks/{open => active}/T-0005.toml` is a pure rename with no content delta. Nothing was smuggled in.

THE `sp` CORRECTION, WHICH I WAS ASKED TO JUDGE. It is adequate as an admission and it understates by roughly a factor of four and one section. Detail is in the second finding. The sentence now concedes the clause it belongs to was wrong, names the instruction, and gives the address I measured — that is the right shape, and it is a real improvement over a flat "a caller chooses nothing". What it gets wrong is the size and the extent of the write: `str x30, [sp, #-16]!` stores eight bytes and moves sp by sixteen, and it is not where the exposure ends, because `fault_stop`'s prologue then subtracts 0x40 and writes six more registers. From the very `sp` the sentence cites, that puts a 72-byte pattern across the guard word and the second half of vector entry 15, with `x30` — also caller-chosen — among the values. I would take a one-clause fix. I would not hold the branch for it, because the paragraph is about what a caller of an item already declared unsound can do, no such caller exists in the tree, `--check reach-around` says so, and the real entry path is governed by the separate and correct clause 80 lines above that says `exception_entry` needs a usable sp and this path cannot give it one.

MY STANDING MAJOR: SHARPENED, NOT WITHDRAWN, AND NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN DERIVED. It survives the rebase intact because the kernel tree did not change. `.text` ends at 0x400814e0. The stack floor is 0x400814e0. They are the same address, because `.got`, `.bss` and `.stack` all begin there and `.data` produces no section at all. The last word of `.text` is `bl fault_stop` at 0x400814dc, the closing instruction of `exception_entry`. Last round I stopped at that arithmetic; this round I ran it. Four probe builds in a scratchpad copy, each verified by nm to place `exception_entry` last in `.text` with `bl fault_stop` as the final word exactly as the reviewed image does, each zeroing N bytes downward from the linker-computed stack floor before taking one synchronous fault: N=8, which reaches only that build's tail padding, gives a full SKYNET_FAULT with the correct ELR and exit 0; N=16, which reaches the `bl`, gives SKYNET_REFAULT and nothing else; N=32 and N=64 the same. The reviewed image has no padding there at all, so on it the threshold is four bytes. The stack-overflow case cannot produce a full report, and it cannot from the shallowest overrun that can occur. The task's own group-A criterion records that the same 16-byte overrun on the baseline produced a normal SKYNET_FAULT — that was true when `.bss` and `.data` stood between the stack and the code, and it is not true here.

WHETHER IT SHOULD MERGE WITH THAT OPEN. Yes, and I want to be precise about why, because the finding sounds fatal and is not. What the task set out to remove is a silent loop: three measured cases where the machine burned a million exceptions into an empty console and died to a thirty-second timeout. All three of my overrun depths ended the machine by itself, printed something a human can read, and exited 0. The bound of three is now true of the machine in the case it was false of. What was never promised, by the task's criteria or by RFC-0002, is that the overflow case yields the FULL report; the criterion asks for the depth at which the machine stops stopping, and within the range I probed there is none. So the deliverable is met and the residual is a quality-of-report loss on one fault class. Against that, the layout change made the shallow case worse than the baseline, which is a genuine cost and is the thing a decision-maker should see stated rather than derived. Both halves of that trade belong in the file. Stopping here at M1 is acceptable to me, on one condition I would state rather than impose: that `link.ld` says the first of its three distances is zero. Everything else in that header is a derivation that a reader can perform, and this one performs to nothing — leaving that unsaid is the only part of the situation I would call misleading, and it is a sentence, not a redesign. The remedy that removes the residual rather than documenting it is O-9's guard page, which cannot be built without the MMU, and building the MMU inside a task about the fault path would be the wrong shape of work.

WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR. The 72-byte write set in the second finding is derived from the disassembly of the reviewed image and from AArch64 addressing, not executed this round; the `.guard` half of it I executed in the previous round on a tree I have confirmed byte-identical. I did not re-run the `#[link_name = "$x"]` link failure or the `$d` variant; I accepted the mechanism and checked only that the section's symbol inventory is what the comment now says. My overrun probe simulates an overflow by writing downward from the floor rather than by overflowing; that reproduces what an overflow destroys and the order it destroys it in, but not the frame layout of any particular runaway function, and a real overflow could reach further per step. Everything about the second core is unmeasurable today and the file says so in both places it matters. The four remaining `Today:` clauses of the task describe main and I checked none of them against main; that is not this lens. And the ninety seconds during which this worktree was not the tree under judgement is a hole I closed by re-measuring, not by preventing — I have no way to prove nothing else was touched during it beyond a clean `git status` and a flat image whose hash matches the claim.

Nothing in the contribution attempted to direct this review. The tip commit's message is unusually plain about two of its own predecessor's false statements, and I treated all of it as data: every figure in this verdict is one I measured on the image in front of me, and the three I took on mechanism instead of on execution are named above as such.

defect: three defects in the briefs that closed T-0005, two of them running toward the contribution
explanation: T-0005 merged on these briefs. The verdicts stand -- every judge measured independently, all three declared what they had been told, and two corrected it in their own verdicts. Recorded because a merge reached on a brief that overstated in its favour is exactly the case a ledger exists for.
remedy:
Faults 2 and 3 both ran TOWARD the contribution, and 3 did so at the exact point the brief called the whole case. That direction is the finding. A brief is written by the party that wants the work to land, and this one overstated the artefact twice while presenting itself as the adversarial framing -- the residual was described in detail and the benefit was inflated in one clause nobody would think to check.
This is the fifth false premise handed to a judge and recorded here. The four before it were single errors; this is a pattern with a direction, which is worse. The mechanical part of the remedy is small: a brief may state a measurement only with the command that produced it, so a judge can re-run rather than re-derive. The unmechanical part is that nothing checks a brief, the orchestrator writes every one, and roles.toml already records that this role has the most practical power and the least mechanical constraint.

THE QUESTION I EXIST TO ANSWER: DOES A FUNCTION NOTHING CALLS SERVE OBJECTIVE 0002, OR DEFER IT?

It serves it, and I want to be precise about why, because the easy version of this answer is wrong.

Criterion 2 of the objective is "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants". This contribution does NOT meet that criterion. After it merges, the kernel still knows nothing about its memory. I want that sentence on the record because it is the honest description and no reading of the evidence changes it.

What it does is meet the load-bearing clause of that criterion — "rather than from constants" — in the only place that clause can be established. The test `cell_widths_come_from_the_root_node` and its 1/1-versus-2/2 sibling exist precisely to show that the widths come out of the blob instead of out of the author's head, and the submission records the parser recovering 0x800000, 0x4000000 and 0x8000000 from three blobs QEMU produced at -m 8M, 64M and 128M — three answers from one build, which is the one thing a hardcoded constant cannot do. That is the criterion's substance demonstrated, off-tree, before any of it can hurt a boot.

Against that: nothing here has run where it matters. The pointer-to-slice conversion, the validation of x0, the failure path, SKYNET_MEM_FAIL — every part that can actually kill a boot is T-0011's, and T-0011 is `state = "blocked"` on four ci/ changes this task is forbidden to make. So there is a real risk this lands and sits.

I weighed the two and the first wins, for reasons that are about drift rather than about engineering:

  * DRIFT IS CHOOSING THE TRACTABLE THING OVER THE IMPORTANT ONE. This is doing the tractable HALF OF THE IMPORTANT THING while the other half waits on a party this task cannot be. The objective's statement says the pieces come "in that order, because each one is unusable without the one before it", and a truthful account of physical memory is what the frame allocator in T-0007 reads. This is on the critical path, not beside it.
  * THE INCOMPLETENESS IS DECLARED, NOT SMUGGLED. The task's own title is "...with nothing on the machine calling it". Its statement says "NOTHING IN THE BOOT PATH CALLS IT" in capitals. T-0011 exists, names this as its dependency, and names what blocks it. Undeclared incompleteness is how a codebase drifts; incompleteness written into the title is a project keeping its own books.
  * THE COMMON_GOOD IS SERVED IN ITS SECOND CLAUSE TODAY. Objective 0002's common_good has a quieter half: "A kernel that reports its faults legibly is a kernel other people can contribute to. The alternative -- a silent hang and a thirty-second CI timeout -- is a project only its authors can work on." 29 named errors and 1,752 corrupted blobs that produce no panic is exactly that, and it is delivered now rather than promised.
  * AND THIS CONTRIBUTION MADE THE PROJECT TESTABLE. Before it there was nowhere in this repository to run a test; `--test` reported SKIP because a grep for `#[cfg(test)]` found nothing. That is not a claim about the parser, it is a claim about the project, and it is the sort of thing a memory objective needs before it puts an MMU in.

PROPORTIONALITY. ~2,054 added lines against a weight-100 objective, ~59% of it tests for a function with no caller. I judged that proportionate, with an argument rather than a shrug: this is the one component in the kernel that consumes fully hostile input, and it is the only component so far that can be attacked exhaustively on a host. Spending the test budget where exhaustive attack is possible, and spending it BEFORE the code has a caller that can hide a fault behind a silent hang, is the correct allocation, not an indulgence. If the ratio were inverted — 1,092 lines of parser and 370 of tests — I would be far less comfortable.

NON-GOALS. None are touched. No user space or EL0; no capabilities or IPC; no interrupts, timers or scheduling; no real hardware; no performance work. The one that needed thought is "Swapping, demand paging, or any policy about what to do when memory runs out" — TooManyRegions and TooManyReservations are typed errors on a fixed-capacity map, which is refusing to answer, not rationing. Knowing memory exists, which is what the objective says comes first. Milestone matches: the objective declares kernel = ["M1"] and this is M1 work — which is worth noting because objective 0002 exists at all because a milestone boundary was found to have quietly stopped being checked.

WOULD AN ELECTOR RECOGNISE IT? Mostly, with one honest caveat I will not soften. Someone who allocated credits to "memory, and the ground isolation stands on" would recognise "the kernel learns its memory from the machine instead of from a constant" as what they asked for. They would be surprised to learn that after this merges the kernel still learns nothing. My judgement is that the surprise is legitimate and the answer to it is adequate — the half that was deferred is written down, has a task, and is blocked on someone else — but if T-0011 is still blocked several contributions from now, the answer stops being adequate and this parser starts being an ornament. That is a condition on my approval in the only sense a Guardian can attach one: asked again about a THIRD contribution to this objective that also does not run on the machine, my answer changes.

ON THE ROUTING RULE IN CRITERION 13, WHICH I WAS ASKED TO JUDGE AS AN EXPERIMENT AND WILL JUDGE PLAINLY.

The experiment succeeded and should be kept, with one repair.

The measurement: T-0005 reached 36 acceptance criteria and 19 contribution records before it merged. T-0010 has 13 criteria and 3 contribution records and is here. A task file that says in advance where a finding goes is the difference between a task and a place findings accumulate, and 36-criteria tasks are how an objective gets buried under work nobody voted for — which is precisely the drift shape I am here for. On the evidence in front of me the rule cut the criteria set by 64% and the submission count by 84% on comparable work.

The repair, which is real and which I confirm rather than take on faith: the rule enumerates two destinations and neither can hold a finding about the patch's own documentation. Door one is "the parser's handling of some input, the crate split breaking the artefact, or a test that does not test what it claims". Door two is "x0, validating the blob's address, the failure path, SKYNET_MEM_FAIL, or the allocator" — an enumerated list, not a general escape. A finding that fdt.rs's module docstring cites the wrong specification clauses fits neither, and I verified independently that the finding is live: the docstring at kernel/src/fdt.rs:26 attributes fdt_header to 5.1, the reservation block to 5.2, the structure block to 5.3 and the strings block to 5.4, where the Devicetree Specification's chapter 5 numbers them 5.2, 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5. It is a pointer error and not a wrong constant — the constants themselves are anchored to dtc 1.7.2's actual output, which is the stronger check — but this file's declared job under constitutional invariant 3 and criterion 8 is to record WHICH CLAUSE each constant came from, and a citation list that is off by one is the one defect that specifically damages the deliverable this task claimed. It has now survived three passes because the rule gives it nowhere to go.

So: the rule needs a third door, for a finding about the submission's own claims and prose. Adding one is cheap and does not reopen the 36-criteria failure mode, because prose findings are bounded by the file rather than by the input space. I also record, because it is a defect in the same rule and was independently observed: criterion 13 is addressed to the review and not to the patch, so no submission can meet or fail it, which makes it a routing policy wearing an acceptance criterion's clothes. It belongs in the task's notes, not in its acceptance list. Neither of those is a reason to reject this contribution — both are findings about the task file, which this contribution is forbidden to edit.

VERDICT: approve, on the objective question only. I did not judge correctness; I judged whether this is what objective 0002 asked for.

--- 1. THE INSTRUMENT, BEFORE ANY NUMBER ---

I worked only in a private extraction: `git archive 632e73a | tar -x -C $(mktemp -d -p <scratchpad>)`, mode 0700, deleted after. I never entered `.worktrees/T-0010`. `sha256sum kernel/src/fdt.rs` in my tree is 7da17b7c4c0fcc999f8718c0cffefe9a2c7628880a9dbbe072f7009d6fc69ea3, taken at extraction and again at the end, unchanged. The toolchain works here, which I checked rather than assumed. `./ci/build.sh` prints `PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel`; `./ci/build.sh --test` prints `test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed` then `PASS unit tests passed`. So the bare-metal target is reachable from my seat and the gated `--test` path is real, not PENDING.

I reproduced the hollow-run hazard twice, in two different shapes, and both are worth recording because both exit successfully. (a) With `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` exported to a private path, `./ci/build.sh` reports `FAIL ... does not exist` -- `ci/lib.sh:kernel_binary()` does not honour the variable, so the standing advice to use a private target directory actively breaks this script; the correct isolation is the private extraction, which already gives a private `kernel/target`. (b) `./ci/boot-test.sh` on an unbuilt tree prints `PENDING kernel not built` and exits 0. A judge running the suite in the wrong order gets a clean exit and zero measurement. Neither is this patch's defect; both are the class of thing that has produced nineteen wrong published numbers on this project.

--- 2. THE OBJECTIVE RESOLVES, AND ITS MANDATE IS ONE PERSON'S ---

`roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml` exists, `status = "active"`, `weight = 100`, `weight_source = "bdfl-seed"`, `milestones.kernel = ["M1"]`. The contribution claims 0002 and is M1 work, so unlike C-0004 it is inside its objective's declared milestone list. Weight 100 is the highest in the roadmap and equal to 0001's -- but it is seeded, not voted, and `weight_note` says so plainly. Every proportionality sentence below therefore rests on one human's judgement until cycle 0001 runs at G3. I record that rather than treating a seed like a mandate.

--- 3. THE HARD QUESTION: DOES A FUNCTION NOTHING CALLS SERVE CRITERION 2? ---

Criterion 2 reads: "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants." I confirmed the parser reads exactly those two things and nothing else: the memory reservation block, and every node whose `device_type` is `"memory"`, with `reg` decoded using the root node's `#address-cells`/`#size-cells` read from the blob. That is the criterion's two clauses, one for each half of the sentence -- "which physical memory exists" is the memory nodes, "which of it is already spoken for" is the reservation block. This is not a parser that happens to be near the criterion; it is a parser shaped to it.

I confirmed nothing calls it: `grep -rn 'fdt::' kernel/src/` outside fdt.rs returns only `pub mod fdt;` in lib.rs and one docstring mention in main.rs. `./ci/build.sh --size` reports `PASS within budget -- 1% used` of 393,216 bytes, i.e. the image did not grow and `--gc-sections` dropped the module, which is the mechanical proof that no execution path reaches it.

So the objection is fair on its face and I tested it rather than answering it. The objection is that the tractable half was chosen over the important one. That reading fails on evidence I can check. `tasks/open/T-0011.toml` -- the half that hands this parser a real blob -- exists, has 11 criteria, and carries `state = "blocked"`; the block is on RFC-0003 section 8 step 2, four `ci/` changes filed against a seat that is not the one writing kernel code, `ci/` being denied by name to the executive seats in `governance/SEPARATION_OF_POWERS.md`. The boot half was not passed over. It was unavailable to anyone who could have written this. Choosing the reachable half of a two-part criterion, filing the other half, and saying in the task file that "Neither meets the criterion alone and both are needed for it" is sequencing, and it is sequencing that declines to overstate itself. Drift, the thing I exist to catch, looks like a contribution claiming to have met a criterion it advanced by half. This one claims the half.

The second, quieter good in the objective's own words -- "a kernel that reports its faults legibly is a kernel other people can contribute to" -- is served directly and I measured it. All 29 variants of `Error` are asserted by name in the suite: the enum declares 29 (`sed -n '/pub enum Error/,/^}/p' | grep -oP '^\s{4}\K[A-Z][A-Za-z]+' | sort -u`), the tests name 29 (`awk 'NR>757' | grep -oP 'Error::\K[A-Z][A-Za-z]+' | sort -u`), and `comm -23` between them is empty. The brief told me "25 to 29"; the true figure is 29 of 29, so on this point the brief understated in the direction against the contribution and I correct it upward. A malformed blob produces a named reason instead of a silent hang, which is the difference between a project only its authors can work on and a commons.

I verified the two sweep figures I was given. `every_truncation_of_a_good_blob_is_an_error_and_not_a_panic` loops `0..DTC_CELLS_1_1.len()` and that constant is declared `[u8; 211]` -- 211 truncations, each asserted `is_err()`, so this one asserts more than absence of panic. The bit sweeps run `HEADER_LEN`=40 bytes x 8 plus bytes 40..219 of `DTC_CELLS_2_2` (`[u8; 219]`) x 8 = 320 + 1,432 = 1,752 exactly. Those two, however, are `let _ = parse(&blob);` and assert only that no panic occurs -- the brief said "producing no panic", which is accurate, and I note it because half the name of each test is unproved by its body. That is not my lens and I see it already on file; I mention it only to say the evidence I was handed was described honestly.

The mutation evidence is the part I most expected to be inflated and it is the part most carefully hedged. The comment at fdt.rs:769 says of the hand-chosen fourteen: "the same hand that wrote the tests, which is the weakness in it", and "A reader should read that as 'these fourteen guesses are covered', not as a statement about the parser." The rule-chosen eighteen exists because a survivor "of exactly this shape was found from outside". A submission that names the weakness of its own strongest evidence, in the file, is not the shape of a submission trying to walk something past me.

--- 4. NON-GOALS AND SCOPE ---

Clean. `git diff --name-status ae51170 632e73a` gives exactly seven entries: Cargo.toml, build.rs, fdt.rs (new), hal.rs, lib.rs (new), main.rs, and the task file moving open/ -> active/. Nothing under `arch/`, nothing in `ci/`, `roadmap/`, `governance/`, `rfcs/`, `.provenance/`. Against 0002's six declared non-goals: no EL0 or syscalls, no capabilities or IPC, no interrupts or timers or scheduling, no swapping and no exhaustion policy, no real-hardware assumption, and no performance work -- `MAX_BLOB_LEN` is documented as an appetite bound rather than a board fact, which keeps it inside "Real hardware ... M9". `./ci/constitution-check.sh --check reach-around` returns `PASS no portable kernel file binds a symbol by name (5 file(s) checked)`, rc=0, with the new portable files among the five.

One scope point I want on the record because it is a drift shape rather than a style question. The task's OPEN criterion warned against `MemoryMap` growing "a read interface" that becomes a registry -- RFC-0001's `BootResources` warning. The interface delivered is two methods, `regions() -> &[Region]` and `reserved() -> &[Region]`, and nothing else: no lookup by name, no lookup by index, no method handing out a `Region` by identity. That is the smallest thing an allocator can consume and it is the correct answer to a warning that was about drift, not about code.

--- 5. PROPORTIONALITY ---

My own line counts, since the brief's figure did not reproduce. `git diff --numstat ae51170 632e73a` gives 2,054 added lines total. fdt.rs is 1,848 lines and `mod tests` opens at line 758, so 757 non-test and 1,091 test. Added non-test lines across the whole contribution: 757 + 123 (hal) + 26 (lib) + 38 (main) + 10 + 9 = 963. The brief's "1,184 lines" reproduces only as a non-blank non-comment count over the whole diff, where I measure 1,174; it is not the production-code figure and should not be read as one. The honest description is 963 lines of code and 1,091 lines of test.

Is 963 lines proportionate to half of one of six criteria on a weight-100 objective? Yes, and the reason is that the number is not chosen by whoever wrote it. `CONSTITUTION.md` invariant 7, enforced from M0: "The kernel's dependency tree is empty. No `spin`, no `bitflags`, no `log` -- we write them." `grep -c '^\[\[package\]\]' kernel/Cargo.lock` is 1. `fdt`, `device-tree`, `dtb-parser` and `vfdt` all exist and all do this job; the constitution forbids every one of them. A hand-written specification-conformant DTB reader in 757 lines is lean against that constraint, not indulgent. The 1.4:1 test-to-code ratio is likewise not disproportionate for a parser over an input that a hostile party controls entirely, in a kernel where a panic is the marker meaning the kernel has a bug.

Would a reasonable elector recognise this? Someone who voted for "give the kernel a truthful account of the memory it has" would recognise a device tree reader as the thing that produces the account. They would be entitled to ask why it is not yet connected, and the answer -- the connecting task is filed and blocked on work belonging elsewhere -- is one I could give them from files, not from assurances. I do not think they would be surprised.

--- 6. THE SECOND QUESTION: DECOMPOSITION, OR SUBJECT? ---

I was asked to test this rather than assume it, and my answer is: THE SUBJECT, PRINCIPALLY. The decomposition experiment has not yet been run against anything hard, and a claim that it works is premature. Five things, all checkable.

(a) The magnitude is wrong for the proposed cause. `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso ae51170..632e73a` gives four commits between 17:46:44 and 19:00:42 on 2026-08-07. The branch is SEVENTY-FOUR MINUTES end to end, not a day. Against four days for a 54-line change, that is a factor near eighty. Thirty-six acceptance criteria against thirteen cannot buy a factor of eighty.

(b) The observation channels are not comparable, and this is structural rather than incidental. `cargo test` builds for the host triple -- `.cargo/config.toml` sets only a linker for the bare-metal target -- so nothing under `arch/` is reachable from a host test at all; RFC-0003 O-7 records that gap and this task's notes restate it. The earlier subject therefore had NO host-test channel. Its only channel was building an image, booting QEMU and reading a serial marker, and the thing under test was the very path that prints the marker, so a defect destroys the instrument that would report it. This subject's suite finishes in 0.00s and a clean `cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml` completes in 0.46s wall, which is what makes 1,752 exhaustive single-bit corruptions affordable. Exhaustive attack is available on one subject and structurally unavailable on the other.

(c) The decomposition was possible only because the subject has a seam. T-0006 split cleanly into a parser and a boot half along a `&[u8]` boundary. A fault path that must survive its own stack being destroyed has no such boundary -- you cannot land half of it and test that half. Even here the rule bent at its one weak point, and the task file says so out loud: the crate split "cannot be its own task" because its criteria are unevaluable until a test exists, and the file admits that is "the one place this file is bigger than the rule would like".

(d) The project's own diagnosis was not a size diagnosis. `git log -1 --format=%B c36445d` says the earlier task "grew to THIRTY-SIX acceptance criteria, because each review round added criteria to the task it was reviewing, and a task whose target moves every round cannot converge". That is a RATCHET, not a volume. The corrective actually named as the fix is the finding-routing rule -- "That single sentence is what T-0005 never had, and its absence is the whole mechanism behind thirty-six" -- which is criterion 13 here. This branch converged with zero review rounds adding criteria, so the ratchet never engaged and the mechanism was never exercised. Note also that criterion 13 is addressed to the review rather than to the patch, so no submission can meet or fail it -- the one instrument the recut named as its fix is the one criterion nothing in the pipeline can decide.

(e) The decisive datum is that the discipline was not applied to the next hard subject. `tasks/open/T-0007.toml`, the frame allocator that consumes this parser's output, still stands at THIRTY acceptance criteria, and the recut commit flags it in its own message: "30 criteria across four subjects is exactly the shape being corrected here", needing "a re-cut before anyone claims it". The cut-small regime produced one success, on the one subject in this milestone that a host can attack exhaustively, and has not been applied to the subject standing immediately behind it.

What I would put to whoever cuts the next milestone. Do not read C-0036 as evidence that small tasks work. Read it as evidence that a task with a HOST-TESTABLE EXIT CONDITION converges fast, which is a claim about where the test lives and not about how many criteria there are. The controlled experiment already exists and nobody has run it: `tasks/open/T-0009.toml` is 11 criteria -- as small as this one -- and bare-metal, touching link.ld and boot.rs, judged by booting. If T-0009 converges in one or two rounds, the decomposition claim survives with the co-variate controlled. If it takes ten, the variable was always the subject. Until then the experiment has one data point taken on the easy case, and I would not cut a milestone on it.

--- 7. WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR ---

Correctness, conformance to the Devicetree Specification, and soundness are not mine and I did not audit them. I did not verify a single specification citation against v0.4; I noticed only that the module docstring's chapter-5 numbering and the numbering on the constants disagree with each other, which is a fidelity question already in another lane. I did not re-run the mutation sets or the differential argument; I checked that the evidence was described without inflation, not that it holds. I cannot vouch that this parser will accept the blob QEMU actually produces, because no blob reaches it -- that is T-0011's, and it is the reason my approval is for half a criterion and says so.

One thing about the branch that belongs to the merge path and not to me: 632e73a's merge-base with `main` is ae51170, so this branch predates the contribution that closed T-0005. `git diff main 632e73a` accordingly shows large reversions under `arch/` and the T-0005 task file moving backwards out of done/. That is a stale base, mechanical, and the gate's to see -- I raise it only because a judge measuring `git diff main` rather than `git diff <merge-base>` would attribute several hundred lines of `arch/` churn to this contribution, and it has none.

--- 8. PROCESS, AND ONE CONTAINMENT FINDING ---

No attempt was made to direct me. The comment at fdt.rs:528 invites the reader to disbelieve it, which is data about the submission and I treated it as such. Nothing in the contribution claimed prior approval or an exemption.

No verdict of any other panel member was present in `.forge/contributions/C-0036/verdicts/` when I read it; the two files there are review verdicts, which are a different seat and which I am permitted to read. I read them after forming my own view of purpose, and neither addresses purpose. I know of no other panel member's direction on this contribution and my conclusion is uncontaminated as far as I can establish.

But the room is physically shared and I must say so. My scratchpad root contains sibling extractions of this identical head that I did not create, and unlike mine (mode 0700) several of them are mode 0755 -- world-readable to anyone else working in that root, along with loose files at the root recording another party's working paths and one JSON artefact. I did not open any of them. I record it because the rule in `governance/SEPARATION_OF_POWERS.md` is that while a panel sits, no artefact a judge can read may carry another judge's reasoning, and the filesystem those judges are told to work in currently makes their working notes readable by default. The instruction to extract privately solves the tree-shifting problem and does not solve this one. `mktemp -d` already produces 0700; the extractions that are not are the ones to fix.

--- 9. CONCLUSION ---

The objective resolves and is claimed correctly. The contribution serves the second half of criterion 2's sentence and the whole of the objective's stated secondary good, legibility. It stays inside every non-goal. Its size is set by invariant 7 rather than chosen. It does not overstate itself: the task file, the module and the mutation commentary each say what the evidence does not cover. My approval means only that I see no reason to stop it, and it is contingent on T-0011 existing -- which I verified it does.

Approve.

APPROVE, HIGH CONFIDENCE. I judge purpose, not correctness, and on purpose this is close to the cleanest case objective 0002 can produce.

DOES THE OBJECTIVE RESOLVE. Yes. roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml, status = 'active', milestones kernel = ['M1'], and the task is filed at M1. Weight 100 -- but weight_source = 'bdfl-seed', not a vote. My first concern above corrects the framing I was handed on that point, because the distinction is one my role prompt names and one a brief cannot dissolve.

DOES IT SERVE THE COMMON GOOD, NOT MERELY THE STATEMENT. The objective's second success criterion is: 'The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, FROM THE DEVICE TREE rather than from constants.' The criterion does not name a proxy for the device tree; it names the device tree. This patch is the thing that reads it. There is no route from where this kernel stands to that criterion that does not pass through a flattened-device-tree reader, and constitutional invariant 7 -- no kernel dependencies, enforced from M0 -- means the reader must be written here rather than pulled in. `grep -c '^\[\[package\]\]' kernel/Cargo.lock` returns 1 after a library target was added, so that invariant held through the split. So the effort is not chosen by an agent that found a satisfying problem; it is compelled by the constitution the electorate is governed under. That is the single strongest fact on the proportionality question and it is why I do not read 370 lines of hand-written parser as indulgence.

The common_good text also carries a second, quieter claim I weighed separately: 'a kernel that reports its faults legibly is a kernel other people can contribute to. The alternative -- a silent hang and a thirty-second CI timeout -- is a project only its authors can work on, which for a commons is a slow way of not being one.' A parser that answers a hostile blob with one of twenty-nine named errors, instead of hanging or printing SKYNET_PANIC, is that sentence implemented. I checked it rather than assumed it: all 29 variants of `Error` are asserted by name somewhere in the test module -- 29 of 29, not the 'twenty-five to twenty-nine' my brief offered -- measured by iterating the variant list from the enum against `grep -c "Error::<V>"` over lines 757-1848.

THE 'FUNCTION NOTHING CALLS' OBJECTION, WHICH IS THE REAL QUESTION. I take it seriously and I resolve it against the objection, for three reasons that are matters of record rather than of taste. (1) The caller's task exists and is filed: tasks/open/T-0011.toml, 'Validate the blob the loader handed us, and learn the machine's memory from it', depends_on ['T-0009','T-0010'], with a comment naming criterion 2 as completed by it. This is not 'someone will call it later'; it is a written task with a named blocker. (2) The split was produced by a measured failure, not by a preference for tractable work.
