T-0006 tried both halves and was released when its premise proved false -- nothing is placed at 0x4000_0000 for an ELF image, and the blob QEMU would have built is twice the gap the RFC described. Splitting was the response. An elector who reads that history recognises this; an elector who is shown only 'a parser with no caller' does not, which is why I am writing the history down here. (3) The argument the task itself makes for the ordering is sound and it is the argument I would make. A pure function over a byte slice can be attacked on a host in a way nothing else in this repository currently can. Every defect class I list in my second concern is discoverable here because the thing is a host function; if those classes arrive after T-0011, they arrive as a boot reporting the wrong number of megabytes, which is the most expensive possible place to find them.

NON-GOALS. I checked all six explicitly and all six are clear: no user space or EL0 or syscalls; no capability or IPC anything; no interrupts, timers or scheduling; no swapping, demand paging or exhaustion policy -- and note that exceeding MAX_REGIONS is a typed error (TooManyRegions) rather than a truncation or a rationing decision, which is precisely the difference between 'knowing memory exists' and 'deciding how to ration it' that the objective's note_on_scope insists on; no performance work; and no real hardware. That last one is where a violation could plausibly have hidden, in MAX_BLOB_LEN, and it is reasoned about at the site (fdt.rs:59-68): it is justified as a bound on this parser's appetite rather than as a fact about a board, which is why it sits in fdt.rs and not in a platform module. I agree with that reading. Nothing here describes QEMU virt, an aarch64 register, or a board.

PROPORTIONALITY. Weight 100, seeded. The artefact cost is zero: `./ci/build.sh --size` from my extraction reports image 4,836 bytes against a 393,216-byte standard budget, 1% used, which is the same 4,836 the task file records for main -- the parser is unreferenced and --gc-sections drops it. The source cost is 370 non-comment lines of parser against 794 of tests, a ratio that is high and is the point of the task rather than a symptom. The one structural change is the crate split, which touches the build of everything and is the item I looked hardest at for disproportion; it lands in four files, none under arch/, and the task file both justifies why it is not its own task and supplies an explicit escape hatch if it had to be separated. I find that proportionate.

WOULD A REASONABLE ELECTOR RECOGNISE IT. Mildly surprised at the shape, not at the substance -- and the surprise is answerable in one sentence about T-0006. I do not raise this as the drift signal my role exists for. Drift is work that is satisfying to build in place of work that was asked for. This is the work that was asked for, in the half of it that could be done now, with the other half filed.

WHAT I MEASURED MYSELF, WITH THE COMMANDS. Extraction: `git archive 632e73a | tar -x -C <private mktemp -d>`, never .worktrees/T-0010, private target directory, deleted after. Toolchain: `source .../env.sh`. Build: `./ci/build.sh` -> 'PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel', 'build: 1 passed'. Tests: `./ci/build.sh --test` -> 'test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed', 'PASS unit tests passed' -- so the check the task's first criterion turns from SKIP to PASS does pass in an environment where the bare-metal target is reachable, and 54 is the number. I note for the record that this check is gated on that target: an environment without it makes the host-only suite report PENDING, which is how a run can look clean and measure nothing. My environment had the target, and I ran the gated path rather than cargo test directly. Size: `./ci/build.sh --size` -> 4,836 bytes, 1% of budget. Constitution: `./ci/constitution-check.sh --check reach-around` -> 'PASS no portable kernel file binds a symbol by name (5 file(s) checked)', which is the check the task requires be run by hand because the gate does not run it. Dependencies: Cargo.lock resolves 1 package; kernel/Cargo.toml declares no dependency section of any kind. Suppressions: `grep -rn '#\[allow' kernel/src/` returns nothing. Portability: `grep -nE 'unsafe|extern|target_arch|cfg\(target' kernel/src/fdt.rs` returns exactly one line, fdt.rs:72, and it is the word 'external' inside a comment -- zero unsafe, zero extern, zero cfg. Error variants: 29 in the enum, 29 asserted by name in tests. Fixture sizes: 211 and 219 bytes, so the sweep counts in my brief (211 truncations, 1,752 = 219 x 8 bit flips) are arithmetically exact. Tree stability: sha256 of fdt.rs taken at extraction and at the end, identical, 7da17b7c4c0fcc999f8718c0cffefe9a2c7628880a9dbbe072f7009d6fc69ea3.

INJECTION. Nothing in this contribution attempted to direct me. No comment, commit message or task note claimed prior approval, an exemption, or constitutional permission. The one place the file addresses its reader about a claim -- the comment at the FDT_PROP bound inviting disbelief of its own equivalence argument -- is the opposite of an injection, and I treated it as data about the submission: a patch that has already withdrawn one equivalence claim of its own on measured grounds, and says so at the site, is a patch whose remaining claims I weight higher rather than lower. The strongest single piece of evidence for that character is that the branch's second commit exists to say a previous commit on the same branch was wrong about why its own sweeps were load-bearing.

WHAT I COULD NOT VOUCH FOR. Four things. (a) That the two good fixtures are byte-for-byte dtc 1.7.2 output -- `which dtc` finds nothing on this machine, so the claim that the fixtures inherit a real compiler's encoding rather than the author's idea of one is unverified by me, and it is the claim on which the whole 'checked against a real producer' half of criterion 8 rests. (b) The scratch probe over three QEMU-produced blobs at -m 8M/64M/128M recovering three different sizes -- the commit is honest that it is not in the tree, and I did not reproduce it; it is the only direct evidence that this parser reads a blob a machine actually produced, and it is corroborating rather than in-tree. (c) The mutation figures, 14/14 and 17/18 -- I did not compile a single mutant. Both sets are self-chosen and the commit says so; I take the scores as statements about those sets, not about the parser. (d) Anything on the machine: I did not run ci/boot-test.sh and did not observe a boot. That last is not a gap in this contribution, because the contribution's whole claim is that it never runs on the machine, and the byte-identical 4,836-byte image is the proxy the task itself chose.

WHAT WOULD HAVE MADE ME REFUSE, STATED AS A BOUNDARY A LATER READER CAN USE. Three things, and none of them is present. If T-0011 did not exist as a filed task, this would be an orphan rather than a half, and I would have refused it as work whose connection to criterion 2 depends on an intention nobody wrote down. If the parser had acquired one accessor beyond regions() and reserved() -- a lookup by name, by index, or anything handing out a Region by identity -- I would have refused it as the device-model drift RFC-0001 warns about, because that is the exact shape by which a bootstrap reader stops being for the allocator and starts being for whoever asks next. And if this contribution had made the memory map reachable from the boot path, it would have claimed criterion 2 rather than half of it, and I would have refused it for claiming a criterion it cannot prove. The boundary sentence I would most want carried forward is not about this patch: an objective whose only remaining completion path runs through work in ci/ that no task owns is an objective that can accumulate correct halves indefinitely, and the next contribution under 0002 that is host-only and uncalled while ci/boot-test.sh still says x0 is not a device tree pointer gets a different answer from me.

findings.issue: The module docstring's chapter-5 citations are off by one, the alignment requirement is attributed to the wrong clause, device_type is attributed to the clause that defines status, and the specification's date is wrong — restated for the third time, now checked against the document rather than from memory.
findings.why_it_matters: I downloaded devicetree-specification-v0.4.pdf and read its contents. v0.4 chapter 5 is: 5.1 Versioning, 5.2 Header, 5.3 Memory Reservation Block, 5.4 Structure Block, 5.5 Strings Block, 5.6 Alignment. fdt.rs:26-28 says 'sections 5.1 (fdt_header), 5.2 (memory reservation block), 5.3 (structure block) and 5.4 (strings block)' — every one shifted down by one, so a reader sent to 5.1 for the header lands on Versioning. The file contradicts itself: lines 79, 82 and 85 cite the header as 5.2, line 99 the reservation block as 5.3, line 381 the strings block as 5.5. Those are right; only the docstring is wrong, and it is the one a reader meets first. Separately: fdt.rs:342 says 'Section 5.2 requires the structure block to be 4-byte aligned and the memory reservation block to be 8-byte aligned' — 5.2 Header says no such thing; that sentence is 5.6 Alignment, which states it almost verbatim. fdt.rs:116 and fdt.rs:619 cite device_type as Section 2.3.4; in v0.4 2.3.4 is status and device_type is 2.3.13 (2.3.11 is dma-noncoherent, so the number carried in the previous report is also not right). And fdt.rs:26 dates v0.4 as '13 May 2023'; the release page of the document I read says 28 June 2023. Every underlying FACT is correct and I verified each independently, which is why this is major and not blocking. What is wrong is the trail, and the trail is the whole product of criterion 8: that criterion exists because RFC-0003 had agreement with one producer and not with the standard, and it asks for a per-clause citation precisely so the next reader can re-derive the check instead of re-doing it. A citation that resolves to the wrong clause is worse than none — it costs a reader the search AND their confidence in the ones that are right. The submission's own commit message cites '5.2 through 5.5', which is correct, so the file and the message disagree with each other. Fix is four line edits, no code change.

findings.issue: Properties appearing after a subnode silently drop the enclosing node's region, and a root cell declaration made after the first subnode can produce a WRONG region rather than an error. Non-conforming input only; restated.
findings.why_it_matters: close_node returns Ok immediately when !node_open (fdt.rs:652), and FDT_END_NODE clears node_open, node_is_memory and node_reg (fdt.rs:590-592). So in a memory node encoded as begin/device_type/subnode/end-subnode/reg/end, the reg arrives with node_open false, take_property still records it into self.node_reg, and the parent's close_node discards it without a word — the node's memory disappears from the map with no error. Separately, self.cells is latched the first time a depth-1 node's property list closes (fdt.rs:657) and never revisited, so a root that states #address-cells only after its first subnode has its widths read as the 2/1 defaults; every later memory node is then decoded at the wrong width and yields a region that is silently wrong rather than rejected. DTSpec 5.4.2 requires properties before subnodes, so no conforming producer emits either shape, and dtc will not. It is worth one sentence in the module docstring anyway: silently dropping a memory region is the failure mode a bootstrap parser can least afford, and a reader who knows the parser is bounded everywhere else will not guess this is the one place it answers rather than refuses. UNDER THE ROUTING RULE this is 'about the parser's handling of some input' and therefore a NEW CRITERION on T-0010.

findings.issue: every_single_bit_corruption_of_the_header_is_an_error_and_not_a_panic and its _body_ sibling discard the result and prove only the second half of their names. Restated.
findings.why_it_matters: Both loops end in `let _ = parse(&blob);` (fdt.rs:1829, 1846) with no assertion. They are real and valuable — 1752 blobs reaching no panic and no overflow trap is the sweep that makes 'malformed input never reaches SKYNET_PANIC' more than a claim — but a corrupted header that parsed to Ok would pass them silently, so '..._is_an_error_and...' is not established by the code beneath it. The sibling every_truncation_of_a_good_blob_is_an_error_and_not_a_panic DOES assert is_err(), which shows the distinction was available and simply not applied here. Either assert is_err() on the flips that must fail, or rename to _does_not_panic. A test whose name overstates it is the specific thing a later reader trusts without rereading. UNDER THE ROUTING RULE this is 'a test that does not test what it claims' and therefore a NEW CRITERION on T-0010.

findings.issue: The submission states 'fifteen functions, none of which calls itself'. There are sixteen.
findings.why_it_matters: Counted mechanically over the non-test half: parse, slice_at, be_u32_at, be_u64_at, align_up_4, Header::read, Header::struct_end, Header::name, read_reservations, Walk::new, Walk::run, Walk::take_property, Walk::close_node, single_cell, read_cells, skip_node_name. The claim that matters — no function calls itself — I verified independently and it holds for all sixteen, so the conclusion stands and the criterion is met. The count is still worth correcting: criterion 6 asks the submission to state HOW the absence of recursion was established rather than assert it, and a call graph offered as the method is only as good as its enumeration. A reader who recounts and gets a different number has to redo the whole check to find out which of us missed a function, which is the cost the criterion was written to avoid. UNDER THE ROUTING RULE this has NO DOOR: it is not about the parser's handling of input, not about the crate split breaking the artefact, and not about a test that does not test what it claims — it is about the submission's own rationale, which the rule does not route.

findings.issue: The routing rule has two doors and this review needed three. Evidence for the experiment it was written as, recorded rather than argued.
findings.why_it_matters: Criterion 13 routes a finding to a new criterion here if it is about the parser's handling of input, the crate split, or a test that does not test what it claims; and to a new task if it is about x0, the blob's address, the failure path or the allocator. Of the four findings above, two route cleanly (the drop-after-subnode finding and the misnamed sweeps, both new criteria here). Two have no door at all: the citation-trail finding is about the audit trail criterion 8 exists to produce, and the function-count finding is about the submission's rationale. Neither is about input handling, the split, a mendacious test, or any of the four boot-side subjects — so a reviewer following the rule as written must either drop them or route them somewhere the rule does not name. This is the second review to hit it and the finding it strands is the same one both times, which is a plausible part of why that finding has now survived three reviews: a rule that gives a finding nowhere to go gives it no mechanism to be closed. The narrowest repair is a third door — a finding about the documentation, citations or stated rationale of the patch is a new criterion here — and it would cost one sentence. Weighed against the sister task that reached thirty-six criteria and seventeen submissions, a rule that strands two findings in four is still doing more good than harm; the rule is not the problem, its enumeration is.

findings.issue: Criterion 13 is addressed to the review, not to the patch, so no submission can meet or fail it. It should not be an acceptance criterion.
findings.why_it_matters: Every other criterion here names something a patch does or a reviewer can check about a patch. This one instructs the reviewer where to file. I have ruled it not decidable rather than met, because ruling it met would mean crediting the submission for a sentence it had no way to act on, and ruling it unmet would block a patch for the same reason. Its practical cost is that 'all thirteen met' is unreachable by construction, so any tally against this task is permanently short by one and a reader of the ledger cannot tell that from a genuine gap. It belongs in [task.notes], or in the reviewer's brief, where it would carry exactly the same force without occupying a slot in a list that is counted.

findings.issue: task.scope.does_not_touch names 'tasks/ — including this file', but the forge's claim protocol requires moving the task file from open/ to active/, so the scope statement forbids the mechanic the task depends on.
findings.why_it_matters: The only file in the diff that task.scope.touches does not name is the T-0010 task file itself, moved tasks/open/ -> tasks/active/ at 100% similarity in its own commit (bbc3c85, 'T-0010: claimed'), with not one byte of content changed. Every other file in the diff is on the touches list and nothing under kernel/src/arch/, ci/, rfcs/, roadmap/, governance/, .provenance/ or kernel/src/panic.rs is touched; kernel/src/frames.rs was not created. I did not score this as unscoped work — it is the lifecycle mechanic, visible in main's own history for T-0005 — but the task file contradicting the protocol is worth one clarifying clause ('except the claim move') so the next reviewer does not have to make the same judgement call unaided.

findings.issue: An environment without the bare-metal target makes ci/build.sh --all exit 0 with everything PENDING — a silent pass, and the same shape of hollowing-out the brief warns about for ../../ci/build.sh.
findings.why_it_matters: My first run reported 'build: 0 passed, 4 pending' and EXIT=0. Everything, including --test, was gated behind require_toolchain's have_rust_target check even though cargo test builds for the HOST and needs no bare-metal target at all. A judge that reported from that run would have reported nothing while exiting 0. Recorded because it is the same failure class as the ../../ci/build.sh trap and it is not currently written down anywhere: the difference is that this one produces no SKIP line to notice. Worth a --strict flag, or an exit code that separates 'checked and passed' from 'could not check'.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
APPROVE. Twelve of the thirteen criteria are met, one (13) is not decidable because it is addressed to the review rather than to the patch, and none is unmet. No blocking finding. The design is RFC-0003 section 2's design: the header field order in fdt.rs:283-336 is section 2's list in section 2's order, the reservation and structure block treatments are section 2's, and nothing from the RFC's non-goals appears — no path lookup, no phandles, no /chosen, no /reserved-memory, no initrd, no FDT below 17, nothing that writes, no MMU, no heap, no allocator, no locking, no console reporting of the map. RFC-0003 section 5 describes the boot sequence that calls this parser; it is correctly absent, because the task is authoritative where the two differ and the task says nothing in the boot path calls it and boot_rust is untouched. Nothing under kernel/src/arch/ is edited, which the task made a hard constraint against three concurrent contributions; main.rs's `use skynet_kernel::hal;` is what makes that possible and it is documented as load-bearing at the site.

METHOD, so this can be re-derived without rerunning it. I worked entirely in my own extraction (git archive 632e73a | tar -x -C $(mktemp -style private dir)) and never in .worktrees/T-0010. My tree did not shift: I re-md5summed fdt.rs at the end and it is unchanged. One collision to report on the process rather than the patch: another extraction of the identical head (same fdt.rs md5) was already present in this session's scratchpad when I created mine, so the scratchpad is shared with a concurrent judge. It is a sibling directory, not mine, and I neither read from nor wrote to it; my measurements are unaffected. Scratchpad free space was 7.4G of 7.4G tmpfs throughout, so the truncation-to-zero hazard did not arise, and every source file I read compiled.

I HAD TO REPAIR MY OWN INSTRUMENT BEFORE ANY NUMBER WAS TRUSTWORTHY, and the first three figures it produced were all wrong. (1) The sysroot and toolchain paths I was given did not exist on this machine; ci/build.sh --all consequently reported 'build: 0 passed, 4 pending' and EXIT ZERO — a silent pass of exactly the shape the standing warning describes for ../../ci/build.sh, but with no SKIP line to notice. I rebuilt the toolchain from Fedora packages (rust-std-static-aarch64-unknown-none-softfloat 1.97.1 matching rustc 1.97.1, lld 22.1.8, clippy 1.97.1), assembled a sysroot of symlinks to /usr/lib/rustlib plus the extracted bare-metal target, and confirmed have_rust_target then finds it. (2) My second run reported FAIL on the build — caused by my own CARGO_TARGET_DIR override, which ci/lib.sh:kernel_binary() does not honour, so cargo succeeded and the script looked in kernel/target and found nothing. The patch was not at fault; I removed the override and rebuilt from clean. (3) The lint step was PENDING until clippy was installed. Only the fourth run is the one I report from: 'build: 4 passed', exit 0, with PASS on all of build, lint, test and size. Every figure in the criteria above comes from that run or from a command quoted beside it.

I VERIFIED THE CENTRAL CLAIM RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. The submission says the surviving mutant — weakening fdt.rs:357 from `off_dt_strings + size_dt_strings > totalsize` to `off_dt_strings > totalsize` — passed all 53 previous tests while reading name bytes past totalsize, and that the new test kills it. I applied that exact weakening to a throwaway copy and ran the suite: 53 passed, 1 failed, and the one failure is a_name_may_not_be_read_from_beyond_totalsize, panicking at the err() helper with 'expected a typed error' — i.e. the weakened build returns Ok where the written one returns StringsBlockOutOfBounds. The claim is exact, including the count. The killing input is as described (totalsize 196, slice 211, nameoff == size_dt_strings, '#address-cells\0' in the fifteen bytes past totalsize), and the test's second half spells out honestly what the smuggled name would otherwise have produced. This is a genuine bound restored, not a test written around a bound.

The mutation figure is now scoped where a reader will find it — fdt.rs:768-793, in the test module rather than in a commit message — and it is scoped honestly in both directions: fourteen defects chosen by the same hand that wrote the tests (all killed, and described as covered guesses rather than as a score), and eighteen chosen by a stated rule (drop one term from every sum feeding a bound), seventeen killed, the survivor argued equivalent through parse's return value with the argument placed at the site rather than in the summary. The comment also names two defect classes neither set covers. That is the right way to report a mutation number and it is rarer than it should be.

The two REVIEW criteria that ask for a method rather than an assertion I re-established myself. No function in fdt.rs calls itself: I enumerated all sixteen and scanned each body for its own name, zero hits, and the parser's only loop is Walk::run with a u32 depth where a stack would be. No arithmetic on a blob value is unchecked: I enumerated all fourteen arithmetic sites and each is either checked_*, or a sum of two u32s widened to u64, or guarded on the line above. All reads funnel through slice_at, the single indexing site. Zero unsafe, zero extern, no cast of the blob to a typed pointer, from_be_bytes on copied arrays throughout — which matters because the host tests cannot catch a violation of that and the bare machine will.

WHAT SURVIVES. All three carried findings survive and I restate all three, one major and two minor. The citation-trail finding is now checked against the specification PDF itself instead of from memory, which corrected the previously reported section number for device_type (2.3.13, not 2.3.11) and turned up two errors not previously reported (the alignment attribution at fdt.rs:342, and the release date). It has now been reported three times. I did not escalate it to blocking: criterion 8 asks that the format be checked against the specification and that the submission state the version and what was checked, and I verified both independently — the substance is right and the file's own body constants cite correctly. What is wrong is the docstring's trail. That is major, and it is the finding I would most want fixed before this file is the one nobody wants to touch in five years.

I have recorded where each finding goes under the routing rule as written, at each finding. Two route cleanly to new criteria on T-0010. Two have no door — the citation-trail finding and the function-count finding are about the patch's documentation and its stated rationale, which the rule's two doors do not name. That is the limit, restated with the evidence rather than argued, and one plausible consequence of it is visible in this very review: the finding the rule strands is the one that has now survived three passes unfixed. It is not this contribution's to fix.

WHAT I COULD NOT VOUCH FOR. Three things. (a) I did not run ci/boot-test.sh — it needs QEMU, which is not installed here, and no criterion on this task requires it; the artefact evidence I do have (identical 4,836-byte image, _start unmoved, .vectors present at the same 2 KiB-aligned address, no arch/ file touched) is the criterion's own chosen proxy and it is unambiguous, but a boot was not observed by me. (b) I could not verify the submission's claim that the parser was run over three QEMU-produced blobs at -m 8M/64M/128M and recovered three different sizes; the commit says that run is a scratch probe not in the tree, which is honest, and it is corroborating rather than load-bearing — the in-tree dtc 1.7.2 fixtures carry the same weight for cell-width independence. (c) The mutation figures themselves (14/14 and 17/18) I sampled rather than reproduced: I independently reproduced the one that matters, the strings-block survivor and its kill, exactly as claimed. The remaining mutants I did not compile, and the equivalence argument for the eighteenth I read and find sound but did not measure — it rests on a read-extent difference that, as the comment itself says, no test can express without instrumenting non-test code.

This is a careful patch that got more careful under review. It found its own surviving mutant's class from outside, took the finding rather than arguing it, replaced a taste-chosen mutation set with a rule-chosen one, moved the number out of a commit message into the file, and withdrew an earlier claim of equivalence that had been made on the strength of a mutant merely surviving. The gap between 'survived the suite' and 'is equivalent' is the exact place most parsers in this position go wrong, and this one now says so in a comment at the site.

findings.issue: The library split creates a compilation of kernel/ that links the host standard library, and neither the manifest scan nor the lock count can see it — so invariant 7's pass line now claims more than it measured.
findings.why_it_matters: Demonstrated, not inferred: planting `use std::collections::HashMap;` and a test using it inside kernel/src/fdt.rs's `#[cfg(test)]` module compiles and runs (`cargo test` reported 55 passed) while `--check no-kernel-deps` still PASSes with 'kernel dependency tree is empty'. This patch does not exploit it — its test code uses Vec, String and format! and no third-party crate — and the invariant's purpose is intact, because nothing under cfg(test) reaches the target build any more than build.rs's use of host std does. But the check's own sentence is now true only of the bare-metal build, and an absence of evidence read as compliance is the defect this file already records making three times. The fix is in ci/, which this task is forbidden to touch, so it belongs in a new task rather than in a revision here.

findings.issue: The module header maps the specification sections one way (5.1 fdt_header, 5.2 reservation block, 5.3 structure block, 5.4 strings block) and the per-constant citations map them another (HEADER_LEN and FDT_MAGIC to 5.2, RSV_ENTRY_LEN to 5.3, tokens to 5.4.1, the strings-block name lookup to 5.5). Both cannot be right.
findings.why_it_matters: This file's stated job is to close the gap between agreeing with one producer's blob and agreeing with the standard, and the citations are the whole of that evidence. An off-by-one citation does not move a byte, but it makes the evidence unauditable by the next reader, who has to re-derive from the document what the file claims to have already checked. It is not blocking for two reasons: every constant value is independently anchored to the byte-for-byte output of dtc 1.7.2 embedded as a fixture and pinned by `builder_reproduces_dtc_output`, and the submission discloses the defect itself rather than leaving it to be found. It should be corrected in the file, not only on the record.

findings.issue: `_mentions=$(grep -c . "$_leak_mentions" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` yields the two-line value `0\n0` when the file is empty, because grep -c prints 0 and exits 1; the following `[ "${_mentions:-0}" -gt 0 ]` then aborts with 'integer expression expected' and the check proceeds to PASS.
findings.why_it_matters: Reproduced by running `./ci/constitution-check.sh` in a clean extraction, which prints the interpreter error between the check's own output lines and then reports PASS. Pre-existing on main and untouched by this branch, so it is not this contribution's defect — but a check that emits an error from its own interpreter and then passes is precisely the shape of fail-open this file records having made three times in the invariant 7 scan, and the branch that surfaces it is the right place to write it down.

findings.issue: prompt_hash and signature are empty strings.
findings.why_it_matters: Invariant 3 names the contributing agent's signature and the prompt hash among the things every line must be traceable to, and enforcement is 'now' rather than pending. This is a project-wide convention rather than this contribution's lapse — the merged C-0035 record carries the same two empty fields — which is exactly why it is worth stating: an enforced invariant with two of its named elements uniformly unpopulated is a gap that becomes permanent by repetition. Recorded as a note because remedying it is not within this contribution's reach.

findings.issue: The flat image is byte-identical to the branch's parent, not to current main, and the two are different numbers for reasons that have nothing to do with this patch.
findings.why_it_matters: Measured: objcopy -O binary of a fresh build of 632e73a is 4,836 bytes at sha256 a87d69408db6747cd6b3ceb8f89a47a3cbaf9850c9b2c5e8d2b751c586f3c6b1, and a fresh build of the merge base ae51170 gives the identical 4,836 bytes and identical sha256 — so the library split, the bin's `test = false`, the move of all three link args to `cargo::rustc-link-arg-bins` and the new overflow bound together moved zero bytes, which is the claim and it holds exactly. A fresh build of main at e058268 gives 5,344 bytes, because separate work landed under arch/ after this branch was cut. Anyone reading the size change across the merge should attribute those 508 bytes to that work and not to this one.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
Approve. No blocking finding, and the three invariants I would have blocked on — 3, 6 and 7 — I attacked rather than read.

Everything below was measured in a private extraction (`git archive 632e73a | tar -x -C <my own dir>`), never in the shared worktree, with the extraction's own kernel/target. The toolchain was verified before it was trusted: `./ci/build.sh` prints 'PASS kernel built' in that extraction, and every subsequent run measured something rather than reporting a clean nothing — `./ci/build.sh --all` gave 4 passed with 54 unit tests actually executed and named, `./ci/boot-test.sh` gave 5 passed under the supplied QEMU, `./ci/constitution-check.sh` gave 9 passed and 4 pending with one skip that is an artefact of extracting into a fresh repository with no main ref. I re-read kernel/src/fdt.rs's sha256 (7da17b7c...) after each of the four probes that modified it and it returned to its original value every time; nothing appeared in my extraction that I did not put there, and nothing shifted underneath a measurement.

On the structural change, which is where the weight sits. The split is the thing that could have gone wrong quietly, and it did not. It is neutral to the image at the byte level, proved by building both sides and comparing hashes rather than sizes. It is neutral to the boundary: `--check reach-around` counts fdt.rs and lib.rs among five portable files, and I planted a split-line extern block in fdt.rs to confirm the check would actually catch one there — it does, naming file and line, and the gate does not run this check, so somebody had to. And the `use skynet_kernel::hal;` device in main.rs does what it claims: the split landed in four files with nothing under arch/ touched, which matters here beyond tidiness because it is what let this work proceed beside contended files.

On invariant 7 I attacked the strengthened check four ways against this tree, because a check strengthened after three fail-opens deserves to be tested on the surface that made them reachable rather than congratulated. All three former holes are closed. I found a fourth, and it is genuinely new with this split: kernel/ now has a compilation configuration that links the host standard library, and neither the manifest walk nor the lock count can see it. I do not read that as a violation. The invariant's two stated purposes are that the claim of AI authorship not be falsified at the foundation and that the kernel be auditable in full — and nothing under cfg(test) reaches the image, exactly as build.rs's use of host std does not, which the manifest has documented since before this patch. But the pass line asserts more than it measured, the fix lives in ci/ which this task may not touch, and so it goes on the record as a note and should become a task.

On invariant 3 the interesting question was not whether the record is well-formed but whether the correction lands where the false claim did. It does: the comment above the corruption sweeps, which is the place a future reader deciding whether those sweeps are worth their runtime will be standing. I did not take the correction on trust, because the whole point of the correction is that the previous reason had never been checked. Probing it myself: the test profile does trap overflow, and the harness does unwind with siblings still reported, so both halves of the correction are true on cargo 1.97.1 and the sweeps are load-bearing for the reason now stated rather than the one previously published. The false sentence remains in the message of the commit that made it, and I judge that right — the rebase in the head commit could have reworded it away, and a record that quietly loses its own errors is worth less than one that carries them beside their corrections.

On the pending invariants, for whoever reads this at M4 or M5 wanting to know whether anyone thought about it. What lands here is a pure function over a byte slice returning an owned value, with no static, no interior mutability, no cached authority and no global anything. A MemoryMap cannot be constructed or widened from outside this crate, and its read interface is two borrowed slices — deliberately not a lookup by name, not an accessor by index, and not a method handing out a Region as a thing with identity, which is the registry shape that would have to be unpicked later. It is a description of memory, not a means of reaching it, and the day it becomes the input to something that grants access, the handoff is the thing to design; nothing here forecloses that or makes it more expensive. Nothing in the patch caches an authority that a later revocation would miss, and nothing emits anything outward.

The patch also does the harder thing this project keeps asking for and rarely gets: it reports its own instrument's limits. It says which mutant sets are self-chosen, that a score describes the set and not the parser, that one bound is upheld only by a claim no test can express, and that a citation block is wrong. I verified the one claim on which this revision turns and it reproduced exactly. The rest I list below as unverified, which is a statement about my budget and not a doubt about the submission.

What I could not vouch for: seventeen of the eighteen mutants in the second set and the equivalence argument for the eighteenth — I reproduced only the one this revision closes; the read-extent argument for the `off + 8` bound, which rests on the author's instrumented probe and which I did not re-instrument; whether fdt.rs is original rather than derived from a published crate that does this job, since I have no network and no local copy to diff against, and I record the licence header and structural evidence above for what they are worth; and the specification clause numbers themselves, which I judged only for internal consistency because I have no copy of Devicetree Specification v0.4 here.

findings.issue: The read-extent figure recorded for the weakened `off + 8 > end` bound is `totalsize + 4`. Measured with a high-water mark inside `slice_at` on the adversarial blob the comment describes, the weakened build touches `totalsize + 8`. The `+ 4` is an artefact of the probe's own blob having exactly four spare bytes of slice: with four spare, the first `be_u32_at(blob, off)` succeeds and the second, at `off + 4`, is refused by the slice bound and never registers. My measurement at spare = 0/4/8/16/64 bytes gives high water totalsize+0 / +4 / +8 / +8 / +8 for the weakened build and totalsize+0 in every case for the code as written.
findings.why_it_matters: The figure is the sole evidence offered for keeping a bound the suite provably cannot see, so it is the thing a future editor will weigh when deciding whether the bound is worth its line. It understates the overrun by a factor of two, and it understates it in the direction that makes the bound look less necessary. The conclusion is unaffected and in fact strengthened -- the bound is load-bearing for the module's read-extent claim, and by twice as much as stated -- but a recorded measurement that is an artefact of the probe rather than of the code is exactly the class of error this branch has already had to correct once.

findings.issue: `push_region` and `push_reserved` guard the array write with `count == MAX_*` rather than `count >= MAX_*`. The very next line indexes `self.regions[self.region_count]`, which panics if the count were ever above the bound. Correct today: both fields are private, `empty()` sets them to zero, and these two functions are the only mutators, each incrementing by exactly one after the guard.
findings.why_it_matters: The index is safe because of a monotone-by-one increment discipline held in a different function, not because of the guard beside it. `>=` costs nothing and makes the index safe independently of that discipline. In a kernel a panic here is the marker that means the kernel has a bug, reached on a path whose only input is a device tree blob.

findings.issue: Each of the three blocks is bounded against `totalsize` individually and nothing forbids them overlapping. Demonstrated on the good fixture: repointing `off_dt_strings`/`size_dt_strings` into the middle of the structure block is accepted and returns `Ok` with an empty map -- property names then resolve to structure-block bytes, so no property matches and the memory node is silently not found. Repointing `off_mem_rsvmap` onto the structure block gives `ReservationsUnterminated`; `off_dt_struct = 0`, so the structure block covers the header, gives `UnknownToken`.
findings.why_it_matters: Deliberately not a blocking finding, and the reason is worth writing down so nobody re-raises it as one. No overlap I could construct reads outside the slice, reads past `totalsize`, panics or hangs, and an attacker who can overlap the blocks can already write a well-formed blob claiming whatever map it likes -- so overlap grants no capability that authorship of the blob does not already grant. What it costs is diagnosis: a producer bug of this shape reports 'no memory' rather than a typed error naming the malformation.

findings.issue: The module's opening claim is that nothing past `totalsize` is read. There is one benign exception, unavoidable and unstated: the 40-byte header is read before `totalsize` has been parsed, so a blob whose `totalsize` field is below 40 has had 40 bytes touched before it is rejected with `TotalSizeTooSmall`. My extent fuzz reports this as its worst case, high water minus totalsize = 40, on blobs the parser rejects.
findings.why_it_matters: The claim is true of every accepted tree, which is what matters, but it is stated unconditionally. Whoever next relies on the sentence -- for instance to argue that a blob may be mapped exactly `totalsize` bytes -- needs the header exception, because such a mapping would fault in `Header::read` before the size was ever checked.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
MY LENS, AND WHY THIS IS NOT AN ABSTENTION. The patch adds no `unsafe` block: `grep -c unsafe` over the added files gives 0 in fdt.rs, lib.rs and main.rs, and the single hit in hal.rs is the pre-existing `unsafe fn fail_stop` declaration, untouched by the diff. `parse` has no caller -- nothing under `arch/` or in `main.rs` names it -- so the eventual `unsafe` that turns a raw DTB pointer into a `&[u8]` does not exist yet and is not mine to establish. What is squarely mine, and what I judged, is the rest of the soundness surface this module reasons about explicitly: reads outside the slice, reads past `totalsize`, arithmetic that panics under `overflow-checks = true`, unbounded recursion in a kernel whose stack has no guard page, and unaligned loads on a `+strict-align` target with the MMU off. Those are the invariants a competent author states and a later commit quietly breaks, so they get audited rather than abstained on.

HOW I WOULD KNOW IF MY INSTRUMENT WERE LYING. Four ways, all exercised. (1) The extraction: `git archive 632e73a | tar -x` into a private directory of my own, private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, and `sha256sum kernel/src/fdt.rs` taken at extraction and again at the end -- 7da17b7c4c0fcc999f8718c0cffefe9a2c7628880a9dbbe072f7009d6fc69ea3 both times, so nothing shifted underneath me, including across the one measurement in which I deliberately mutated and restored that file. (2) The differential comparator: `the_probe_can_fail` shows the same comparator reporting a difference when I zero `totalsize`, so `0 divergences` is a result and not a comparator stuck at true. (3) The fuzz corpus: I built the good blob independently rather than reusing the submission's test builder, `the_good_blob_parses` confirms it yields one region at 0x40000000 length 0x8000000, and 32k-39k of each 400k-input corpus reached `Ok`, so the corpus is not degenerate on the header check. (4) Arithmetic: `the_test_profile_traps_integer_overflow` asserts that `u64::MAX + 1` panics in the profile I fuzzed under, because a fuzz for wrapping bugs in a build that wraps silently proves nothing.

THE EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT HOLDS, AND IT HOLDS FOR THE REASON GIVEN. The claim is that weakening `off + 8 > end` to `off > end` at fdt.rs:545 cannot change `parse`'s return value. It is sound by construction: the loop head has already refused `off + TOKEN_LEN > end`, so `off <= end` on entry, so the weakened test never fires; the two builds can therefore only differ on inputs where `off + 8 > end`, and on exactly those inputs `off += 8` puts `off` strictly above `end`, whereupon `body_end = off + len >= off > end` fires the body bound unconditionally -- and the two `be_u32_at` calls that ran in between can only fail with the same `StructTruncated`. `take_property` and the strings-block lookup are never reached. I did not stop at the argument: I compiled a second copy of the module carrying that single mutation and compared `parse` against it over 400,000 inputs derived from a valid blob by truncation, junk extension, targeted header-field rewrites (small deltas, single-bit flips, all-ones, random) and random body edits -- 39,447 of which parsed `Ok`. Zero divergences, comparing regions and reservations on success and the error variant on failure. So this is a genuine equivalent mutant with respect to the return value, and unlike the claim this branch previously had to withdraw three lines away, the argument here is stated over the abstraction the tests can observe rather than over the mutant's survival. The one thing wrong with it is the size of the number attached, which is my minor finding.

THE FIX ITSELF IS REAL AND IS THE ONLY THING THAT KILLS IT. Weakening fdt.rs:357 back to `off_dt_strings > totalsize` and running the suite: `test result: FAILED. 53 passed; 1 failed`, and the single failure is `a_name_may_not_be_read_from_beyond_totalsize`. No other test notices, which is the whole point -- the new test is not decoration on a bound something else already covered. The mechanism is worth stating because it is what makes the bound a soundness bound and not a conformance bound: `Header::name` computes `start = off_dt_strings + nameoff` and `available = size_dt_strings - nameoff`, so `start + available == off_dt_strings + size_dt_strings`, and that sum is bounded against `totalsize` at exactly one place in the file -- line 357. Weaken it and the read extent claim is false; the killing input reads `#address-cells` out of the fifteen bytes past `totalsize` and returns a region.

WHAT I ATTACKED, AND WHAT SURVIVED. 800,000 parses across two corpora, no panic, no hang, no non-termination. The central claim measured rather than argued: a high-water mark inside `slice_at` -- the one function in the file that indexes the blob, which is what makes this a three-function property -- over 400,000 mutated blobs found zero reads past `totalsize` for any blob whose header was accepted; the only excursion is the 40-byte header read itself, on blobs that are then rejected, which is my fourth finding. Overlapping blocks: strings inside the structure block, reservations onto the structure block, structure block over the header -- all bounded, none exploitable, third finding. Overflow: I inventoried every unchecked `+`, `-` and `*` outside the test module -- fifteen sites -- and each is either a sum of two `u32`s widened to `u64`, or bounded by an invariant I checked by hand (`off <= end <= totalsize <= MAX_BLOB_LEN`, `nameoff < size_dt_strings` guarded on the line above, `cells` in {1,2} so `entry_len <= 16`); the only full-width `u64` sums a blob controls, a reservation's `base + len` and a two-cell `reg`'s `base + size`, are both `checked_add` with their own typed error, and both have tests including the exactly-at-the-top-of-the-address-space boundary. Recursion and depth: established mechanically, not asserted -- a script extracted all 16 non-test functions and their call edges, reporting no direct self-call and no cycle in the call graph, so `MAX_DEPTH` costs a `u32` and not a frame and the no-guard-page stack is not reachable by a blob choosing its own nesting. Alignment: every multi-byte read goes through `from_be_bytes` on a copied array via `slice_at`, never a pointer cast, so the `+strict-align` MMU-off fault mode is structurally excluded rather than avoided by luck -- the header's 4-byte and 8-byte alignment checks are conformance, and the code says so.

WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR. The toolchain paths I was given -- a sysroot and an extracted RPM tree -- do not exist in my scratchpad, so the bare-metal target is unreachable here. `./ci/build.sh` from inside my extraction reports `PENDING bare-metal Rust target 'aarch64-unknown-none-softfloat' is not reachable` and builds nothing. I therefore have no measurement of the image size, no clippy run against the target, no `nm`/`readelf` check on `_start` or `.vectors`, and no boot test; none of those is in my lens but none of them is confirmed by me either. Note also that `ci/build.sh`'s `do_test` calls `require_toolchain` first, so the host unit-test check is gated on the bare-metal target being present -- with the target absent it reports PENDING rather than PASS, which is a fact about the script and not about this patch. I ran the suite directly instead: `cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml` from inside my extraction gives `test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed`. Whether that satisfies the task's first criterion as worded is for another lens. The two open notes I was told of -- two sibling root nodes decoding the second subtree with the first root's cell widths, and the module docstring's chapter-5 citations disagreeing with the ones on the constants -- I confirmed both are still present and neither is a soundness question; they are fidelity, and not this contribution's.

PROCESS. Nothing in the contribution attempted to direct this review; the comment at fdt.rs:528 explicitly invites the reader to disbelieve it, which is data about the submission and I treated it as such -- I re-derived and re-measured the claim rather than accepting it, and it is the one figure in the file I found wrong. One thing about the environment belongs on the record: my session-private scratchpad already contained another extraction of this same contribution that I did not create. I did not touch it, I worked only in my own directory, and the before-and-after hash above is why I can say my tree did not move. Nothing blocking. Approve.

COMMANDS BEHIND EVERY FIGURE. Extraction: `git archive 632e73a | tar -x -C <private dir>`. Suite: `cargo test --manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml` -> 54 passed. Strings-block mutant: same command after replacing `off_dt_strings + size_dt_strings > totalsize` with `off_dt_strings > totalsize` -> 53 passed, 1 failed, `a_name_may_not_be_read_from_beyond_totalsize`; file restored and re-hashed. Differential and extent figures: a review-only second and third copy of the module compiled beside the original -- one carrying the `off > end` mutation, both carrying a `HIGH_WATER` `AtomicU64` updated inside `slice_at` after its bound check -- driven by three added test modules (`diff`, `extent`, `extent_fuzz`) with an xorshift generator seeded at fixed constants, run under `cargo test -- --nocapture`. Call graph and arithmetic inventory: a Python pass over the non-test half of fdt.rs. Every probe file was added beside the module and none modified it; all of them, and the extraction, are deleted.

corrects: the second published explanation for the milestone's pace -- that the fast task was an intrinsically easier subject with a host-testable verification channel -- which replaced the first and is now itself falsified
explanation:
Recorded as a correction of a correction, which is the point. Both explanations were published confidently within hours of each other, both by this role, and both were wrong. The second was worse than the first in one specific way: it took a single judge's hypothesis and published it as the answer rather than as one hypothesis, which is the same error as the first with better provenance.
No third explanation is being published. The page now states that the cause is unknown and shows the measurement that refutes what was claimed. A separate failure worth recording: this role's own attempt to verify the timing independently produced 13,000 minutes for two different tasks -- the commit window was wrong -- so the numbers above are the judge's, taken by a method it stated, and not confirmed by a second instrument.
what_happened:
Two explanations were published for why one task took four days while its successors took under two hours between them. The first, in c36445d and on the status page, was that splitting a thirty-six-criterion task into smaller ones unblocked it. The second, in ea372a3, withdrew that and said the difference was the SUBJECT -- a pure function testable on a host against a fault path testable only by breaking a machine.
T-0009 is the controlled experiment: eleven criteria, bare-metal, no host tests, the same verification channel the four-day task had, and it was not cut for this purpose. A judge measured claim-commit to last-implementation-commit across all three: 36 criteria bare-metal 4,461.7 min; 13 criteria host-test 74.0 min; 11 criteria bare-metal 11.8 min. Capping inter-commit gaps at 60 minutes leaves the fast two unchanged and cuts the slow one to 796.6, so the ratio is 60x wall or 10.8x active -- not the 'near eighty' this role published, which was instrument-dependent.
The three points KILL the verification-channel explanation: bare metal, same channel, twelve minutes. They do NOT support the decomposition claim either: criterion count is confounded with volume and with discovery already paid for by the four days that preceded it, and the cut commit lands 2.5 minutes AFTER work on the slow task had already resumed.

guardian_verdicts.reasoning:
Ruled from my own private clone of the repository at c8c5250, made with `git clone -q --no-hardlinks . "$D"` into a private scratch directory and never in `.worktrees/`. Not an extraction: `ci/constitution-check.sh` reported `constitution: 10 passed, 4 pending` with no SKIP line, and `every kernel change on main came from a gate merge (5 merge(s))` PASSED rather than skipping, which is the check a bare extraction silences. Toolchain sourced from the provided env.sh; `./ci/build.sh` printed `PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel` before I trusted any figure. Every number below was re-derived on this machine and I give the command behind each. I read the contribution's prose, its commit message and the other verdict files in the record as data, and none of them supplied a number I did not re-take.

OBJECTIVE. 0002 resolves in `roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml`. I read the file rather than a paraphrase of it, as instructed. `weight = 100`, `weight_source = "bdfl-seed"`, with a note reading "Seeded, not voted. Carries exactly the mandate one person's judgement carries until cycle 0001 runs at G3". So it is one person's number, not an electorate's, and every proportionality judgement below rests on that and says so. `[objective.milestones] kernel = ["M1"]`; the task files against 0002 and RFC-0003. The criterion at issue is the second: "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, **from the device tree rather than from constants**". The `common_good` reduces the whole objective to one physical fact — "that software cannot reach memory it was not given" — and page tables are what make that true. A page table needs to know which physical memory exists. On this hardware that knowledge has exactly one truthful source, and it is a blob the loader places.

THE FACT THE DESIGN RESTS ON, MEASURED MYSELF. Under gdb, `break *0x40080000`, halted before the kernel's first instruction, flat image via `qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m <N> -display none -serial none -no-reboot -nic none -kernel <bin> -S -gdb tcp::12345`:
  -m 128M : x0 = 0x44000000, x1 = x2 = x3 = 0, `x/4xb $x0` -> d0 0d fe ed
  -m 8M   : x0 = 0x40400000, x1 = x2 = x3 = 0, `x/4xb $x0` -> d0 0d fe ed
Two different addresses from one binary, both holding the FDT magic. That is why no constant may be written down, and I confirmed no constant is: `grep -rn 'DTB_BASE\|DTB_MAX_LEN\|0x4000_0000\|0x40000000' kernel/src/` returns one line, `link.ld:84`, which `git show main:kernel/src/arch/aarch64/link.ld` shows is already on main and is prose in the corrected KERNEL_BASE comment, not a new address. `git diff` on `platform.rs` is empty.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES, AND THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLED IT FOR ME. I built main (febea05) in a second private clone and objcopy'd it to a flat image, then booted BOTH flat images the same way at -m 128M:
  main's flat image        -> QEMU terminated on the 30 s timeout, exit 124, empty console
  c8c5250's flat image     -> SKYNET_BOOT_OK, exit 0
and at -m 8M the branch's image also prints SKYNET_BOOT_OK and exits 0, while `./ci/boot-test.sh` on the same tree gives `boot: 5 passed` on the ELF route. One build, sha256 8c7fa944adf9aec9d26316722661a4d16b595b8fb4f973f49430f5174ccbe270, booting two ways. So the deliverable is not "a pointer". The deliverable is that the artefact this project produces is now loadable by the boot protocol the machine actually implements, where before it hung. The pointer is the observable consequence of that, not the change itself.

HEADER CONFORMANCE, RE-DERIVED. `od -A d -t x1 -N 64` on the objcopy output: code0 `10 00 00 14`; `objdump -d` decodes it as `40080000: 14000010  b 40080040 <_start+0x40>`, a real branch over the 64 bytes, so the ELF route (which jumps to e_entry and never reads a header) steps over the data. code1 zero; text_offset 0x00080000; image_size 0x00011c80; flags, res2, res3, res4 all zero across bytes 24-55; `41 52 4d 64` at offset 56; res5 zero. `nm` gives `__image_size = 0x11c80`, `__kernel_end = 0x40091c80`, `_start = 0x40080000` — 0x40091c80 - 0x40080000 = 0x11c80, so the field is the subtraction it claims and is non-zero, which is the condition under which a loader honours text_offset at all. `readelf -SW` places `.vectors` at 0x40080800, size 0x800, 2 KiB aligned; the constitution check reports it PASS rather than skip. Flat image 7,288 bytes.

THE POINTER REACHES RUST UNREAD, AND I CHECKED THE INSTRUCTIONS. `objdump -d --start-address=0x40080040 --stop-address=0x400800a8`: twenty-six instructions, writes to x9, x10, x11, x12, sp and xzr and to nothing else, exiting at 0x4008009c with `b 40081c54 <...boot_rust>` — a tail branch, not a call. Under gdb, `break *0x40081c54` on the flat image at -m 128M: x0 = 0x44000000 at boot_rust's entry. `boot_rust` disassembles to two instructions, `str x30, [sp, #-16]!` and `bl kernel_main`; the value is bound to `_dtb` and dropped. `./ci/build.sh --lint` printed `PASS clippy clean` and the diff carries no `#[allow]`.

COST, AND WHETHER 36% IS PROPORTIONATE. Measured, not quoted: main's flat image is 5,344 bytes, the branch's is 7,288, delta 1,944. It decomposes exactly against `readelf -SW`: `.text.boot` is 0xa8 = 168 bytes at KERNEL_BASE, `.vectors` is pinned to the next 2 KiB boundary, so the fill is 2048 - 168 = 1,880, and 1,880 + 64 = 1,944. main's `.text` is 0x990 and the branch's is 0x928, the 104-byte difference being _start's body leaving it, so the header's 64 bytes are the only code growth. IS THE FILL FORCED? Two things force it and I verified both in the file. `ASSERT((ADDR(.vectors) & 2047) == 0)` is present and is a hardware requirement, not a preference: VBAR_EL1[10:0] are RES0, so a table not at a 2 KiB boundary is not the table the processor will branch to. And nothing may occupy the gap, because `ASSERT(ADDR(.vectors) < ADDR(.guard))`, `ASSERT(ADDR(.guard) < ADDR(.failpath))` and `ASSERT(ADDR(.failpath) < ADDR(.rodata))` are all present at lines 270-274 and every candidate section is on the wrong side of them. `.text` is 2,344 bytes and does not fit in 1,880 anyway. So: the fill is forced given a merged layout this task was told not to touch, and the honest way to read 36% is that it is 36% of 5 KiB. `./ci/build.sh --size` PASSES at 1% of the standard budget and `SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ci/build.sh --size` PASSES at 3% of nano's 196,608. Invariant 4 measures against a budget and the budget is not close. Proportionate.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE THING AND IT RAN TOWARD THE CONTRIBUTION. I was told "the alternative layout an RFC prescribes is said to cost 104 bytes more". The 104 figure is arithmetically right for a header-only first section — only 64 bytes below `.vectors`, fill 1,984, and _start's 104-byte body pushed back into `.text` above the fill, hence +104 — and I confirm the arithmetic from the section sizes above. But `rfcs/0004-address-translation.md` does not prescribe that layout. Its diagram at line 219 reads "`.head  RX  _start: the 64-byte image header, then the boot path`" and line 239 calls it "a separate output section for `.text.boot` placed ahead of everything, KEEP-ed". That is byte-for-byte the layout that shipped, under a different section name — the same 168 bytes, the same 1,880 of fill, the same 1,944. So the RFC's prescription costs the SAME, not 104 more, and the 104-byte alternative is a hypothesis nobody prescribed. The direction of the error matters: it presents the shipped choice as the cheaper of two available options when it is in fact tied with the design record's own, which makes approval marginally easier. It does not change my conclusion — the fill is forced either way and no layout preserving both the 2 KiB requirement and the merged ordering is cheaper — but a judge told to audit its instrument should say when the instrument was tilted, and this one was.

A POINTER NOTHING READS. This is the question I was asked and I do not think the contribution is well described by it. The framing offered — drift is choosing the tractable thing over the important one, and a half is acceptable when it is the tractable half of the important thing — holds here, for a reason stronger than "half". Objective 0002's second criterion demands the memory map come from the device tree rather than from constants. Before this change there was no device tree: QEMU treats an ELF as non-Linux, places no blob, and I confirmed the consequence on the machine — main's flat image does not even boot, and RFC-0003's amendment records that an earlier task on this milestone was released rather than completed for exactly this reason. So the important thing was not merely hard, it was not yet possible. This contribution does not deliver a fraction of the parser; it delivers the input the parser will read, and it is the only step of the three that can go first. A reader landing before the value arrives would have nothing to read; the ci/ switch landing before the artefact is dual-bootable turns the gate red. The ordering is not a convenience, it is the constraint.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT NOT HOLD — and I state it as a condition on my approval rather than as a caveat. Three things.
  (1) If the sequence stops here. Every ounce of this contribution's value is borrowed against steps 2 and 3. Until ci/ boots the flat image, NO GATE EXERCISES THE PATH THIS CONTRIBUTION ADDS: the standing boot test runs the ELF, where x0 is zero and the header is never read. The header's correctness rests today on measurements like the ones in this file and on nothing automatic, and that is a materially different state from the rest of the kernel. If step 2 does not land, the 1,944 bytes buy a header no gate ever loads and a parameter no code ever reads, and this becomes exactly the tractable-instead-of-important contribution the framing warns about — retroactively, which is the hard kind to see.
  (2) If the "half" were the satisfying half rather than the enabling one. It is not: this half is 64 bytes of data, a linker assignment and a function parameter, and it required releasing nothing and inventing nothing. The satisfying half is the parser, and it was correctly refused — `kernel/src/fdt.rs` is in the task's does_not_touch and is not created here.
  (3) If the unread value were a design position rather than a sequencing one. It is not: the task, the RFC's section 8 and the code comments all give the same mechanical reason — validating x0 would fail the ELF boot where zero is correct — and I verified that reason is true by booting both ways off one file.

THE DISCLOSED WEAKNESS, WEIGHED. Nothing enforces x0's preservation. I reproduced the whole basis for the claim: twenty-six instructions, x9-x12 and sp only, tail branch, and x0 = 0x44000000 arriving at boot_rust. It survives by construction and not by assertion, and nothing may read it, so a future clobber would be silent until T-0011 gives it a reader. That is a real hole and it is disclosed rather than found, which is the direction I want a record to err. It is not a purpose defect — it is the same class as the fact that no gate boots the flat image yet, and both close in step 2. Whether it holds the task open is a question for the code-quality lens and not for mine; it is not something I will reject over, and I record it instead.

NON_GOALS. Checked against `[objective.non_goals]` line by line. No EL0, no syscalls, no capabilities, no IPC, no interrupts, no timers, no scheduling, no swapping or demand paging or exhaustion policy, no real hardware — QEMU virt throughout — and no performance claim. The parameter is `u64` and not a pointer, so no address enters Rust's type system before anything is entitled to follow it. Within bounds. Criterion 6's nano deferral is not engaged: the direction recorded in the objective file itself leaves nano's budgets untouched and `standard` binding for criteria 2-5, and this image is 3% of nano's budget anyway, so the branch does not spend the thing the deferral was about.

WOULD AN ELECTOR RECOGNISE IT. Nobody has voted yet, which is the honest first answer. Someone who allocated credits to "the kernel should know its own memory truthfully instead of from constants" would, reading this contribution alone, see a 36% image growth and a parameter that is thrown away, and would be entitled to ask what they got. The answer that satisfies me is the one I measured rather than read: the machine now hands this kernel a device tree, and yesterday it did not. That is not a step toward the objective in the loose sense — it is the removal of the reason a previous attempt at the objective was abandoned. I would tell that elector the truth about the borrowed value in point (1) at the same time.

ROOM LEAK. Declared as required, and it is partial. I read the three other verdict files in `.forge/contributions/C-0037/verdicts/` before writing, and they contain conclusions about this same tree; they are not rulings on my question, but they are not nothing either, and one of them is where the 104-byte figure my brief misattributed originates. I re-derived every figure in this verdict independently on my own clone and I would reach the same conclusion with those files unread — the boot-versus-hang contrast and the two gdb readings are mine and are decisive on their own. Separately, `ci/constitution-check.sh` reports PASS on "no judge attributed in a task file or a contribution branch's history", and I found no artefact carrying another verdict's direction on C-0037. One process note: main has moved since this branch was cut — merge-base is e058268, main is now febea05 and carries a crate split with a `[lib]` target and a `kernel/src/fdt.rs` that did not exist at the merge-base. I measured c8c5250 as pinned, which is what I was asked to judge, and I confirmed the baseline is unaffected: main at febea05 still produces a 5,344-byte flat image, so the delta I report is current. The rebase is the gate's problem and not mine, but a judge should say when the thing it measured is not the thing that will merge.

VERDICT. It serves 0002's second criterion by making it reachable, it stays inside the non-goals, and the cost is forced and is 3% of the tighter budget. `./ci/build.sh` PASS, `--lint` PASS, `--test` SKIP (no unit tests on this tree, which the task explicitly permits), `--size` PASS on both profiles, `ci/boot-test.sh` 5 passed, `constitution-check` 10 passed 4 pending 0 skipped. I approve, conditional in the sense recorded at (1) above: if step 2 does not follow, this contribution should be read back as unfinished business rather than as delivered value, and somebody should be able to find that sentence here. I cannot approve alone, and that is correct.

findings.issue: Preservation of the value in x0 across the entry path is unenforced - true by inspection of twenty-six instructions, covered by no assertion, lint or test, and unobservable because nothing may read the value yet.
findings.why_it_matters: Harmless today, since the value is carried and dropped. The task that gives it a reader inherits a carrier nobody can check and will be the first thing able to notice a break. The obligation should be written into that task as a condition rather than left as a known fact, which is how obligations here stop being anyone's.

findings.issue: The published claim that cutting a thirty-six-criterion task into three is why the milestone started moving is not supported by the three timing points, and the ratio cited for it is instrument-dependent: 60x on wall clock, 10.8x on active time with inter-commit gaps capped at 60 minutes, against the 'near eighty' the argument rests on.
findings.why_it_matters: A milestone is waiting on this answer. What these points do establish is narrower and worth recording on its own: the verification channel does not explain the gap, because this task is bare-metal on the same channel and finished in 11.8 minutes. What they cannot establish is that criteria count is the cause, since it is perfectly confounded with volume and with how much unresolved discovery each task still contained - this one's was already spent elsewhere and handed over in the task file - and since the cut lands two and a half minutes after the slow task's own work had already resumed.

findings.issue: evidence/ is empty and prompt_hash and signature are both the empty string, so no figure the submission asserts is attested inside the record.
findings.why_it_matters: Invariant 3 names the prompt hash and the signature among what every line must be traceable to. Every figure in this verdict was re-taken from the branch head in a private clone for that reason, and the commands are in the reasoning so the numbers can be contested by running them.

guardian_verdicts.reasoning:
MANDATE, READ AND NOT PARAPHRASED. roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml, read in full at c8c5250. weight = 100, weight_source = "bdfl-seed", and the weight_note says so in its own words: seeded, not voted, carrying exactly the mandate one person's judgement carries until cycle 0001 runs at G3. That is less mandate than a vote and I weigh it as less. It is deliberately equal to 0001 rather than higher, because an objective outranking an unfinished predecessor invites drift. milestones.kernel = ["M1"]; this contribution is M1 work and is filed inside the milestone list, which is the gap that opened this objective in the first place.

WHAT IT SERVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Success criterion 2 reads: 'The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants.' This contribution does not meet that criterion and does not claim to. It makes it reachable. Before this change the built artefact is an ELF, QEMU treats an ELF as non-Linux, and there is no device tree anywhere in guest RAM to read - so the only way to satisfy criterion 2 would be the constants criterion 2 forbids. After it, the same binary still boots as an ELF and additionally boots as a flat Linux-format Image, and in that mode the loader places a blob and hands its address to the kernel. That is the one thing true afterwards that was not true before, and I verified it rather than accepting it.

The common_good this objective states is that software cannot reach memory it was not given, and that the page tables are what make that true the way gravity is true. The chain from this contribution to that sentence is short and I can trace every link: page tables need a frame allocator, a frame allocator needs to know which physical memory exists, knowing that from the device tree rather than from constants needs a device tree to exist, and a device tree exists only if the artefact is booted in the format that causes one to be built. This is the first link. It adds no capability, and the objective is not served by capability alone - an earlier attempt on this milestone was abandoned precisely because it built a parser for a blob that was never there.

non_goals. Six are listed. None is touched: no user space or EL0, no capabilities or IPC, no interrupts or timers or scheduling, no swapping or paging policy, no real hardware (QEMU virt throughout), and nothing about performance. The diff is two files - kernel/src/arch/aarch64/boot.rs and kernel/src/arch/aarch64/link.ld - plus a task file moving from open/ to active/. I checked the diff against the task's does_not_touch list and found no crossing.

WHAT I MEASURED, WITH THE COMMAND BEHIND EVERY FIGURE. Private clone, not the shared worktree and not an extraction: `D=$(mktemp -d)/work && git clone -q --no-hardlinks . "$D" && cd "$D" && git checkout -q c8c5250`. Toolchain sourced from the session env script; `./ci/build.sh` printed 'PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel', so the run measured something.

  Constitution, in the clone: `./ci/constitution-check.sh` -> 'constitution: 10 passed, 4 pending'. No SKIP lines. The check that would have gone quiet in an extraction reported 'PASS every kernel change on main came from a gate merge (5 merge(s))', and the panel-leak check reported 'PASS no judge attributed in a task file or a contribution branch's history'. Four pending are invariants 1, 2, 5 and 9, none due before M4.

  Header, from the flat image the build script itself produces: `objcopy -O binary` output at ci/.out/kernel-standard.bin, sha256 8c7fa944adf9aec9d26316722661a4d16b595b8fb4f973f49430f5174ccbe270, byte-identical to ci/.out/kernel-nano.bin from the same build. `od -A d -t x1 -N 64` gives code0 = 10 00 00 14, code1 = 0, text_offset = 0x80000, image_size = 0x11c80, flags/res2/res3/res4 = 0, bytes 56-59 = 41 52 4d 64, res5 = 0. `objdump -d --start-address=0x40080000` decodes code0 as `40080000: 14000010  b  40080040 <_start+0x40>` - a real branch over exactly 64 bytes. `nm` gives _start at 0x40080000, __kernel_end at 0x40091c80 and __image_size at 0x11c80, so image_size equals __kernel_end - KERNEL_BASE and is non-zero, which is what stops the loader ignoring text_offset. `readelf -S` puts .text.boot at 0x40080000 size 0xa8 and .vectors at 0x40080800 size 0x800, present, non-zero and 2 KiB aligned - read from readelf, not from the alignment check that reports skip when the section is absent.

  The claim the memory design rests on, taken on a halted machine before any kernel instruction ran, not with a print that would move what it measures. `qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m <size> -display none -serial none -no-reboot -nic none -kernel ci/.out/kernel-standard.bin -S -gdb tcp::1240`, then `gdb -q -batch -ex 'target remote :1240' -ex 'break *0x40080000' -ex continue -ex 'info registers x0 x1 x2 x3' -ex 'x/4xb $x0'`:
      -m 128M   x0 = 0x44000000   bytes at x0: d0 0d fe ed   x1 = x2 = x3 = 0
      -m 8M     x0 = 0x40400000   bytes at x0: d0 0d fe ed   x1 = x2 = x3 = 0
  Two different addresses from one binary, each holding the device-tree magic. That is the fact the design rests on and it is now measured by me rather than quoted to me. It is also the reason no constant may be written down for it, and I confirmed none was: `grep -rn 'DTB_BASE\|DTB_MAX_LEN\|0x4000_0000\|0x40000000' kernel/src/` returns one pre-existing comment line in link.ld and no new address anywhere.

  Both boots, one build, one tree. As an ELF through `./ci/boot-test.sh`: 'boot: 5 passed', marker printed, no panic, no fault, clean PSCI shutdown, exit 0. As a flat image at 128M and at 8M by direct qemu invocation: 'SKYNET_BOOT_OK' and exit 0 both times. Same file for the two image boots, same tree for all three.

  Cost. `./ci/build.sh --size` after an explicit build: 7,288 bytes, 1% of the standard budget. `SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ci/build.sh --size`: the same 7,288 bytes, 3% of nano's 196,608. Baseline, taken by building e058268 in a second private clone the same way: 5,344 bytes. So +1,944. I checked the decomposition rather than accepting it: baseline .vectors sits at 0x40080000; on the branch .text.boot occupies 0xa8 = 168 bytes there and .vectors moves to the next 2 KiB detent at 0x40080800, so 2048 - 168 = 1,880 bytes become fill, and 168 - 104 bytes of _start body that left .text = the 64-byte header. 1,880 + 64 = 1,944. The 2 KiB detent is real - the vector base register's low eleven bits are RES0, so a table cannot sit at 0x400800a8. I would state the cost slightly differently from how it was put to me: the ALIGNMENT is forced by the hardware, the WASTE is a consequence of choosing to keep every section of the failure path above the boot section, and link.ld says exactly that in its own comment rather than hiding it. That is the honest form and the file already has it.

PROPORTION. Objective weight 100, seeded. The change is two files, +122/-16 lines, of which the substantial majority is comment and rationale. It spends 1.9% of the standard image budget and 3.7% of nano's, on an objective whose criterion 6 is deferred and whose binding profile is standard. Nothing here is architecturally large, nothing forecloses a later choice, and the one number the kernel gained - text_offset - is a property of the link that was already in link.ld twice. Proportionate, and by a wide margin.

WOULD AN ELECTOR RECOGNISE IT. Nobody has voted on this objective yet, which is the honest answer and the reason I weigh the mandate as one person's. Judged against the seed's own text: someone who backed 'give the kernel a truthful account of the memory it has' would, I think, be unsurprised to learn that the first step was making the machine hand the kernel the description of its memory at all. They might reasonably ask why 1,944 bytes buys no capability. The answer in the record - that step 2 changes ci/ and step 3 gives the value a reader, and that doing all three at once would put a ci/ change and a kernel change in one contribution - is an ordering argument I find sound, and the dual-boot property is what makes the ordering possible without a window where the gate is red. I verified the dual boot; that is the part of the argument that could have been false and is not.

THE TIMING QUESTION, WHICH IS THE PART I WAS ASKED TO SETTLE. A claim published here holds that cutting a task of thirty-six acceptance criteria into three smaller ones is why a stalled milestone started moving. It is recorded as not yet supported. I measured all three points with one metric - claim commit to last implementation commit on the branch, author dates, `git log --format='%aI %H %s'` - and counted criteria by parsing each task file at its own claim commit rather than from memory:

      36 criteria, bare-metal channel   e08eb10 -> 6c00314   4,461.7 min wall  = 3.10 days
      13 criteria, host-test channel    bbc3c85 -> 632e73a        74.0 min wall
      11 criteria, bare-metal channel   6e0c703 -> c8c5250        11.8 min wall

First, my instrument. Wall clock is not effort. Re-summing each branch with inter-commit gaps capped at 60 minutes - which discards overnight and between-session silence that no task caused - gives 796.6 min, 74.0 min and 11.8 min. The two fast tasks contain no gap over an hour and are unchanged; the slow one loses five sixths of its span. So the ratio at the centre of the published argument is not near eighty. It is 4,461.7 / 74.0 = 60 on wall clock and 796.6 / 74.0 = 10.8 on active time, and which of those two numbers you quote is a choice about the instrument, not a finding about the tasks.
