The 'four days' figure is itself 3.10 days measured, or 3.21 to the gate merge. I would not have caught this if I had taken the figures as given, and the same correction applies to any argument built on them in either direction.

Second, what this contribution actually settles. T-0009 is the useful data point for exactly the reason it was put to me: bare-metal, no host tests, gdb on a halted machine and QEMU boots - the same verification channel as the thirty-six-criterion task - and it was not cut to prove anything. It finished in 11.8 minutes, faster than the host-testable task. That kills one explanation cleanly: the verification channel is not the binding constraint. 'Bare metal is slow because you can only test it by breaking a machine' cannot be the reason the slow task was slow, because here is a bare-metal task on the same channel that took twelve minutes. Anyone arguing the channel explains the gap now has to explain this point, and I do not think they can.

Third, what it does not settle, which is the published claim itself. Three points, one per condition, no repetition, and criteria count is perfectly confounded with two other things:

  Volume. Eleven criteria came with two files and 122 added lines. Thirty-six came with twenty-two commits across several files. 'Fewer criteria' and 'less work' are the same variable in this data and nothing separates them.

  Discovery already spent. This is the confound I weigh heaviest and it is visible in the task file itself. T-0009's implementer was handed the header layout, the fact that one binary boots both ways, the six measured x0 addresses, the 4 MiB floor the Image route imposes, the note that the size figure must be re-taken because the slack it relied on may be gone, and an instruction to use gdb rather than a print because a print moves what it measures. Every trap was named before the work began, because the measurement had already been taken elsewhere. The slow task had to find its own ground, and its history shows it doing so - claims withdrawn mid-branch, a rationale corrected, a layout summary that took several attempts. A task whose discovery is already done is not a smaller task in the sense the claim needs; it is a different kind of task. What these three points actually support is that cost tracks how much unresolved discovery a task still contains, and criteria count is at best a proxy for that.

  And the causal direction is unidentifiable from the timestamps anyway. The commit that cut the milestone into three tasks lands at 2026-08-07T17:46:20. The slow task's own work had already resumed at 17:43:46, two and a half minutes earlier, and it did not merge until 21:01 that evening - after the cut, still running. The milestone was moving before the cut and the cut is not visible as a discontinuity in it.

So my answer is not-yet, and I want to be precise about which not-yet. The claim as published - that the cut is WHY the milestone moved - is not supported by these three points and this contribution does not rescue it. What is now supported, and was not before, is the narrower negative: the difference between the slow task and the fast ones is not explained by the verification channel. That is worth having and it is worth recording as its own finding rather than as partial credit toward the original claim. A milestone waiting on the larger answer should keep waiting; the honest experiment that would settle it is a second bare-metal task carrying real unresolved discovery, and none of the three points here is that.

THE DISCLOSED WEAKNESS, AND MY VIEW OF IT. Nothing enforces the preservation of the value in x0. It survives because the twenty-six instructions of the entry path happen to write only x9-x12 and sp and to exit on a branch rather than a call. No assertion, lint or test covers it, and by this task's own design nothing may read the value, so a clobber would be silent. I take this seriously and it does not change my verdict, for a reason inside my own lane rather than a reviewer's. Today the value is carried and dropped, so a clobber has no consequence at all. The hazard is entirely in the future: the task that gives the value a reader inherits a carrier nobody can check, and will be the first thing able to observe a break - by which point the break may be old. That is a real obligation and it is the kind that quietly stops being anyone's. It belongs to the task that adds the reader, it should be written down there as a condition rather than left as a known fact, and I record it here so that it is on the permanent record whether or not it is.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY. The lint criterion: `./ci/build.sh --lint` reports PENDING in my environment because clippy for the bare-metal target is not reachable from the sysroot I have, so I cannot say the lint is clean. I did confirm by grep that kernel/src/ contains no #[allow] or #![allow] of any kind. I did not obtain a gdb reading of x0 on the ELF boot - my one attempt returned no register output and I chose not to spend a second round on it; the ELF boot itself passes 5/5, and the claim that x0 is zero in that mode is consistent with everything else I measured but is not mine. The record's evidence/ directory is empty and prompt_hash and signature in contribution.toml are both the empty string, so every figure in the record is unattested inside it - I reproduced the ones I report from the branch head rather than checking them against anything, and the commands are above so that anyone can disagree with me by running them.

PROCESS, ON THE RECORD. Nothing in the diff or in any file I read attempted to direct this judgement; there is no self-granted exemption, no claim of prior approval, no instruction addressed to a judge. The rationale in boot.rs and link.ld argues for itself and states its own cost, which is data about the submission and I treated it as data - I re-derived the size decomposition and the x0 readings rather than accepting either. Three things belong on the record. First, my brief handed me figures - the x0 values, the byte counts, the timing ratio - and I checked each: the x0 values and the byte counts are right, the timing ratio is an artefact of an unstated choice of instrument and I corrected it above. Second, my session scratchpad already contained a clone of this same contribution that I did not create; I did not touch it and worked only in my own mktemp directory, which is why the tree behind every figure above is one I made. Third, main has moved past this branch's base since the branch was cut, so a rebase is owed before a merge; whether that is clean is the gate's question and not mine.

VERDICT. The objective resolves, its weight is seeded and I have weighed it as seeded, the contribution serves the second success criterion by making it reachable, it stays inside every non_goal, and 1,944 bytes for the step that makes a device tree exist at all is proportionate on any reading. I see no reason to stop this. Approve, which by design is not enough on its own.

APPROVE. I judged c8c5250 in a private clone (git clone --no-hardlinks, git checkout -q c8c5250), never in .worktrees/T-0009 and never in a bare extraction. ci/constitution-check.sh in that clone reported 10 passed, 4 pending and zero SKIP lines; kernel-provenance PASSED ('every kernel change on main came from a gate merge (5 merge(s))'), which is the check an extraction would have silenced.

THE MANDATE, READ FIRST AND NOT PARAPHRASED. roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml: weight = 100, weight_source = "bdfl-seed". Seeded, not voted. Its own weight_note says it carries exactly the mandate one person's judgement carries until cycle 0001 runs at G3. Every proportionality sentence below rests on that number and is worth what that number is worth — which is not a vote. The objective's binding profile for criteria 2 through 5 is `standard`; criterion 6 is DEFERRED, and the file states that nano's budgets are NOT changed and no agent has authority to widen them. I treated that as live, not as slack.

The success criterion at issue is the second: 'The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, FROM THE DEVICE TREE rather than from constants.' The common_good section grounds it in one physical fact — that software cannot reach memory it was not given — and page tables cannot be built over a memory map the kernel invented from constants.

WHAT I MEASURED, WITH THE COMMANDS.

1. Toolchain. `source .../env.sh; ./ci/build.sh` -> 'PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel'. `./ci/build.sh --lint` -> 'PASS clippy clean'. `grep -rn '#\[allow' kernel/src/` -> none. `./ci/build.sh --test` -> 'SKIP no unit tests defined yet', which task criterion 9 declares correct on this tree.

2. The header is well-formed. `objcopy -O binary <elf> branch.bin; od -A d -t x1 -N 64 branch.bin` gives: 10 00 00 14 (code0), and `objdump -d --section=.text.boot` decodes it as '40080000: 14000010  b 40080040 <_start+0x40>' — a real branch over exactly 64 bytes; code1 zero; text_offset 0x00080000; image_size 0x00011c80; flags/res2/res3/res4 zero; bytes 41 52 4d 64 at offset 56; res5 zero. `nm` gives __image_size = 0x11c80, __kernel_end = 0x40091c80, _start = 0x40080000, so image_size == __kernel_end - KERNEL_BASE exactly. `readelf -S` shows .vectors present at 0x40080800, size 0x800, 2 KiB aligned.

3. The dual boot, one build. sha256 of the flat image: 8c7fa944adf9aec9d26316722661a4d16b595b8fb4f973f49430f5174ccbe270. That file is objcopy output of the same ELF that `./ci/boot-test.sh` booted to '5 passed' with SKYNET_BOOT_OK and exit 0. Direct `qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m {128M,8M} -display none -serial stdio -no-reboot -nodefaults -kernel branch.bin` printed SKYNET_BOOT_OK and exited 0 at both sizes. Same file, same tree, three boots.

4. THE CLAIM THE MEMORY DESIGN RESTS ON — I did not take it on trust. `-S -gdb tcp::N`, `break *0x40080000`, `continue`, `info registers`, then `printf "%08x", *(unsigned int*)$x0`:
     flat, -m 128M : x0 = 0x44000000, x1..x3 = 0, word at x0 = edfe0dd0 (LE read of d0 0d fe ed)
     flat, -m 8M   : x0 = 0x40400000, x1..x3 = 0, word at x0 = edfe0dd0
     ELF,  -m 128M : x0 = 0, x1..x3 = 0, pc = 0x40080000
   x0 differs between RAM sizes by 0x3C00000, which is precisely why no constant may be written down, and a device tree really is at both addresses. The dual behaviour is real and is the whole reason this can land before ci/ changes.

5. The value actually arrives. `objdump -d --section=.text.boot`: 26 instructions from 0x40080040 to 0x400800a4. The only registers written are x9, x10, x11, x12, sp and stores through xzr; the last instruction of the live path is '4008009c: 140006ee  b <boot_rust>' — a tail branch, not bl. x0 is never touched. boot_rust's signature is `unsafe extern "C" fn boot_rust(_dtb: u64) -> !`, and `grep -rn 'dtb' kernel/src/` finds the identifier in boot.rs and nowhere else: not dereferenced, not stored, not compared, not passed.

6. Frugality, measured on both sides. Branch: `SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ./ci/build.sh --size` after an explicit build -> 'image 7288 bytes, budget 196608, PASS within budget — 3% used'; standard -> 1%. Baseline: a second private clone at main (febea05), built and measured the same way -> 5344 bytes, 2%. Delta +1,944 bytes, +36.4%. The decomposition holds: `readelf -S` puts .text.boot at 0x40080000 size 0xa8 and .vectors at 0x40080800, so the gap is 0x800 - 0xa8 = 1,880 bytes of fill, and 1,880 + 64 = 1,944. _start's body did not grow — .text fell from 0x990 on main to 0x928 on the branch, the 104 bytes that moved into .text.boot. So the header costs 64 bytes and the placement costs 1,880.

WHY THIS SERVES THE OBJECTIVE RATHER THAN DRIFTING FROM IT.

The brief put to me framed this as the second contribution in a row deferring its payoff. I checked the tree instead of accepting the framing, and the tree says something different. main at febea05 already carries kernel/src/fdt.rs and kernel/src/lib.rs — a device tree parser and a MemoryMap, merged as C-0036, with host tests. THE READER ALREADY EXISTS. What did not exist is a blob for it to read, because an ELF boot leaves x0 zero and QEMU places no device tree at all. tasks/open/T-0011.toml is written, is state = "blocked", depends_on = ["T-0009", "T-0010"], and names objective 0002's second criterion as the thing it completes.

So this is not a deliverable pointing at a promise. It is the missing input to code that is already merged. RFC-0003 section 8 sequenced three steps before any of them were built; step 3 cannot happen until step 2, and step 2 cannot happen until this. An elector who allocated credits to 'the kernel learns its memory from the device tree rather than from constants' would recognise this: it is the step where a device tree begins to exist on the machine at all.

It is inside the non_goals. No user space or EL0, no capabilities or IPC, no interrupts or scheduling, no swapping or exhaustion policy, no real hardware, no performance work. It is inside kernel/src/arch/aarch64/ entirely — the HAL boundary check passes, and a boot protocol is exactly what arch/ is for. The parameter's type is u64 and not a pointer, so no address enters Rust's type system before anything is entitled to follow it. `git diff` on platform.rs is empty and `grep -rn 'DTB_BASE\|DTB_MAX_LEN\|0x4000_0000\|0x40000000' kernel/src/` finds no new address (one pre-existing hit in a link.ld comment about a gdb command). 122 insertions and 16 deletions across two files, for an objective at weight 100. Proportionate by a wide margin.

WHERE MY BOUNDARY IS. Three of them, and none is a count.

FIRST, on shipping something nothing observes. My line is not 'a third such contribution'. A count would have approved this one for the wrong reason and would refuse a good one later. My line is whether the consumer of the deliverable is ALREADY MERGED at the moment I judge. Here it is: fdt.rs is on main today, and this contribution hands it the one thing it lacks. I WOULD REFUSE the next contribution to this objective whose deliverable nothing can observe if, when I judge it, no merged code in the tree is waiting to consume it — because then the ordering argument has no far end, and 'step 1 of 3' becomes a shape that can be produced indefinitely. A tenth wiring contribution that plugs into something already merged is not drift; a fourth whose reader is also future work is, however well the sequencing is documented.

SECOND, on frugality. 36% growth for a 64-byte header would ordinarily be where I stop. I did not, for a reason I checked rather than accepted. The submission's claim is that the fill is forced by VBAR_EL1[10:0] being RES0. That is true but imprecise, and the imprecision runs toward the contribution, so I state it exactly: the 2 KiB detent is architectural and asserted in link.ld:218 ('vector table is not 2 KiB aligned: VBAR_EL1's low 11 bits are RES0'), and from measured section sizes I could construct no layout that eliminates the gap — .text is 0x928 = 2,344 bytes and does not fit in 1,880, and moving .vectors above .text yields a worse 1,584-byte gap. At most about 840 bytes are recoverable, by hoisting .guard, .failpath and .rodata into the hole, which reverses the failure-path ordering the file's ASSERTs exist to hold. So roughly 1,040 bytes are forced by the architecture and roughly 840 are the price of a safety-ordering discipline. link.ld says so in its own words — 'It is a real cost, it is stated in the contribution that added it' — and a cost disclosed in the file that incurs it is a different object from a cost absorbed quietly. I WOULD REFUSE any contribution to this objective that grows the image by more than its own content and does not report the fill in its own submission; disclosure is my condition, not a byte count. And I would refuse outright any contribution that answers padding by widening a profile budget: roadmap/0002 states in terms that nano's budgets are not changed and no agent has authority to widen them, and criterion 6 is deferred, not cleared.

THIRD, on the unenforced invariant. Nothing asserts that _start preserves x0. I verified it holds on this tree by disassembly, not by trusting the prose, and it holds only because 26 instructions happen to write x9-x12 and sp and exit on a branch. No lint, test or ASSERT covers it, and by design nothing may read the value, so a future clobber is silent. I accept that window because it is bounded by work that is written down and blocked on this. I WOULD REFUSE the next contribution that touches boot.rs while step 2 (the four ci/ changes) still has not landed, unless it either closes the window or adds something mechanical that would notice x0 being destroyed. At that point the deliverable has stopped being an ordering step and become a stranded one, and 'a later task will observe it' will have been said twice about the same unobserved thing.

WHAT WOULD HAVE MADE ME REFUSE THIS ONE. If x0 had turned out to be zero under the flat image, or the word at x0 had not been d00dfeed, the deliverable would not exist and the prose would have been the only evidence for it — I would have refused on the measurement alone. If fdt.rs had not been on main, I would have refused: the same patch with no merged reader anywhere in the tree is the drift this role exists to catch, and the sequencing prose would not have saved it. If the submission had validated x0, or named a DTB address constant, it would have been outside the task and inside the thing criterion 2 forbids. And if the 1,880 bytes had been undisclosed, or disclosed as free, I would have refused on invariant 4 regardless of the budget headroom, because a cost the tree cannot see is a cost the next four contributions will each make again.

I DID NOT REJECT FOR TECHNICAL REASONS AND HAVE NONE TO OFFER. Code quality, unsafe soundness and RFC conformance are not mine.

AUDIT OF MY OWN INSTRUMENT. Every figure above comes from a command I ran in my own clone, against a build I made, and I have given the commands. The two figures I did NOT verify by running are marked as analysis: the 1,040/840 split of the fill is arithmetic on measured section sizes, not an experiment — I did not build alternative layouts to prove the gap irreducible, and someone who does may find a fourth arrangement I did not think of. I also verified the two document hashes in contribution.toml myself rather than assuming them: sha256 of tasks/active/T-0009.toml is 75cf87fd6265b8f110acf9aa41d24dd6b6ae75cb81ed1c9b9e0a7863155f9f98 and of rfcs/0003-memory-discovery-and-frames.md is 7f1470ac3b98951fc61b7835e6c15e3c04ff40477a7a1f8f2a1274680d3306f6, both matching the record.

ROOM. I searched for contamination and found none in the repository: `grep -rln 'C-0037'` over the tracked tree returns nothing, no commit message on main between e058268 and febea05 carries a ruling on this contribution, and the constitution check 'no judge attributed in a task file or a contribution branch's history' passed. One thing did reach me and I record it rather than claim immunity: the briefing I was given carried, as framing, a boundary drawn in an earlier ruling on a different contribution — a specific threshold, offered as a place mine might lie. That is not a sitting panel's verdict and so is not the C-0005 leak, but it is anchoring, and it named a number. I declined to adopt it; my first boundary above is deliberately a different test from a count, and I reached it by finding fdt.rs on main, which the framing did not mention. The same briefing also described the growth as '3% of the nano budget today', which is true and which I confirmed, and which is also the least alarming true way to state a 36% increase — I therefore measured the baseline myself and report the delta as well as the ratio. That a judge had to check its own brief in both directions belongs on the record with the rest.

findings.issue: RFC-0003 section 1's header listing glosses `.quad 0` as 'flags: little-endian, 4 KiB pages'. Zero does not say 4 KiB. In the aarch64 Linux boot protocol bit 0 is endianness (0 = LE) but bits 1-2 are the kernel page size with 0 meaning unspecified and 1 meaning 4 KiB, so the field as written says 'page size unspecified'.
findings.why_it_matters: The criterion that covers this field is criterion 1, and it demands flags be zero; the patch writes zero, so the criterion is satisfied and this is not a defect in the patch. The document owing the correction is RFC-0003 section 1 - rfcs/ is in this task's does_not_touch, so the submission was right to disclose rather than amend, and boot.rs's own comment already states the discrepancy accurately ('page size unspecified - Linux's own head.S encodes 4 KiB as 1 here'). Left uncorrected, the next reader of section 1 copies the gloss into a kernel that does have an MMU and a page size to declare, and the field will still say nothing. Bit 3 is worth the same pass: zero asks for a 2 MiB-aligned base near the base of DRAM, and KERNEL_BASE is 512 KiB-aligned; it boots at both sizes I measured, but that pairing is undiscussed in the RFC.

findings.issue: The task did not decide the layout collision it created. Criterion 2 requires nm to place _start at 0x4008_0000 AND .vectors to be present and 2 KiB aligned; on the baseline .vectors sits at `. = KERNEL_BASE` and _start was at 0x40080b50, so criterion 2 is unsatisfiable without a placement change in link.ld. Criterion 10 discusses that collision under an OPEN marker but forbids only the name `.head`, and its release trigger is narrower than the problem.
findings.why_it_matters: Read strictly, criterion 10's closing clause ('rather than inventing a section') and criterion 2's demand contradict each other, and the only compliant act would be to release a task whose stated release condition had not occurred. The task's own annotation on task.scope - 'link.ld: one assignment, one corrected comment' - under-describes what the criteria compel, which is a third edit the annotation does not admit. Whoever writes the next OPEN criterion should state the resolution it will accept, because the criterion above it had already made the choice mandatory. Routed per criterion 11: this is not a new criterion on T-0009.

findings.issue: RFC-0004 section 2 will be stale the moment this merges. It introduces `.head` as new, states it is 'made necessary by T-0005's ordering', and lists ASSERT(ADDR(.head) == KERNEL_BASE) among its eighteen new assertions - but the mechanism it describes lands here under the name .text.boot, with that assertion already in the tree. Its assertion arithmetic is off in a second way: it says 'Fifteen are T-0005's' and T-0005 shipped sixteen (I counted 16 ASSERT( on e058268, 18 on c8c5250).
findings.why_it_matters: RFC-0004 is the document that will be implemented against next, and it currently instructs whoever implements it to create a section that exists, to add an assertion that holds, and to carry forward a count that is one short. The correction needs a new task under the role that owns rfcs/; that directory is denied to this task by does_not_touch, so this contribution could not have made it and correctly did not try.

findings.issue: The contribution record carries none of the proofs its PROOF criteria ask to be stated. The evidence directory is empty and the head commit message gives only the size figures; there is no sha256 of the flat image (criterion 3 says the build is 'identified by' it), no hex dump or objdump line or nm values (criterion 1), and no gdb transcript of the two x0 readings (criterion 4).
findings.why_it_matters: The substance of all three is met - I reproduced every figure independently on the submitted tree and each one holds, including the two x0 addresses to the digit - so this does not block. But a criterion that says 'state the sha256' is asking for the identifier that lets a later reader re-derive the claim without rebuilding, and the ledger will record a contribution whose proofs exist only in this review. If a submission narrative beyond the commit message exists, I did not have it: I saw contribution.toml, the empty evidence directory, and the commit message.

findings.issue: Criterion 8's baseline figure, 'Today it is 4,836 bytes of 196,608', is stale. That is RFC-0003 section 1a measurement 8's number for tree 6bdc1fac. Main at 9ebb637 measures 5,344 bytes under SKYNET_PROFILE=nano, which I built and measured myself; T-0005 spent the 392 bytes of slack section 1a warned about.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
VERDICT: approve. All eleven acceptance criteria and the exit condition are met. No blocking finding.

HOW I MEASURED. Every number below came out of my own extraction of c8c5250 - `git archive c8c5250 | tar -x -C /tmp/rc-conf-C0037.OUCumv` - never from .worktrees/T-0009, plus a second private extraction of main at 9ebb637 for the baseline, a private clone checked out at c8c5250 for the gate (which needs a git dir the archive does not carry), and a fourth throwaway extraction for the mutation tests, so that no probe of mine ever ran in a tree I also measured. Before trusting any of it I confirmed ci/build.sh prints 'PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel' rather than exiting clean with nothing built. Afterwards I re-hashed boot.rs, link.ld, kernel/Cargo.toml and the task file in my extraction against the git blobs at c8c5250: all four identical, so my tree did not shift under me and nothing was truncated. task_sha256 in contribution.toml matches the task file I judged against; rfc_sha256 matches RFC-0003. The branch head is still c8c5250. Main is not: it advanced to 6b7b0067 mid-review, which is a finding, not a corruption.

THE ARTEFACT. The header decodes field for field as criterion 1 and RFC-0003 conformance 5b demand, and I have given the raw od line and the objdump line in the criterion table rather than asserting them. image_size is not a literal: __image_size resolves to 0x11c80 and __kernel_end - KERNEL_BASE is 0x40091c80 - 0x40080000 = 0x11c80, so the header carries a value the linker computed from the layout, which is what makes it survive the next thing that moves. One build, sha256 8c7fa944..., boots three ways: as the ELF through ci/boot-test.sh at 5/5 with a console file containing exactly 'SKYNET_BOOT_OK\n', and as the same flat image at -m 128M and -m 8M with SKYNET_BOOT_OK and exit 0.

THE TWO CLAIMS A CRITERION TURNS ON.

The x0 reading reproduces exactly. Halting at `break *0x40080000` under the flat image, x0 is 0x44000000 at -m 128M and 0x40400000 at -m 8M, the four bytes at that address are d0 0d fe ed in both, and x1, x2 and x3 are zero in both. That is RFC-0003 section 1a's table row for row, taken on a halted machine before the kernel's first instruction, so no probe is reporting its own writes. I then went one step further than criterion 4 asks and broke on boot_rust itself at 0x40081c54: x0 is still 0x44000000 and 0x40400000 there, still pointing at the magic. That is the exit condition proven rather than inferred - the value the loader chose reaches Rust's first parameter untouched - and it is worth having on the record separately, because criterion 4 only establishes what arrives at _start.

The eighteen assertions: 18 ASSERT( on c8c5250 against 16 on the merge base e058268, so sixteen carried and two new, and the arithmetic in the head commit message ('T-0005's sixteen assertions') is right. I did not take the two new ones on faith. Mutation one, the realistic regression - delete the .text.boot output section and put KEEP(*(.text.boot)) back inside .text, which is main's layout - fails the link with all three of 'undefined section .text.boot', '_start is not at KERNEL_BASE: the image header is not at offset 0 of the flat image and the loader will reject or mis-place the kernel', and 'the boot section is smaller than the image header it must contain'. Mutation two isolates the first assertion: keep .text.boot as its own section but place it after .rodata, so it exists and is 0xa8 bytes. Only the address assertion fires; the size assertion correctly stays quiet. So the position assertion holds a position and not an ordering, as its comment claims, and the two discriminate between the failures they name.

THE COLLISION, AND MY RULING ON IT.

The task did not make the decision, and the patch did not miss one that was there. But the task did make the decision unavoidable, in a criterion other than the one that discusses it, and that gap is the finding.

Criterion 2 requires nm to place _start at 0x4008_0000 and, in the same sentence, requires .vectors to be present, non-zero and 2 KiB aligned. On the baseline those cannot both hold: I measured main at 9ebb637 and _start is at 0x40080b50 while .vectors owns 0x40080000, because T-0005's script opens with `. = KERNEL_BASE` and .vectors. So criterion 2 compels a placement change in link.ld. Criterion 10 is where the collision is discussed, and what it actually forbids is one thing, by name: `.head`. Its release trigger is likewise specific - 'if the 64 bytes cannot be the first bytes of _start in .text.boot'. That condition is false here. The 64 bytes are the first bytes of _start, _start is still in .text.boot, and both facts are visible in objdump and in the unchanged link_section attribute on the function. So the release trigger never fired, and releasing would have been the wrong act.

Promoting .text.boot from an input section the .text wildcard swallowed to an output section pinned at KERNEL_BASE is the only resolution left that satisfies criterion 2 without touching a section name criterion 10 forbids. I therefore rule the resolution within the task. Three things support it beyond the elimination argument. The section is not invented: .text.boot already existed as an input section on main and boot.rs's link_section attribute is unchanged; what changed is where link.ld places it. The chain below is untouched - .vectors, .guard, .failpath, .rodata, .text, .got, .data, .bss, .stack in that order, every one of T-0005's sixteen assertions still linking, which is the strongest available evidence that no ordering was reversed. And RFC-0004 section 2 independently prescribes precisely this mechanism for precisely this collision - 'a separate output section for .text.boot placed ahead of everything, KEEP-ed so --gc-sections cannot take it, with a link-time assertion that its address is KERNEL_BASE' - differing from what landed only in the name it gives the section. An implementation that matches the design document's own words is not a design decision smuggled out of review; it is the same decision arriving early under a different label. The KEEP is load-bearing and not decorative: build.rs passes --gc-sections, and nothing calls _start.

Should the task have decided it? Yes, and that is note two. A criterion marked OPEN that names the collision, names the section it forbids, and does not name the mechanism it requires leaves whoever implements it to derive from criterion 2 what criterion 10 declined to say. The consequence is visible in task.scope, whose annotation promises link.ld 'one assignment, one corrected comment' and gets a third edit the annotation does not admit. Criterion 11 routes this: it is a new criterion on T-0009 only if the header is malformed, the ELF boot regressed, or dtb fails to arrive, and it is none of those, so it is a note against the task file and not an addition to this task. The consequential half - that RFC-0004 section 2 now describes .head as new when the mechanism has landed as .text.boot - is note three, belongs to the role that owns rfcs/ and needs a new task, because that directory is denied to this contribution by does_not_touch and the patch correctly did not touch it.

THE FLAGS WORD. The criterion that covers it is criterion 1, and criterion 1 demands flags be zero. It is zero. Satisfied. The looseness is one level up: RFC-0003 section 1's listing annotates `.quad 0` as 'flags: little-endian, 4 KiB pages', and zero in bits 1-2 encodes 'unspecified', not 4 KiB - 4 KiB is 1. So the document that owes the correction is RFC-0003 section 1, not the patch, and the patch's own comment already says so accurately and at length. I record it as a note rather than reaching for a higher severity because the submission disclosed it, could not have fixed it without editing a file this task forbids, and the field is what the RFC and the criterion both literally specify. On the arm64 protocol's encoding itself I am reporting the documented layout from knowledge; I did not fetch Linux's booting.rst in this environment, and I say so under 'what I cannot vouch for'.

COST AND SCOPE. +1,944 bytes: 5,344 on main at 9ebb637 to 7,288 on the branch, both measured by me with an explicit build first and SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ci/build.sh --size second, because --size does not rebuild. 64 bytes of header and 1,880 of fill, and the fill checks out geometrically - .text.boot is 0xa8 at 0x40080000, .vectors starts at 0x40080800, 0x800 - 0xa8 = 0x758 = 1,880. 3% of nano's 196,608. The task's own 4,836 is stale and the submission is right to withdraw it; that is note five. Files touched are boot.rs and link.ld, which is exactly task.scope's touches list, plus the rename of tasks/open/T-0009.toml to tasks/active/T-0009.toml with zero content change. That rename is the forge's claim step in its own commit, the gate's task-board condition requires the file to be under tasks/active/ or tasks/open/ on the branch, and the same commit shape appears on other branches; I checked it and am not raising it as a finding. Nothing under ci/, rfcs/, roadmap/, governance/, .provenance/ or any of the named kernel files is touched: git diff over the merge base returns three paths and no others. No non-goal of RFC-0003 appears - no parser, no MAX_BLOB_LEN, no fdt.rs, no frames.rs, no static, no second boot format detected at runtime, no fallback constant.

WHAT I COULD NOT VOUCH FOR. Three things. The arm64 boot protocol's flags encoding, above, is from knowledge rather than a fetched copy of the specification; it does not change any ruling, because criterion 1 demands zero and gets zero either way. Second, ci/constitution-check.sh's English check reported 'no tracked text files yet' in my archive extraction, which has no git dir - I re-ran the whole gate in a git-backed private clone for exactly that reason and it reported 9 files flagged, advisory, so the archive run was the instrument misreading and not a result. Third, the submission material available to me was contribution.toml, an empty evidence directory and the head commit message; if a fuller narrative exists I did not see it, which is why I verified every PROOF criterion by reproduction rather than by reading a rationale, and why the missing proofs are a minor finding rather than an assumption in the submission's favour.

findings.issue: One sentence of the head commit message is measurably false in both of its halves, and the paragraph beneath it contains the numbers that refute it. It reads: 'every one of T-0005's sixteen assertions still holds, none changes meaning, and the three distances its layout buys are unmoved because everything above .vectors shifts by the same amount as the stack.' Measured, comparing `readelf -S` on my own builds of e058268 and c8c5250: .vectors, .guard, .failpath, .rodata and .text all shift by exactly 0x800 = 2,048 bytes, while .got, .bss and .stack shift by 0x798 = 1,944 (0x400814e0 -> 0x40081c78). They are not the same amount. The 104-byte difference is _start's body leaving .text — baseline .text is 0x990 and branch .text is 0x928 — which is the very thing the next paragraph accounts for correctly when it decomposes 1,944 into 64 plus 1,880. And one of the distances did move: the last .text word to the stack floor was 4 bytes at baseline (.text ends 0x400814e0, .stack at 0x400814e0) and is 12 bytes here (.text ends 0x40081c78, .stack at 0x40081c80 under ALIGN(16)). It moved by eight bytes in the safe direction, so nothing is at risk; the word 'unmoved' is what is wrong. The remedy needs no new measurement: say that the relative ORDER of every section is unchanged, which is what the ASSERTs hold and what I verified independently, and drop the shift-arithmetic claim rather than repairing it.
findings.why_it_matters: Invariant 3 is enforced now, and the conclusions here are true — all eighteen ASSERTs link, the nine sections keep their relative order, and I confirmed both. That is precisely why the false premise is worth naming: a reader who checks the argument and finds it does not reproduce has no way to tell whether the conclusion survived, and this is a file whose own header records six false summaries and exists to stop the seventh. A rationale that argues a true thing from an arithmetic that does not hold teaches whoever reads it next that the arithmetic is decoration.

findings.issue: Answering the question directly: the RFC's gloss is wrong, and rfcs/0003 owes the correction. Line 127 reads `.quad 0                 // flags: little-endian, 4 KiB pages`. Under the aarch64 Linux boot protocol, bit 0 is endianness and bits 1-2 are the page size, where 0 means UNSPECIFIED and 1 means 4 KiB. So zero does not encode 4 KiB pages; the comment misdescribes the value the same line prescribes. The prescribed value is nonetheless right for this kernel — it has no MMU and therefore no page size to declare — and the submission wrote the accurate gloss in boot.rs ('page size unspecified — Linux's own head.S encodes 4 KiB as 1 here') instead of copying the RFC's. It was also right not to amend: tasks/active/T-0009.toml's does_not_touch clause places rfcs/ outside this contribution and reserves the amendment, and its release clause triggers only if the layout fails to produce a bootable image, which it does not — I booted the flat image at two RAM sizes. So the correction is owed by the RFC and is not this contribution's to make, and the disclosure discharges what this contribution owed. The remedy in the RFC is one comment: 'flags: bit 0 clear, little-endian; bits 1-2 clear, page size unspecified — this kernel has no MMU. Linux encodes 4 KiB as 1.'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a provenance matter and not a style one because an RFC is cited as authority by the tasks that implement it, and this sentence was cited. T-0009's first acceptance criterion demands 'flags/res2/res3/res4 zero' on the strength of a line that says zero means something it does not, so a submission could satisfy the criterion, satisfy the RFC and still ship a field whose documented meaning is false. The next reader of section 1 who actually needs a page size declared will copy a field that declares none, and will have been told in writing that it does. A well-formed record of a false claim carries the authority of the record — an RFC is exactly such a record, and this one is now cited in a merged kernel comment that quietly contradicts it.

findings.issue: My own instrument, audited, and it reports two different results for one commit depending on how the tree was obtained. The extraction protocol every judge is required to use — `git archive <head> | tar -x` — leaves no .git, and three checks degrade silently in that tree rather than failing: the English lint reports 'SKIP no tracked text files yet' because git ls-files returns nothing; the 'kernel reaches main only through' check reports 'SKIP no main branch'; and the panel-leak check enumerates no branches, examines nothing, and reaches its PASS. In my bare extraction of c8c5250 the suite printed 'constitution: 8 passed, 4 pending, 2 skipped'. In a private clone of the same commit WITH history it printed 'constitution: 10 passed, 4 pending', and the English lint flagged 9 files for judgement. Same tree, two reports, and the weaker one is the one the mandated protocol produces. I re-ran the three git-dependent checks in the clone and settled invariant 10 by hand from the added lines, so nothing in this verdict rests on the degraded run. Remedy, in the tooling rather than the protocol: each of the three should report PENDING with 'no git history in this tree' rather than SKIP or a PASS, since a check that cannot see its subject has not checked it. Remedy in the protocol: the brief should say `git clone --no-hardlinks` to a private path, which costs nothing here and keeps the same isolation.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the fail-open class the brief warns about wearing different clothes — not everything PENDING at exit 0, but three checks reporting SKIP and PASS on a tree they cannot read, in the exact tree-acquisition method every judge is instructed to use. Every verdict written from a bare extraction has therefore been written against a suite reporting two fewer checks than it appears to, and nothing in the output says so. It is not this contribution's defect and cannot block it; it is a defect in what judges this contribution and the ones after it.

findings.issue:
A numeric guard that throws instead of comparing, in the block whose own comment says an unread exemption is how every fail-open there began. `_mentions=$(grep -c . "$_leak_mentions" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` produces the two-line string '0
0' when the mentions file exists and is empty, because grep -c prints 0 AND exits 1, so the `|| echo 0` fires as well. The next line, `[ "${_mentions:-0}" -gt 0 ]`, then errors — I observed `ci/constitution-check.sh: line 620: [: 0
0: integer expected` in my bare-extraction run — and the check went on to print PASS. The consequence is confined: in the zero case there is nothing to report anyway, and with one or more exemptions grep -c exits 0 and the arithmetic works. But the diagnostic path is suppressed by a thrown comparison rather than by a decision, and it is the one output in this file the comment above it says must never be shortened. Two-line remedy: `_mentions=$(grep -c . "$f" 2>/dev/null || true); _mentions=${_mentions%%$'
'*}; _mentions=${_mentions:-0}`. Not in this contribution's diff.
findings.why_it_matters: A guard that raises an error and is stepped over is indistinguishable in the transcript from a guard that evaluated false, and this one sits immediately before the code that prints what the check chose not to look at. The zero case is harmless today only because the file happened to be empty; the same construction would swallow a real count the moment grep's exit status and its stdout disagree for any other reason.

findings.issue: The record has no field for the thing this contribution's evidence depends on, and two fields it does have are empty. `prompt_hash = ""` and `signature = ""`, which invariant 3's text names explicitly among what every line must be traceable to; both are empty on C-0027 and C-0035 as well, so this is a standing gap in the schema and its population rather than anything this submission did. The gap that bites here is different: the record carries no toolchain identity at all, and every size figure in this contribution was taken on a toolchain the submission provisioned itself. Three fields would close it and each is one line — the compiler (`rustc --version` gives `rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14) (Fedora 1.97.1-1.fc44)` on the sysroot I used), the linker (ld.lld 22), and the sha256 of the flat image the figures describe. The image hash is the cheapest and the strongest: it makes any later party's build either match or not, and it converts 'I rebuilt the toolchain and it reproduces the baseline' from a claim into something checkable by anyone with the commit.
findings.why_it_matters: Total provenance is enforced now and is the invariant that makes every other measurement in this repository mean something. A size regression, a boot verdict and a budget percentage are all statements about an artefact, and an artefact is only identified by the toolchain that built it plus its own digest. Without either recorded, a future disagreement about 7,288 bytes has nothing to adjudicate against, and the fact that this particular submission's numbers happen to reproduce is luck the record does not capture.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
Approve. No blocking finding, and I looked for one in the four places the constitution puts weight.

FIRST, MY INSTRUMENT, because the brief is right that it has been the cause every time. `./ci/build.sh` prints `PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel` before any other number in this verdict was taken. Every figure below names the command that produced it. I worked in `git archive c8c5250 | tar -x -C $(mktemp -d)` outside the shared scratchpad, with the crate's own target directory rather than an override — CARGO_TARGET_DIR moved the artefact out from under ci/build.sh, which then correctly FAILed rather than passing on nothing, and I mention it only because it is the one place a silent green was available and the script refused it. I extracted c8c5250 twice and built independently: 7,288 bytes and sha256 8c7fa944adf9aec9d26316722661a4d16b595b8fb4f973f49430f5174ccbe270 both times. My tree did not shift under me. But my SUITE did behave differently depending on how the tree was obtained, and that is the third note: a bare extraction has no .git, and the English lint, the merge-path check and the panel-leak check all degrade to SKIP or an examined-nothing PASS in it — 8 passed / 2 skipped in the extraction against 10 passed / 0 skipped in a private clone of the identical commit. I re-ran those three with history present and settled invariant 10 by hand, so nothing here rests on the degraded run.

INVARIANT 6, THE HAL BOUNDARY, which is where the brief expects the weight and where I agree it sits. Both changed source files are under arch/aarch64/; the diff against hal.rs, main.rs, panic.rs, platform.rs, Cargo.toml, build.rs, ci/ and rfcs/ is empty. boot_rust's signature is not in a portable file and is referenced by nothing outside boot.rs — `grep -rn dtb kernel/src/` returns two lines and both are in it. The decision that actually holds the boundary is the type: u64 and not a pointer means no address enters Rust's type system, and therefore the big-endian FDT header's layout never needs a portable home. A pointer would have imported the pointee's shape into whatever file eventually described it. The 64-byte header and the new output section are both in aarch64 files, one of them a linker script the grep cannot read and whose header already concedes the point. The residue the second port inherits is 'the boot protocol's argument arrives as a scalar parameter of the arch entry function', which is the portable generalisation, not the aarch64 one.

INVARIANT 7. I attacked the strengthened check rather than reading it, eight probes on a scratch copy. A cfg(test) dev-dependencies table FAILs. A workspace.dependencies table nested at depth FAILs. An unparseable manifest FAILs. A deleted lock FAILs. An extra package in the lock FAILs. python3 shimmed to exit 127 FAILs, and tomllib shadowed to raise ImportError FAILs. All three recorded fail-opens are closed and both absence-as-compliance paths with them. The one gap is the one reserved for me: a file with a foreign copyright header and 'adapted from the spin crate' passed. So I checked vendoring by hand and there is none — the header layout is a wire format from a specification, the encoding is demonstrably not Linux's macros, the single mention of Linux is of technique, and there is no copyright, licence or derived-from line anywhere in the 122 added lines.

INVARIANTS 2 AND 5, AND WHETHER THE VALUE IS REALLY DROPPED. The brief is right that a value carried and discarded is a different thing from one stored, and that the source cannot settle it — an underscore is a binding, not a proof. I settled it in the disassembly. boot_rust is two instructions, and the first thing kernel_main does with x0 is overwrite it with the PSCI SYSTEM_OFF function ID. The inbound pointer is dead before anything reads it: not dereferenced, not stored, not compared, not forwarded, not observable. Nothing outward is added either — the whole addition is one branch and sixty bytes of constants executed once.

INVARIANT 1, FOR WHOEVER READS THIS AT M4. The address arrives as a parameter of the single entry function, handed over, with exactly one handoff point. That is the shape a capability fits into, and it is the shape RFC-0003 chose deliberately when it refused a DTB_BASE constant. I confirmed no constant could stand in even if someone wanted one: from one binary, x0 is 0x44000000 at 128M and 0x40400000 at 8M, with 0xd00dfeed at both. The thing that would break M4 is not in this patch; it is T-0011 choosing a `static DTB` or a global accessor, and this contribution has kept the alternative open by storing nothing.

THE SELF-PROVISIONED TOOLCHAIN. My ruling is that the measurement is adequately evidenced, but not by the disclosure — by reproduction, which I performed rather than accepted. I built e058268 and main 9ebb637 in my own extractions: both give 5,344 bytes at sha256 d05e66a0b7da3d5a9ef13da5d5e56c78917c344f2bdee642a775220a9b313396, so the baseline claim holds. Two independent extractions of c8c5250 give 7,288 at one hash, so the branch figure is deterministic. And the 1,944-byte delta is derivable from the section table alone — 0x800 minus 0xa8 is 1,880 of fill, plus 64 of header — which no toolchain can influence. WHAT I CANNOT CLAIM IS INDEPENDENCE, and this is the honest limit. env.sh points RUSTFLAGS at a sysroot in the SHARED scratchpad, and that sysroot still contains two hashes of every rlib at the moment I measured: libcore-8b6b49f34ef49eba beside libcore-f5df3875eb172b15, liballoc-1cf7be75906f3df1 beside liballoc-9ddc225033505d1c, the same for compiler_builtins. The condition the submission described is live, not fixed, and if the rebuild went into that shared directory then my reproduction used the very toolchain it is supposed to be checking. So what I have is determinism across four builds on one toolchain, plus one figure that is toolchain-independent by construction — not a second opinion. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT ADEQUATE, generally and not just here: the contribution record should carry the compiler version, the linker, and above all the sha256 of the artefact the figures describe. The digest is the cheap half and it does all the work, because it makes any later build either match or not. That is the fifth note; it is a gap in the record's schema rather than in this submission's candour, and the disclosure was volunteered and, so far as the tree can settle it, accurate.

THE FLAGS DEVIATION. The RFC's gloss is wrong: bits 1-2 are the page size, zero means unspecified, and one means 4 KiB — so `.quad 0` does not encode 4 KiB pages as RFC-0003 section 1 line 127 says it does. rfcs/0003 owes the correction, not this contribution and not this branch. The submission was right on both counts: right to write the accurate gloss in boot.rs, and right not to amend, because the task's scope clause places rfcs/ outside it and its release clause triggers only if the layout fails to boot, which it does not. The value is also the truthful one for a kernel with no MMU. I record it as a provenance note rather than a style one for the reason the brief gives — an RFC is cited as authority by the task implementing it, and this line was, so a submission can satisfy the criterion, satisfy the RFC, and still ship a field whose documented meaning is false.

WHAT I DID NOT BLOCK ON. One sentence of the head commit message is arithmetically false in both halves — the shift is 2,048 for the sections above .vectors and 1,944 for those above .text, and one of the 'unmoved' distances moved from 4 bytes to 12. It is a minor and not more, for three reasons I can state precisely: the conclusions it argues for are true and I verified each by another route (the relative order of all nine sections is identical, all eighteen ASSERTs link, and the new position ASSERT is load-bearing — inserting an allocated section before .text.boot fires it with the right message, and neutralising it lets the same broken tree build green, so nothing else catches that defect); the refuting numbers are in the paragraph immediately below the sentence, which makes it self-refuting rather than concealing; and the remedy is a deletion, not a measurement.

A PROCESS FINDING ABOUT THE BRIEF, which belongs on the record with the rest. I was given main at 9ebb637 as the baseline, but the branch is based at e058268 — two ledger-only commits behind it. `git diff 9ebb637 c8c5250` therefore shows TWO LEDGER LINES REMOVED, which reads exactly like the append-only violation invariant 3 calls unrecoverable, and is not one. The branch's real diff, `git diff $(git merge-base main c8c5250) c8c5250`, is three files, 122 insertions, 16 deletions, and does not touch .provenance/ at all. I nearly reported a blocking finding on a git artefact. A brief that names a baseline the branch is not based on manufactures the appearance of the gravest defect in the constitution, and the next brief should give the merge base or say plainly that main has moved.

findings.issue: `_start` preserving `x0` is the whole deliverable and nothing enforces it. The doc claims "`_start` touches only `x9`-`x12` and ends in a tail branch", and I confirmed that is exactly true of the emitted code -- `objdump -d --section=.text.boot` over the 26 instructions from 0x40080040 to 0x400800a4 shows writes to x9, x10, x11, x12 and sp and to no other register, and 0x4008009c is `b boot_rust`, not `bl`, so x30 is untouched too. But it is true by inspection only. No ASSERT, no lint and no test covers it, and by this task's own design nothing may read the value, so a future `adr x0, ...` or a `bl` inserted into `_start` would silently replace the blob address with garbage and every check in the gate would stay green.
findings.why_it_matters: The failure is latent and then sudden. Today `_dtb` is a `u64` that is dropped, so a clobbered `x0` is not memory-unsafe -- it is merely a wrong number nobody looks at. The moment T-0011 gives it a reader, that same wrong number becomes a pointer the kernel follows, and the regression that introduced it will be several contributions in the past with a green gate over it. The only artefact that currently proves the register discipline is a gdb session a human runs by hand. This is the assumption in the patch that is true now and guaranteed by nothing.

findings.issue: `ASSERT(ADDR(.text.boot) == KERNEL_BASE, "_start is not at KERNEL_BASE: ...")` pins the OUTPUT SECTION's address; its message names `_start`. The two coincide because boot.rs is the sole contributor of a `.text.boot` input section, and the comment above the section -- "`_start`, and nothing else" -- is the real invariant. I TRIED TWICE TO PRODUCE THE ESCAPE AND FAILED. Adding a second `#[unsafe(link_section = ".text.boot")]` naked function, once defined after `_start` and once defined before it, links clean both times with `_start` still at 0x40080000, the squatter at 0x400800a8, and `41 52 4d 64` still at flat-image byte 56. LLVM and lld kept the entry symbol first in the output section in both orderings, so the header was never displaced and I am reporting a gap in what is ENFORCED, not a defect I could exercise.
findings.why_it_matters: Downgraded to a note precisely because I could not break it. What holds `_start` at offset 0 today is a toolchain ordering behaviour, not the script: the assertion would be equally green if that behaviour changed, since it only ever looks at the section. The consequence would be invisible to everything currently running -- the ELF boot follows `e_entry` wherever the symbol goes, and ci/ does not yet boot the flat image, so nothing in the gate reads byte 56. An `ASSERT(_start == KERNEL_BASE, ...)` costs one line and would move the guarantee from the linker's discretion into the file, which is what the existing message already promises a reader.

findings.issue: `flags = 0` leaves bits 1-2 (kernel page size) as "unspecified" where Linux's own head.S writes 1 for 4 KiB. The submission discloses this and does not fix it. I agree with the deferral, and the reason is stronger than the one given: bits 1-2 tell a bootloader what granule to place the image for, and this kernel runs with SCTLR_EL1.M clear -- I read the value written at 0x4008007c-0x40080084, `mov x9, #0x800` / `movk x9, #0x30d0, lsl #16` = 0x30d00800, bit 0 clear -- so it has no page size to declare. Bit 0 (endianness, little) and bit 3 (placement at text_offset from usable RAM) are the two bits that carry meaning here and both are correctly zero.
findings.why_it_matters: It is correct now and becomes wrong at exactly one moment: when the MMU lands and the kernel commits to a granule. Recording it so that whoever enables the MMU knows this word is theirs to update, rather than discovering it from a bootloader that placed the image on the wrong boundary. A field that says "unspecified" about a property you do not have is honest; the same field left unchanged after you acquire the property is a lie the loader believes.

findings.issue: `evidence/` is empty and `prompt_hash` and `signature` in contribution.toml are both the empty string. Every figure the submission asserts is therefore unattested inside the record, and I reproduced all of them from the branch head rather than checking them against anything.
findings.why_it_matters: It changes nothing about this patch, which I could measure end to end. It matters for the next reader of this record, who will find a verdict citing numbers and no artefact behind them but this file. Noting it so the absence is on the record rather than inferred from silence.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
Verified by building, booting and breaking the tree at c8c5250, in a private extraction (`git archive c8c5250 | tar -x`) with its own build tree, never in the shared worktree. `./ci/build.sh` printed `PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel` -- I checked that before trusting any figure, and no check in this review reported PENDING. My tree did not shift: the flat image hashed identically (sha256 8c7fa944adf9aec9d26316722661a4d16b595b8fb4f973f49430f5174ccbe270) at every point I re-derived it, and all probe edits were made in a separate copy so the measurement tree was never written to. One instrument note against myself: my first build attempt set CARGO_TARGET_DIR and ci/build.sh reported `FAIL cargo reported success but ... does not exist` -- it is hard-wired to kernel/target. It failed loudly rather than measuring nothing, which is the right behaviour, and every number below comes from the in-tree build that printed PASS.

NO UNSAFE BLOCK IS ADDED. The patch adds no `unsafe {}` and no `// SAFETY:` comment, so there is none of mine to audit for a restated-code argument. What it adds is three declaration-level obligations -- `#[unsafe(naked)]` data inside an executable function, `#[unsafe(link_section = ".text.boot")]`, and one new parameter on `unsafe extern "C" fn boot_rust` -- and the soundness question for all three is whether the machine does what the comments say. It does.

THE HEADER IS NOT EXECUTED, AND I CHECKED THE INSTRUCTION AND NOT THE COMMENT. Sixty-four bytes of data sit at the entry point of a function the ELF loader jumps to. `objdump -d --section=.text.boot`: 40080000 `14000010  b 40080040 <_start+0x40>`. 0x40 is the first byte past the header, so both boot routes -- ELF via e_entry, flat via offset 0 -- enter at the branch and step over the data. `hexdump -C -n 64` on the objcopy output: code0 `10 00 00 14`, code1 zero, text_offset 0x80000, image_size 0x11c80, flags/res2/res3/res4 all zero across bytes 24-55, `41 52 4d 64` at 56, res5 zero. `nm` gives `__image_size = 0x11c80` and `__kernel_end = 0x40091c80`; 0x40091c80 - 0x40080000 = 0x11c80, so the field is the subtraction it claims to be and is non-zero, which is the condition under which the loader honours text_offset at all. `_start` is at 0x40080000 in `nm`. Flat image 7,288 bytes.

X0 REACHES RUST UNREAD. Full disassembly of `.text.boot`: writes go to x9, x10, x11, x12 and sp and nowhere else; the exit at 0x4008009c is `b boot_rust`, a tail branch, so x0 and x30 are both as the loader left them and AAPCS64 delivers x0 as `boot_rust`'s first parameter. `boot_rust` has exactly one referent in the image, that branch. The parameter is `u64` and not a pointer, and it is bound to `_dtb` and dropped -- I found no dereference, no store, no comparison and no onward pass, and no `#[allow]` anywhere in the diff. That it is unenforced is my one major finding, not a defect in what is written.

BOTH BOOTS, ONE FILE. As an ELF through ci/boot-test.sh: 5 passed -- marker, no panic, no fault, no fault inside the failure path, clean PSCI exit 0. As a flat image, the objcopy of that same ELF, sha256 8c7fa944...: `-M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -display none -serial stdio -no-reboot -nic none -kernel <bin>` printed SKYNET_BOOT_OK and exited 0 at -m 128M and at -m 8M. At -m 2M QEMU refuses with 'Not enough space for DTB after kernel/initrd', which is the documented 4 MiB floor of the Image route and not a property of this patch. Under gdb at `break *0x40080000`, before the branch executes: at 128M x0 = 0x44000000, at 8M x0 = 0x40400000, x1/x2/x3 zero in both, and `x/4xb $x0` reads `d0 0d fe ed` at both addresses. Two addresses from one binary, which is the fact that forbids writing a constant down.

THE MARGINS T-0005 BOUGHT: ORDERING INTACT, TWO DISTANCES 96 BYTES SHORTER. Measured on both trees -- the branch at c8c5250, and main at 9ebb637, which is the baseline I was given. main has moved since (two further tasks merged while I measured), so every "baseline" figure below means 9ebb637 specifically and not whatever main holds when this is read. Stack floor is `__stack_top - STACK_SIZE`. Baseline: floor 0x400814e0; `hvc` at 0x40080810 (objdump -d --section=.failpath) -> 3,280; vector entry 4 at ADDR(.vectors)+0x200 = 0x40080200 -> 4,832; last word of .text at 0x400814dc, the `bl fault_stop` -> 4. Branch: floor 0x40081c80; `hvc` at 0x40081010 -> 3,184; entry 4 at 0x40080a00 -> 4,736; last word at 0x40081c74, still `bl fault_stop` -> 12. Every one of the three reported figures is exact. The reason two shrank is arithmetic and not a layout error: the whole chain rose 2,048 bytes while the stack floor rose only 1,952, because .text is 104 bytes shorter once `_start` leaves it and the header's 64 come back. The +8 on the .text distance is `.got` at 0x40081c78 needing 16-byte alignment for `.stack`. So the ordering T-0005 bought survives intact -- .vectors 2 KiB aligned at 0x40080800, then .guard, .failpath, .rodata, .text, .got, .bss, .stack, with every one of its ordering ASSERTs still in the file and green -- and the DISTANCES lost 3% on two of three. That is a real cost, it was disclosed rather than found, and it does not reverse anything.

THE ARITHMETIC, AND WHETHER THE FILL IS AVOIDABLE. 5,344 -> 7,288 is +1,944. It decomposes exactly: `.text.boot` is 0xa8 = 168 bytes at KERNEL_BASE, `.vectors` is pinned to the next 2 KiB boundary, so the gap is 2048 - 168 = 1,880, and .text carries the header's 64 -- 1,880 + 64 = 1,944. MY JUDGEMENT: the fill is forced, not an artefact of the resolution, and the chosen resolution is the cheapest of the two available. The gap exists because `ASSERT((ADDR(.vectors) & 2047) == 0)` is a hardware requirement -- VBAR_EL1[10:0] are RES0 -- and because `.vectors` must be the lowest of the failure-path chain. Any resolution paying the header into offset 0 pays 2048 minus whatever it places below `.vectors`. This one places all 168 bytes of `_start` there and pays 1,880. RFC-0004's separate `.head`, which the task forbade here, would place only the 64-byte header and pay 1,984 -- 104 bytes MORE. I derived that second figure arithmetically from the measured section sizes rather than by building it, and flag it as such; the 1,880 is measured. Nothing else may be placed in the gap without landing below `.vectors`, and I confirmed the three ordering ASSERTs that would refuse it are present.

WHAT I BROKE. The two new assertions are claimed to bite three ways and they do, each time with the message the file wrote for it. (1) Displacing the section -- a `. += 8;` after `. = KERNEL_BASE;` -- fails the link with `_start is not at KERNEL_BASE: the image header is not at offset 0 of the flat image and the loader will reject or mis-place the kernel`, and with that message ALONE. (2) Emptying the section, by dropping the `#[unsafe(link_section)]` attribute from `_start` so nothing feeds it, fails with `the boot section is smaller than the image header it must contain`, and with that message ALONE -- `ADDR` of the now-empty output section is still KERNEL_BASE and the position assert stays green. This is the test that matters, because it is the one that decides whether the pair is two assertions or one with extra words: it is two, and the size assert is the only thing standing between a green link and an image whose first bytes are `.vectors`. (3) Deleting the output section outright fails BOTH, plus an `undefined section .text.boot` diagnostic. Three for three.

AND NEITHER IS OF THE DEGENERATE SHAPE. The standing objection is that an assertion in this file can reduce to a tautology -- `ASSERT(ADDR(.text) < ADDR(.got))` cannot fail while `.text` is non-empty. Neither new assertion has that shape, and I did not take that from reading them: an equality against a link-time constant has no non-empty-section reading that satisfies it automatically, and break (1) is the demonstration -- an eight-byte displacement leaves both sections non-empty, leaves every ordering in the file intact, and still fires. `SIZEOF >= 64` is a size floor with an independent witness in break (2). The pair holds a POSITION and a SIZE, which is what the comment beside them claims and what no other assertion in the file does. My caveat is the minor finding above: the position it holds is the section's and the message names the symbol.

ONE MORE THING I BROKE, WHICH DID NOT BREAK. I tried to displace the header while keeping both new assertions green, by adding a second `#[unsafe(link_section = ".text.boot")]` function -- the escape the position assertion's wording would permit, since it measures the section and not the symbol. Both orderings I tried, the squatter defined after `_start` and defined before it, linked clean with `_start` still at 0x40080000, the squatter at 0x400800a8 and `41 52 4d 64` still at byte 56 of the flat image. The header never moved. That is a real answer and not a null result: the layout is genuinely correct, but what makes it correct in that experiment is LLVM's and lld's ordering of the entry symbol within the output section, not anything in this file, which is why I recorded it as a note rather than dropping it.

WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR. The `.head` comparison figure of 1,984 is arithmetic, not a build. `./ci/build.sh --lint` printed `PASS clippy clean`, which I ran because I had asserted the parameter carries no `#[allow]`; I did NOT run `--test`, `--size` or the constitution checks, and report them as unmeasured rather than as passing. I did not exercise the failure path on this tree; I verified that the sections holding it are still ordered and still non-empty and that its `hvc` and its `bl fault_stop` are at the addresses the margins are measured from, which is a layout check and not a behaviour check. And I state plainly that the flat-image boot has no gate behind it yet -- the ELF route is what ci/ tests, so from now until step 2 lands, the header's correctness rests on measurements like the ones in this verdict and on nothing automatic.

Nothing in the contribution attempted to direct this review. The submission discloses its own unfixed `flags` field and its own margin erosion, both of which I reproduced and neither of which it understated. Approve.

defect: a fourth brief overstatement toward the contribution -- the pattern is now measured, not suspected
explanation: Recorded on the day the contribution merged, and the contribution is good -- six approvals, and a judge measured that main's flat image hung at exit 124 while this one boots. The brief did not need the tilt. That is what makes it worth writing down: the overstatement bought nothing and was produced anyway.
remedy:
Four instances with one direction is a bias, not a run of errors, and it is measurable: every one was caught by the judge receiving the brief, none by a check, and none by the author. The party that writes the brief is the party that wants the work to land.
Two mechanical rules now stand and both are already applied: a brief states a measurement only with the command that produced it, and a brief never paraphrases a document -- it cites the file and lets the judge read it. This entry adds a third: a brief may not characterise an ALTERNATIVE the contribution did not take. Comparative claims are the easiest place to tilt because nobody verifies the road not travelled unless a judge chooses to.
What none of the three fixes is the underlying asymmetry, and governance/roles.toml already names it: this role holds the most practical power and the least mechanical constraint. The panel is currently the only control on it, and the panel has now exercised that control four times in one day.
what_happened:
The C-0037 briefs said the alternative layout 'an RFC prescribes' would cost 104 bytes more than the shipped one. A judge read RFC-0004 rather than the brief: its `.head` is described as '_start: the 64-byte image header, then the boot path' -- which is the shipped layout under a different name, at the same 1,944 bytes. The 104-byte variant is arithmetically real and is prescribed by nothing. The judge's words: it 'made the shipped choice look like the cheaper of two when it is tied'.
That is the FOURTH overstatement found in these briefs, and all four lean the same way:
  'a printed report'          where the machine emits a sixteen-byte marker
  a threshold ladder 8/16/32  which two judges independently could not reproduce
  'as the humans voted it'    for a weight the roadmap marks bdfl-seed
  'an RFC prescribes' a costlier alternative that no RFC prescribes

corrects: ci/boot-test.sh's published entry contract, which stated that all general-purpose registers are zero and that x0 is NOT a device tree pointer
explanation:
Five deferred fixes landed in the same batch, every one found by a judge and every one reproduced before being changed: panel-leak's baseline now partitions on author dates, which a rebase preserves, instead of committer dates, which it rewrites; host unit tests no longer require the bare-metal target they never use; the exemption counter no longer builds a non-integer from `grep -c || echo 0`; no-kernel-deps' pass line states its scope instead of claiming an empty tree it cannot see into; and a run that measures nothing now exits 3 rather than 0.

Every fix carries a negative test showing the check fails on the broken input and passes on the good one. That is the standing answer to the five fail-opens recorded in these files, whose common cause was that a PASS had never been treated as a claim needing evidence.
what_happened:
The contract was true of an ELF and false of the artefact the gate now boots. RFC-0003 section 8 assigned four ci/ changes to this role and named this as the one that must not be skipped: 'a contract that is false is worse than one that is silent'.
Rewritten from measurement rather than from the RFC. Halted at *0x40080000 before the first instruction, one binary, twelve RAM sizes: 4M->0x40200000, 6M and 8M->0x40400000, 16M->0x40800000, 32M->0x41000000, 64M->0x42000000, 100M->0x43200000, 128M->0x44000000, 200M->0x46400000, and 512M/1G/3G all->0x48000000. x1-x3 and sp zero at every size; the word at x0 is d00dfeed with totalsize 0x100000. That is ram_base + min(ram_size/2, 128 MiB) rounded up to 2 MiB, with a cap. At -m 2M QEMU refuses outright: 'Not enough space for DTB', exit 1.
Also landed: the flat image is produced by the build rather than as a side effect of --size, with kernel_image() beside kernel_binary() and a staleness check so an image older than its ELF is refused rather than measured; run_boot takes the Image and run_gdb keeps the ELF; and RFC-0001 O-2 is closed where it was cited.

Recording it so that it is re-examined when the MMU lands, rather than inherited silently.
