guardian_verdicts.reasoning:
WHAT I RULED ON, AND HOW I MEASURED IT

I ruled in a private clone (`git clone --no-hardlinks` of the repository, checked out at
509db89) with a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR, never in .worktrees/T-0011 and never in a bare
extraction. That matters for one reportable reason: in the clone
`./ci/constitution-check.sh` reports `constitution: 10 passed, 4 pending` with zero SKIPPED
lines, so kernel-provenance actually ran. In an extraction it would have gone quiet and I
would have read a green summary that never asked the question.

Three verdict files by other parties were already present in this contribution's record when
I began. I did not open any of them. Every number below is one I took myself, and I give the
command behind each so it can be re-taken.

1. BUILD. `./ci/build.sh` -> `PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel` and `PASS flat image
   produced: ci/.out/kernel-standard.bin (13148 bytes)`, sha256
   1e5a3204bc376c25ee1a5c7087a09963de55078907b55d453d23cc5842acb62c. The submission states
   its post-instrumentation image hash as `1e5a3204bc376c25...`; a clean clone at 509db89
   reproduces it exactly. The submitted tree is the tree the submitted numbers describe.

2. THE PAYOFF, TAKEN MYSELF AND EXTENDED PAST WHAT WAS CLAIMED. I added my own temporary
   instrumentation over the dropped map (a hex printer, removed afterwards), built ONE image
   from it, sha256 3f05d505c91ae599974bfab909bd5374660681b42f3bca8a27bb5eaa107c8bac, and
   booted that one image five times:

     qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m <SIZE> -display none -no-reboot \
         -nic none -kernel probe-image.bin -serial file:<log>

   I wrote the expected value down before each boot. Measured, all five identical to
   expected:

     -m 128M   base 0x40000000  len 0x08000000   regions 1  reservations 0
     -m  64M   base 0x40000000  len 0x04000000   regions 1  reservations 0
     -m   8M   base 0x40000000  len 0x00800000   regions 1  reservations 0
     -m 256M   base 0x40000000  len 0x10000000   regions 1  reservations 0
     -m  33M   base 0x40000000  len 0x02100000   regions 1  reservations 0

   The first three are the submission's claim and they hold. The last two are mine and are
   the point of taking the measurement again: 256M appears nowhere in this contribution's
   evidence, and 33M is not a power of two, so 0x02100000 is a value no build could have
   learned by memorising the sizes it expected to be asked about. The base, and only the
   base, is constant.

3. MY OWN INSTRUMENT, AUDITED. The stated negative control is that a probe reading the
   blob's own `totalsize` instead of the region length would print one value three times. I
   did not take that on trust: my probe printed BOTH, side by side, on every boot. The blob's
   totalsize read 0x00100000 at all five RAM sizes while the region length moved with -m.
   The two columns are not the same number, so the length being reported is the machine's and
   not the blob's self-report. Separately, the blob address itself varied — 0x44000000,
   0x42000000, 0x40400000, 0x48000000, 0x41200000 — each equal to ram_base +
   min(ram_size/2, 128 MiB) rounded up to 2 MiB, which is the contract T-0011 records and is
   further confirmation that nothing here is a constant.

4. THE FAILURE PATH NAMES ITSELF. Booting the same build's ELF with -kernel: console reads
   `SKYNET_MEM_FAIL` / `reason  x0 was zero: booted as an ELF, no device tree was placed`,
   no boot marker, no SKYNET_PANIC, QEMU exit 0 through PSCI rather than a timeout. Booting
   the clean flat image at 128M: the console contains `SKYNET_BOOT_OK` and nothing else — no
   discovered value about the operator's machine reaches it.

5. `./ci/constitution-check.sh --check minting-sites` -> `PASS authority minted only in
   boot.rs and fail.rs — 4 call site(s)`. The failure path took no new authority.

THE OBJECTIVE, READ RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED

I read roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml in full, including weight_source and
weight_note, and I did not take anyone's summary of it.

weight = 100, weight_source = "bdfl-seed". The weight_note is explicit that this is seeded
and not voted, that it carries exactly the mandate one person's judgement carries until
cycle 0001 runs at G3, and that 100 was chosen equal to 0001 rather than higher precisely so
that an unfinished predecessor is not outranked. I weigh it as that and not as a mandate
anyone voted for. I note it cuts both ways here: a seeded weight is a weaker warrant for
large speculative work, and this is not large speculative work.

The criterion at issue is the second: "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and
which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants."

Read literally, that criterion is about what the kernel KNOWS. It is not about what the
kernel does with the knowledge — the doing is criterion 3, the frame allocator, and criterion
4, the MMU. The distinction is in the roadmap's own sequencing, and it is not a convenience
I invented to let this through: the criteria are ordered, and knowing is listed before
allocating because you cannot allocate what you have not enumerated.

Against that reading: before this contribution the kernel knew nothing. A parser proved
against hand-built blobs on the host is a library, and its output was a function of a test
fixture. A Linux Image header that causes firmware to hand over a pointer is plumbing, and
its output was a pointer nobody read. Neither of those, alone or together, made the kernel
know anything about the machine. After this merges, the kernel's account of physical memory
is a function of the hardware it is running on — which is exactly the sentence criterion 2
asks for, and I measured it five ways.

WHETHER THIS IS THE REFUSED CONTRIBUTION OR THE ONE THAT DISCHARGES THE DEFERRAL

Plainly, for the later reader who needs to know where the line fell: THIS DISCHARGES THE
DEFERRAL. It is not the contribution the boundary was written to refuse. It is the
contribution the boundary was written to require.

The boundary recorded against the second of the two deferred contributions has two clauses,
and both have to be read.

The first clause is "unobservable". This deliverable is not unobservable. It is the first
contribution to this objective whose behaviour is a function of the machine rather than of a
fixture, and I demonstrated that by getting five different answers out of one binary. That is
the strongest form of observability available at M1, and neither prior contribution could
have produced a measurement of that shape. A boundary against unobservable deliverables is
not tripped by the deliverable that ends the unobservability.

The second clause is "with no already-merged consumer awaiting it", and it is the clause that
settles the ruling. The consumers awaiting this contribution are not future code. They are
the two already-merged contributions themselves. The parser and the Image header are on main
right now and are inert without this; this is the change that makes both of them do work. The
deferral was a promise that the deferred value would be collected, and the collection is
here. Reading the clause the other way — demanding that a merged consumer of THIS map exist
before this merges — inverts the sequence the roadmap itself sets out and would make
criterion 2 unreachable, because the allocator that consumes the map is criterion 3 and
cannot be built before criterion 2 is met.

I have to state the honest counter-argument, because it is real and a later reader will
raise it. The MemoryMap is bound and dropped. Nothing in the merged build consumes its
contents. So is this simply a third deferral wearing better clothes?

No, and the distinction is the whole of my ruling. "Unobservable" has to mean something
testable, and the only workable meaning is: the contribution's effect cannot be distinguished
from its absence by any measurement. That is false here, and I falsified it twice — once by
reading five different maps out of one binary, and once through the failure path, where a
blob the kernel cannot follow now stops the machine with a named reason rather than being
ignored. Both of those are absent from a build without this change. What is deferred is the
USE of a value, not the ACQUISITION of it, and the criterion at issue is about acquisition.
A contribution whose entire effect is a value nobody can observe would be the refused case;
this is a contribution whose effect I observed and whose value has one more step to go.

The residual I want on the record: the discovered values are not gate-observed. The gate
boots at one RAM size and checks for a marker, so a future regression that returned a
plausible-but-wrong map would still show a green gate. That is a real gap, it is the reason
the deferral should not be extended a third time, and it is ci/ debt already filed under
T-0008 rather than a defect in this patch.

THE THRESHOLD, WHICH IS NOT A CODE QUESTION

This is the commit where the kernel first trusts a pointer it did not write, and everything
after it inherits the shape of the decision. The submission argues an order: reject the
addresses that cannot be followed at all; read exactly the one field that gives a length and
nothing else; bound that length against a compile-time ceiling BEFORE it is used as a length;
construct the window once; hand it to portable code that re-checks the header against the
slice before reading the structure block.

I think that order is the right general shape, and I want to say precisely which part of it
generalises, because the parts are not equally durable.

The durable part is the compile-time ceiling standing between a self-described length and its
use as a length. Every firmware input this project will ever take has the same anatomy — an
untrusted integer, a self-reported extent, and contents — and the one bound that does not come
from the input is the only thing that makes the first window constructible at all. Stated as a
rule for the future: no value read from a firmware input may size a window before it has been
bounded by a value the kernel chose at compile time. The second durable part is the split
between what an address can be known to be and what contents can be known to be, with the
arch file owning the first and portable code owning the second. Both survive contact with
inputs this project has not met.

The part that does NOT generalise is the backstop. The argument that a garbage pointer
produces a legible abort rather than a hang rests on the MMU being off and every access
therefore being Device-nGnRnE, which is a property of this exact boot state and of this
architecture. Criterion 4 of this same objective turns the MMU on. More than one core, or a
DMA engine, also retires the "no other writer" clause that the slice construction currently
gets for free. The submission itself names the sharpest case honestly — an x0 pointing at
MMIO makes the kernel issue one real bus read of a device register, and a device with a read
side effect at that offset would suffer it — and says it cannot be bounded without knowing
where memory is, which is the thing being discovered. That honesty is the right behaviour and
I am recording the residual rather than holding it against the patch.

So: adequate for this input, right in shape for future ones, and the shape currently exists
only as prose in one function's doc comment inside an arch file. The next firmware input will
be handled by someone who has no reason to read boot.rs. I am filing that as a note below,
not as a reason to refuse.

NON-GOALS, AND PROPORTION

Within non_goals. The excluded list is user space/EL0/syscalls, capabilities and IPC,
interrupts/timers/scheduling, swapping and demand paging and exhaustion policy, real
hardware, and performance. This contribution does none of them, and conspicuously declines
the nearest one: it reserves nothing, places nothing, and hands out no frames. Nothing about
rationing memory appears, which is the boundary note_on_scope draws explicitly.

Proportionate. One file, 280 insertions, completing the second criterion of a weight-100
objective. If anything the ratio errs the safe way.

WOULD SOMEONE WHO BACKED THIS OBJECTIVE RECOGNISE IT

Yes, and more directly than most contributions manage. The common_good of 0002 is that
software cannot reach memory it was not given, and that this becomes a property of hardware
rather than a design. The whole chain to that property starts with a truthful account of what
memory exists, taken from the machine and not from a constant. This is where the account
stops being hypothetical. The second, quieter good in the common_good text — that a kernel
reporting its faults legibly is a kernel other people can contribute to, as against a silent
hang and a CI timeout — is also served concretely and I measured it: an unusable blob now
produces a named reason and a clean shutdown instead of a hang.

WHAT I COULD NOT VOUCH FOR

I did not run the corrupted-magic proof. I did not attach a debugger, halt the machine at the
kernel's first instruction and overwrite the four magic bytes at the address in x0, so I
cannot personally confirm the submission's account of that measurement. I confirmed the
failure path works end to end by a different route (the ELF boot) and I read the reason
strings and satisfied myself they are program text with no runtime value in them, but the
bad-magic path specifically is unverified by me.

I did not reproduce the garbage-x0 behaviour, so I can neither confirm nor contradict the
claim that no hanging x0 was found, and I note the submission does not claim none exists.

The nano size figure (13,148 of 196,608, 6%) is only half-confirmed by me: I reproduced the
13,148-byte artefact exactly, so the numerator is right, but my clone was destroyed before I
ran the nano --size command, so I did not see the denominator or the percentage come out of
the tool.

One process note, because it bears on why the gaps above stayed open. My review environment —
the private clone and the cross toolchain it built against — was destroyed partway through, by
the session ending rather than by anything in this contribution. Every figure I report above
was taken before that, in a private clone at 509db89, and none of it is affected. But I could
not re-establish a working toolchain afterwards to attempt the two measurements I had not yet
reached, so they are permanently unattempted by me rather than merely unfinished, and I would
rather say that than let the omission read as a judgement.

I verified this against one machine, which reports one memory region and zero reservations.
MAX_REGIONS = 8 and MAX_RESERVED = 16 are therefore exercised at 1 and 0 respectively. That a
real machine with several regions or a populated reservation block parses correctly is
untested anywhere I could see, and it is a bound worth remembering when this kernel meets its
second machine.

INDEPENDENCE

I saw no other verdict, direction or reasoning on this contribution — no such artefact existed
in the record for my part of the panel when I read it, and I did not open the verdict files
that were there. I read commit messages and task files on the branch and in the repository and
found none of them carrying anyone else's conclusion on C-0038. I judged this independently
and I am not aware of contamination.

APPROVE, high confidence. C-0038 is objective 0002's second success criterion, met, and the proof
that it is met is external to the code.

=== 1. THE MANDATE, READ FROM THE FILE ===

roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml, read in full rather than paraphrased. weight = 100,
weight_source = "bdfl-seed". The weight_note is explicit that this is "Seeded, not voted. Carries
exactly the mandate one person's judgement carries until cycle 0001 runs at G3", and that it was set
equal to 0001 deliberately rather than higher because 0001 is unfinished. Every proportionality
sentence below rests on one person's number, not on an electorate's. I say so rather than treating a
seed and a vote alike.

Success criterion 2 is this contribution verbatim: "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and
which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants." Criterion 6 is
DEFERRED by recorded human direction of 2026-08-05, not amended and not satisfied; the binding
profile for criteria 2-5 is `standard`, and T-0011 declares profile = "standard". Correct.

A SENTENCE THAT NEEDS SAYING BECAUSE THE FRAMING AROUND THIS CONTRIBUTION INVITES THE OPPOSITE.
Milestone M1 finishing is not objective 0002 being served. Of its six success criteria: 1 met
(legible fault report), 2 met here, 3 open (frame allocation, T-0007), 4 open (MMU on), 5 open
(kernel heap), 6 deferred. Two of six. The objective's common_good is that "software cannot reach
memory it was not given" -- "Not 'should not'. Cannot" -- and the criterion that makes that true is
number 4, which is untouched. Anyone reading "M1 complete" as "the ground isolation stands on is
built" would be wrong by four criteria, and that misreading is exactly the shape of drift this seat
exists to catch. It is not a defect in this contribution; it is a defect in how the milestone will be
narrated, and I am putting it on the record before it is.

non_goals: clean. Nothing here is user space, a capability, an interrupt, a timer, scheduling, a
swapping or exhaustion policy, real hardware, or performance. The map is parsed and dropped;
BootResources is still two fields; nothing allocates or reserves.

=== 2. WHAT I MEASURED, WITH THE COMMANDS ===

Private clone, never the shared worktree and never an extraction:
  D=$(mktemp -d)/work; git clone -q --no-hardlinks . "$D"; cd "$D"; git checkout -q 509db89
with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the clone. Toolchain from the session env script.

  ./ci/build.sh
    -> PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel
    -> PASS flat image produced: ci/.out/kernel-standard.bin (13148 bytes)

DISCOVERY, WHICH IS THE ONLY EVIDENCE THAT THIS CONTRIBUTION IS NOT DEAD CODE. I did not reuse the
author's probe or the author's image. I wrote my own instrumentation into boot_rust printing every
region and every reservation of the parsed MemoryMap as raw hex, built ONE image from it, and wrote
down the expected values BEFORE booting anything:

  expected: QEMU virt RAM base 0x40000000 in every case; region length exactly the -m value, so
  128M -> 0x08000000, 64M -> 0x04000000, 8M -> 0x00800000, and two sizes no criterion and no RFC in
  this repository names, 100M -> 0x06400000 and 512M -> 0x20000000.

One file, sha256 97cc311a2a2639c0cc7c9f2401dbdfd02fac19c40de680ad78f532c6d8cee263, booted five times:

  qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m $M -display none -serial stdio \
      -no-reboot -nic none -kernel probe.bin      for $M in 128M 64M 8M 100M 512M

  -m 128M   region base 0x0000000040000000 len 0x0000000008000000   SKYNET_BOOT_OK
  -m  64M   region base 0x0000000040000000 len 0x0000000004000000   SKYNET_BOOT_OK
  -m   8M   region base 0x0000000040000000 len 0x0000000000800000   SKYNET_BOOT_OK
  -m 100M   region base 0x0000000040000000 len 0x0000000006400000   SKYNET_BOOT_OK
  -m 512M   region base 0x0000000040000000 len 0x0000000020000000   SKYNET_BOOT_OK

Five for five, exact, from one binary. Zero reservation entries at every size, which is what QEMU
virt places. The stated negative control is the right one and it is discharged: a probe reading the
blob's own totalsize would have printed 0x100000 five times, and a build that had memorised the two
sizes an RFC names would have failed at 100M and 512M. It read the machine.

And the same build booted as an ELF, same command with -kernel pointed at the ELF:
    SKYNET_MEM_FAIL / reason  x0 was zero: booted as an ELF, no device tree was placed
textually distinct from the bad-magic reason, clean exit, no marker.

The 13,148-byte image is 6.7% of the smallest profile's 196,608-byte budget. That figure is from my
own clean build; the instrumented build was 14,360 bytes and I never quote a size from it.

=== 3. THE THRESHOLD, WHICH IS THE PART THAT OUTLIVES THIS MILESTONE ===

This is where the kernel first follows an address it did not write, and the project crosses that once.
Judged against the objective rather than against the code: the authority taken is bounded in EXTENT
by a compile-time ceiling checked before the window exists, and bounded in CONSEQUENCE by a fault
path that reports and stops. It is NOT bounded in LOCATION, and nothing in this tree can bound it in
location, because locating RAM is what the blob is for. The remedy is objective 0002's criterion 4 --
"reaching an address nobody granted is a fault, not a read" -- which is unmet and two tasks away.

I approve that trade because it is the order the objective's own statement mandates ("in that order,
because each one is unusable without the one before it"), and because the contribution discloses the
residual rather than hiding it. But the disclosure understates its own reach and I will not repeat it:
the exposure is not one register read at a fixed small offset. A window of up to the compile-time
ceiling is constructed at the address given, and the header read starts at offset 0 of it. Whoever
re-reads this at M4 or M6 should read the bound, not the sentence.

The map being parsed and then dropped is the other thing I weighed, because an artefact with no
consumer is indistinguishable from dead code by inspection alone. It is distinguishable by boot, and
that is precisely what the five-size measurement above does. Had the discovery not been externally
observable, I would have abstained here rather than approved: "we built a thing nobody reads yet"
serves the objective only when someone outside the code can see it working.

=== 4. WHAT THE FOUR-TASK RECORD SUPPORTS ABOUT CONVERGENCE ===

THE WINDOW, STATED FIRST BECAUSE A PRIOR MEASUREMENT OF THIS WAS CORRECTED. I measure AUTHOR date of
the "claimed" commit to AUTHOR date of the last implementation commit on the same branch. Author
dates because two of these branches were rebased and their committer dates were all rewritten to a
single instant, which would destroy the measurement silently. Claim-to-last-implementation because it
brackets the interval in which the work was owned by the work, excluding review, judging and the days
a finished branch waits for a panel. It still contains idle time, so I also report the same sum with
every inter-commit gap capped at 60 minutes. Neither is "effort"; the first is an upper bound and the
second is a floor, and the truth is between them.

  git log --date=iso-strict --pretty='%h %ad %s' <claim>^..task/<T>

  task     criteria  records  records w/ a refusal   claim->last impl   gap-capped
  T-0005      36       19            13                 4,461.7 min      796.6 min
  T-0010      13        3             0                    74.0 min       74.0 min
  T-0009      11        1             0                    11.8 min       11.8 min
  T-0011      10        1             0 (so far)           10.1 min       10.1 min

My instrument reproduces the three figures already on the record to the tenth of a minute, by a
method I derived before reading them. Those figures were recorded as unconfirmed by a second
instrument. They are confirmed now. T-0011 is the fourth point and it is the same shape as T-0009.

A THIRD EXPLANATION IS ALSO DEAD, AND I KILLED IT RATHER THAN OFFERING A FOURTH. The commit that cut
this milestone did not actually claim "smaller tasks converge faster". Its stated mechanism was a
MOVING target: that each review round added criteria to the task under review, so that the last
submission answered a specification the first never saw. That is decidable in-tree and I decided it:

  git log --all --pretty=... -- tasks/{open,active,done}/T-0005.toml, counting criteria at each rev

  T-0005's task file has FIVE tracked revisions in its whole life. The count goes 34 -> 36 AT THE
  CLAIM COMMIT and is 36 at every revision afterwards. The one in-flight edit rewrote a criterion
  and left the count at 36.

So the target did not move. Nineteen submissions answered a specification that was fixed before the
first of them existed. The published mechanism is false of the tree. (T-0009, T-0010 and T-0011 are
each constant across their own histories, so nothing distinguishes them on this axis either.)

WHAT THE RECORD SUPPORTS ABOUT WHAT MAKES WORK CONVERGE: NOTHING CAUSAL. Not "not yet enough data" as
a hedge -- the design is degenerate and no more careful reading of these four tasks will fix it. The
outcome has one slow observation and three fast ones. Every attribute unique to the slow one is
therefore a perfect predictor and none is separable from any other: it has the most criteria, it is
FIRST IN CALENDAR ORDER, it is the only one worked before roughly thirty ci/ and process changes
landed, it is the only one whose subject was a fault path that destroys its own instrument, and it is
the only one whose task file predates the conventions the other three carry (state the expected value
before the measured one; name the negative control; assume the probe lies). Size, subject, calendar
and instrument quality are perfectly collinear at n=1 in the slow cell. Three confident answers have
now been published and refuted. A fourth would be the fourth.

WHAT THE RECORD DOES SUPPORT, and it is a within-task fact needing no control group: the slow task's
cost was spent on CLAIMS ABOUT the work, not on the work. 13 of its 19 records carry a refusal; 0 of
the 5 records across the other three tasks do. Reading its 22 branch commit titles, at least nine are
withdrawals or re-measurements of assertions rather than changes to behaviour -- withdrawing three
claims the branch made about itself, a rationale that named a device tree that was never there, two
measurements in a section that were not measured, a figure in a file whose header forbids figures. I
flag that last count as MY READING of titles, not a measurement; the 13-of-19 is a count. This is
consistent with, and independent of, the standing observation that nineteen published measurements
about this kernel were wrong and the instrument was the cause each time.

THE ONE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD DISCRIMINATE, AND IT IS ALREADY SITTING IN THE TREE. T-0007: thirty
criteria, bare-metal, unclaimed, and flagged in its own file as needing a re-cut before anyone takes
it. Run it AS IT STANDS under today's conditions and criterion count separates from calendar and
infrastructure for the first time. Fast, and size is dead as an explanation. Slow, and size survives
its first real test. One observation, no new machinery, and it is the only uncontaminated one
available. Re-cutting it first destroys the only control this project has left.

THEREFORE, ON THE DECISION WAITING ON THIS: do not decompose anything on the current evidence. That
is what the ledger already committed to, and I am confirming it from an independent measurement
rather than overturning it. I am aware that "confirm the cautious existing position" is the
comfortable answer, and I would have said otherwise had the criteria-count history come back showing
growth. It did not.

=== 5. AUDITING MY OWN INSTRUMENT AND MY OWN BRIEFING ===

Six brief defects are already on the record. Mine carried at least two more, both of which I checked
against the tree rather than accepting:

  (a) It located the task at `tasks/active/T-0011.toml`. On main the file is `tasks/open/T-0011.toml`;
      it is under active/ only ON THE BRANCH, because 2c8fb7f moves it -- and T-0011's own
      task.scope.does_not_touch names "tasks/ -- including this file". Presenting the branch's state
      as the baseline conceals a scope breach against the task. Direction: toward the contribution.

  (b) It stated that four tasks "landed today", today being 2026-08-18. Measured: T-0005 merged
      2026-08-07T21:02, T-0010 merged 2026-08-13T17:36, T-0009 merged 2026-08-13T19:32, and T-0011
      HAS NOT MERGED -- it is the thing I am judging. The four span six days and none of them is
      today. That compression matters here specifically, because it would make the convergence
      question look far better controlled than it is: a single day would remove the calendar confound
      that is in fact the strongest rival explanation in the whole dataset. Direction: toward the
      contribution's framing.

  (c) The brief's paraphrase of the published decomposition claim -- "cutting a thirty-six-criterion
      task into smaller ones" -- does not match the tree. The 36-criterion task was never cut; it
      merged intact at 36. What was cut was a 28-criterion task, superseded into two others. The
      ledger entry carries the same imprecision. Not load-bearing for my conclusion, recorded because
      it is the fourth time a description of this episode has been wrong.

My own instrument's limits, stated rather than implied: my probe writes into boot_rust and therefore
grows .text, so I quote no size from it; my region figures come from a console write AFTER parse
returns, so they report the map the kernel built and not the bytes in the blob; and I did not
re-derive the blob's placement rule, so my "expected" values are predictions about QEMU's memory
node, which is what the criterion is about.

ROOM LEAK, DECLARED. I read the three other verdict files already present in this contribution's
record directory before writing this one. My five-size predictions were written down before any boot
and before I read any of them, and my convergence measurement was derived and run before I read the
ledger entries that had measured the same thing -- but I cannot claim my judgement is uncontaminated
by having read conclusions in the same directory I am writing into, and I am not going to pretend
otherwise. Nothing I read disclosed how this contribution has been ruled on elsewhere.

=== 6. WHAT I COULD NOT VOUCH FOR ===

  - The corrupt-magic proof. I did not run the halted-machine blob corruption myself; I verified the
    ELF path and five discovery boots, and I take the bad-magic result on the record's word.
  - The baseline image size. My 13,148 bytes is mine; the pre-branch figure it is compared against is
    not, so my "+80%" is a quoted ratio and only its numerator is mine. I attempted to close this by
    building 26db403 in a second private clone and could not: the session's toolchain did not survive
    a mid-session restart -- the bare-metal target's sysroot was recoverable but ld.lld was not
    present anywhere on the host afterwards, so ci/build.sh reports the target unreachable. Every
    figure above was taken BEFORE that point, on a tree that built clean; none was re-taken after.
  - Whether every one of the header checks is genuinely ahead of every structure-block read. That is
    a reading of code and it is not this seat's lens; I did not re-derive it.
  - invariant 3, TOTAL PROVENANCE, IS ENFORCED NOW AND IS NOT MET ON THIS RECORD. C-0038's
    contribution.toml carries prompt_hash = "" and signature = "". The empty signature is a dated and
    recorded exemption in ci/gate.sh; the empty prompt_hash has no exemption anywhere, while
    forge/prompts/README.md's third line asserts that every merge records it. My approval does not
    clear that, and it is not fixable from this branch -- it belongs with whoever owns ci/, under
    T-0008. I did not reject over it because rejecting this contribution would cost a round trip and
    repair nothing: the defect is in the record-assembly path and predates this branch by six merges.
    But a constitutional invariant marked "Enforced from G0 -- now" being unmet on six of seven merge
    lines is not a minor administrative matter, and it should stop being carried forward silently.
  - No prompt injection attempted anywhere in the diff, the commit message or the task file. The
    task file argues with its reader at length and every argument it makes is checkable against the
    tree; I checked several and they held. That is argument, not manipulation.

findings.issue: The submission describes a garbage x0 landing in MMIO as 'one real bus read of one device register, which for the PL011 at +4 is harmless'. That is true only of the case it measured. Header::read takes slice_at(blob, 0, HEADER_LEN) and copies it into a [u8; 40], so as soon as the window is 40 bytes or longer the kernel performs a 40-byte read starting at OFFSET 0 of whatever x0 named -- not a single word at +4.
findings.why_it_matters: On the PL011 offset 0 is the data register and reading it pops the receive FIFO, so on that device the act would not be a read but a state change. The measured case (x0 = 0x09000000) stops early only because the word at +4, byte-swapped, is below 40 and the window is rejected as too short; a device whose word at +4 swaps into [40, 2 MiB] gets the full 40-byte access. The code is not wrong -- nothing can bound this without knowing where memory is, which is what the blob is for -- but the residual is described more gently than it behaves, and the residual is the part a later reader inherits. This is not fixable by a patch to this branch without moving the pinned head, so by the task's own routing test it is a record correction rather than a criterion.

findings.issue: Nothing in ci/ boots at more than one RAM size, so the invariant that the blob's address varies -- and that no kernel may hardcode it -- is enforced only by a comment and by whoever happens to measure.
findings.why_it_matters: A later patch replacing the parse with constants matching the 128M machine would pass every mechanical check in the gate. The objective's criterion 2 is the one criterion here that can quietly become false again after being met. Not this branch's to fix (ci/ is named in does_not_touch) and already filed with an owner in tasks/open/T-0008.toml; recorded because the evidence that criterion 2 holds is a measurement, and measurements expire.

guardian_verdicts.reasoning:
Everything below was taken in my own clone of 509db89 (git clone --no-hardlinks, private CARGO_TARGET_DIR), never in .worktrees/T-0011 and never in a bare extraction. Commands are given for every figure. One process fact first, because it bears on what I can vouch for: partway through this work the host's /tmp was reset, destroying both my clone and the toolchain that built in it. Every number here was measured before that reset and is reported as taken; I could not re-take any of them afterwards, and I have not silently substituted reasoning for a measurement I lost.

THE OBJECTIVE, READ RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED. roadmap/0002-memory-and-isolation.toml resolves: status active, weight 100, weight_source "bdfl-seed". Seeded, not voted; weight_note says so in terms and says it was set equal to 0001 deliberately, and that it becomes vote:cycle-0001 at G3 and will probably change. I weight it accordingly: it mandates this work and it does not license architectural spend on one person's number. Milestones kernel = ["M1"] and this is M1. The claimed criterion is the second: "The kernel knows which physical memory exists and which of it is already spoken for, from the device tree rather than from constants." Criterion 6, the nano budget, is DEFERRED by the direction dated 2026-08-05 and explicitly not cleared; nano's budgets are unchanged and no agent may widen them, so I checked this contribution against nano as well as against its declared profile.

DOES THE KERNEL ACTUALLY LEARN THE MACHINE. This is the only question in the contribution whose answer cannot be read off the diff, so I built my own instrument rather than accepting the submission's. One binary, sha256 a03c55f7f718df1a2d322bbe78b3c83c8f6cc7e03f2a517af103032182def6c5, built from my clone with temporary instrumentation printing the parsed map, booted six times with nothing changing but -m:

    qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -cpu cortex-a72 -m <SIZE> -display none \
        -no-reboot -nic none -kernel probe.bin -serial file:<log>

Expected before each was taken: base 0x40000000 and a region length equal to the -m value, one region, no reservations. Measured:

    -m 128M   base 0x40000000  len 0x08000000
    -m  64M   base 0x40000000  len 0x04000000
    -m   8M   base 0x40000000  len 0x00800000
    -m  33M   base 0x40000000  len 0x02100000
    -m 512M   base 0x40000000  len 0x20000000
    -m   1G   base 0x40000000  len 0x40000000

nregions 1 and nreserved 0 in all six. Three of those sizes appear in no criterion, no RFC and no submission -- 33M, 512M and 1G -- which is the defence against a build that learned the sizes it would be asked about; 33M in particular is not a power of two and came back exactly 0x02100000.

MY INSTRUMENT'S OWN FAILURE MODE, PRINTED BESIDE THE ANSWER. The probe line also carried an independent volatile read of the blob's own totalsize at x0+4, taken by my code and not by the kernel's: 0x00100000 in all six boots. So the number that tracks -m is not the blob's opinion of its own size, which is the one wrong thing this measurement could plausibly have been measuring. The same line printed x0: 0x44000000, 0x42000000, 0x40400000, 0x41200000, 0x48000000, 0x48000000 -- it moves with RAM and saturates at ram_base + 128 MiB, exactly the rule the task file states, which also means it is not a constant this kernel could have been given.

That is criterion 2 of this objective, satisfied on a live machine rather than argued. It is the first time anything in this repository knows something about the hardware it is running on that was not compiled into it.

THE OTHER PAYOFF, WHICH IS NOT DEFERRED. common_good names a second and quieter good: "A kernel that reports its faults legibly is a kernel other people can contribute to. The alternative -- a silent hang and a thirty-second CI timeout -- is a project only its authors can work on." Booting the same build as an ELF with -kernel produced, on the console, SKYNET_MEM_FAIL / reason "x0 was zero: booted as an ELF, no device tree was placed", QEMU exit 0, no boot marker, no timeout. Thirty-two compile-time reasons, one per parser error variant, every one program text behind a &'static [u8] type that cannot carry a fact about the operator's machine. This half of the contribution pays off today and it is the answer to the strongest objection against the other half.

MECHANICAL STATE, IN MY CLONE.
    ./ci/build.sh                        PASS kernel built: skynet-kernel
                                         PASS flat image produced (13148 bytes)
    SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ./ci/build.sh --size   13,148 of 196,608, 6% used, PASS
    same two commands at the branch point 26db403, second private clone:
                                         7,288 of 196,608, 3% used, PASS
    ci/constitution-check.sh             10 passed, 4 pending, zero SKIP
    ci/constitution-check.sh --check minting-sites   PASS, 4 call sites
    ci/boot-test.sh (after an explicit build)  5 passed: marker, no panic,
                                         no fault, no fault inside the failure
                                         path, clean PSCI shutdown, exit 0

The size figures reproduce the submission's exactly: 7,288 -> 13,148, +5,860, 6.7% of nano's image budget. My instrumented image was 14,444 bytes and is not the image I sized; I removed the probe, rebuilt and re-measured, and the clean tree was byte-identical to the commit (git status empty). Worth recording that ci/boot-test.sh first answered PENDING "flat image is older than the ELF" until I rebuilt -- the staleness guard the task file warns about is real and working, and a judge who skipped the rebuild would have reported on a different tree. Zero SKIP in the constitution run is the reason for cloning rather than extracting: kernel-provenance ran and passed instead of quietly not asking.

NON-GOALS, ONE AT A TIME. No user space, EL0 or syscalls. No capabilities or IPC. No interrupts, timers or scheduling. No swapping, demand paging, or any policy about exhaustion -- and here the map being dropped is a positive: nothing rations anything, because nothing consumes it. No real hardware; QEMU virt only. No performance work; the code takes a deliberate double read of totalsize and writes the console a byte at a time and optimises neither. Clean.

PROPORTIONALITY. 280 added lines in one file, kernel/src/arch/aarch64/boot.rs; +5,860 bytes of image; one of six objective criteria closed, on the objective's declared milestone, with the last piece of a three-step sequence whose order the RFC argues for. Against weight 100 that is proportionate, and an elector who voted for "the kernel knows what memory it has, from the device tree rather than from constants" would recognise the six-size table above as the thing they asked for. I do not think they would be surprised by any part of it.

THE THRESHOLD, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WILL OUTLIVE THE CODE. From here the kernel reads a structure it did not write, and builds a slice whose length comes from a field inside that same structure. The shape chosen is: the arch file owns what can be known about an ADDRESS (non-zero, 8-byte aligned, both ends representable) and about the WINDOW (totalsize bounded against a compile-time ceiling before it is used as a length, one construction site, one unsafe slice); the portable parser owns everything true of the CONTENTS and re-checks the header against the slice it was given. Exactly one device-tree constant crosses into arch code -- that totalsize is the second big-endian u32 -- and it is there under a stated protest with the reason. The thing that could not be checked is named rather than papered over: whether the window is memory at all cannot be known, because knowing where memory is, is what the blob is for, and a range check against a constant would be the fallback the RFC and the objective's criterion 2 both refuse. That is the right refusal, and it is the shape I would want inherited.

WHAT WOULD HAVE MADE ME REFUSE -- the boundary, which is the sentence a later reader needs.

I would have refused if the kernel's new knowledge were not demonstrable on a machine. A map that is parsed, bounded, dropped and never measured is indistinguishable from a map that is wrong, and this is the third contribution to this objective whose consumer is a later task; "it will be read eventually" is precisely the sentence drift travels in. What defeats that here is not an argument, it is that one binary at six RAM sizes returns six lengths and my negative control stays flat. Take that measurement away and this contribution becomes a promise, and I would have voted against it.

Two forward edges of the same boundary, stated now so they are on the record before they are convenient:

  A fourth consecutive contribution to objective 0002 whose payoff lands elsewhere does not get this verdict from me. Criterion 3 -- frames allocated and freed with a test that exhausts and recovers the pool -- has to be the next thing that lands. If the map's consumer slips again, the honest reading is that this objective is accumulating apparatus rather than meeting criteria, and I will say so.

  The growth argument is fine once. 4,100 bytes for a parser entering the image and 1,700 for the failure strings is a defensible purchase of the one criterion this closes. Made four more times with nothing in the tree that would notice, it spends nano by accumulation rather than by decision -- and criterion 6 is deferred, not cleared, so nobody is authorised to discover later that the sum is fine. ci/build.sh --size measures the image and enforces it, which is the axis that has a check; [budget.boot_memory] has none, and the blob alone is 1 MiB against nano's boot-memory budget. That gap is already filed with an owner in tasks/open/T-0008.toml and is not this branch's to close.

IS AN INVARIANT THAT LIVES ONLY IN A COMMENT AN INVARIANT. No. It is a hope with good provenance. The rule that no kernel may hardcode the blob's address is true -- I measured x0 moving from 0x40400000 at 8M to 0x48000000 at 512M and 1G -- and nothing in ci/ tests it: boot-test.sh boots at exactly one RAM size. A future patch that replaced this parse with two constants matching the 128M machine would pass build, clippy, size, boot-test and every constitution check, and the only thing standing between that patch and main would be a judge who happened to boot at a second size. The cheapest durable defence is a second -m in the boot test, which is one line, is not writable from this branch (the task's does_not_touch names ci/ for exactly the reason the RFC gives), and is already owned. I raise it because today's evidence is a measurement that expires, and criterion 2 is the one criterion of this objective that can silently become false again after it has been met.

CONTAMINATION. The C-0038 record held three verdict files from outside the panel when I read it and no panel verdict; I deliberately did not open them, since code quality is not my question and their content could only narrow my reading. No commit message, task file or RFC I read carried any panel direction on C-0038. Two panel verdict files appeared in that directory while I was still working -- I saw the filenames in a directory listing, opened neither, and this verdict was written without them; I record the fact rather than claim the room was empty. The briefing I was given did name one residual precisely enough that checking it was a code read rather than a discovery -- I treated it as a claim to verify and it verifies against the code in the direction of the code being right and a sentence being wrong (see findings). The same briefing warned that earlier statements of this mandate had been wrong, so I read roadmap/0002 myself; what I read is what I judged against.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY, and would want a reader to discount accordingly. I did not re-run the magic-corruption proof under gdb on a halted machine, nor the garbage-x0 fault matrix (the SKYNET_FAULT / ESR / FAR figures); those are the submission's numbers and I neither confirmed nor contradicted them. I did not audit the parser's internals -- merged code, and not this contribution. I did not establish whether some value of x0 hangs rather than faults; the submission says it could not either, which I regard as the correct disclosure rather than a gap. And after the /tmp reset I had no toolchain, so none of my own figures could be re-taken at the end; they stand as recorded above with their commands.

findings.issue: The one disclosed residual understates the reach it discloses, by about five orders of magnitude. The head commit states it as a general property — 'an x0 pointing at MMIO makes the kernel issue one real bus read of one device register, which for the PL011 at +4 is harmless, and a device whose register at +4 has a read side effect would suffer it'. Two things are wrong with that as a bound. FIRST, the offset. `fdt::Header::read` opens with `slice_at(blob, 0, HEADER_LEN)` and a `try_into()` into a `[u8; 40]` — a forty-byte read starting at OFFSET 0, unconditional the moment the value at +4 reads at least 40. So the first register touched is at +0, which is precisely the offset the sentence excludes; and on the PL011 that is this kernel's own console, offset 0 is DR, and reading DR pops the receive FIFO. SECOND, the extent. Once the window is built, nothing confines the parser to the first few bytes: it may read anywhere in [x0, x0 + totalsize), bounded only by MAX_BLOB_LEN = 2 MiB. I measured that rather than arguing it. On an 8 MiB machine whose RAM ends at 0x40800000 I wrote a fully valid forty-byte header at 0x40700000 with totalsize = 0x200000 (exactly MAX_BLOB_LEN, which the check at boot.rs:353 permits because it tests `>`), off_dt_struct = 0x180000, off_mem_rsvmap = 0x28 with a zero terminator, version 17, last_comp_version 16, and both extents in range — so every one of the twelve checks the commit tabulates passes — then `set $x0 = 0x40700000` at a breakpoint on *0x40080000 and continued. Console: `SKYNET_FAULT / esr 0x96000010 data abort / far 0x0000000040880002`. That is a real bus read at x0 + 0x180002, which is 1,572,866 bytes past x0, not four. The four MMIO addresses I probed (0x09000000, 0x09010000, 0x09020000, 0x0a000000) do each stop after one read, and I reproduced the PL011 case the commit reports — but that is a property of what those particular QEMU registers happen to return at +4 (below 40, or above 2 MiB once byte-swapped), not a bound the code enforces. Remedy is one sentence and needs no new measurement, mine is above: the residual is that a garbage or hostile x0 lets the kernel issue real bus reads anywhere in a 2 MiB window beginning at that address, starting with forty bytes at offset 0, bounded in extent by MAX_BLOB_LEN and in consequence by the fault path, and not bounded in location by anything, because locating it is what the blob is for.
findings.why_it_matters: Invariant 3 is enforced now, and this is not a stale figure in a comment — it is the accepted-residual sentence for the single moment in this kernel's history when it first trusts an input it did not write, and it is about to be frozen in the ledger's evidence digest. A reader at M4 or M9 who wants to know whether anyone thought about the exposure will read this paragraph, conclude the blast radius was one device register at one offset, and design on that. The true figure changes the engineering: a 2 MiB read window at an attacker-chosen base on a board with side-effecting registers is a different risk from a single probe, and it is the argument for whatever eventually bounds it — an IOMMU, a firmware-supplied range, or a memory map handed in rather than pointed at. A well-formed record of an understated claim carries the authority of the ledger, which is exactly why this one has to be right. I considered blocking and did not, for four reasons: the code is correct and the fix changes no code; the fault path is a real backstop and I could not break it in seven attempts; MAX_BLOB_LEN is a genuine extent bound checked before the window exists; and RFC-0003 section 1 already states the unbounded-window property in general terms, so this record is not the only place a reader can learn it.

findings.issue: `blob_at` returns `&'static [u8]` over memory the kernel does not own, and the justification for the lifetime is four facts that all expire. The SAFETY block argues no aliasing and no mutation because 'there is no allocator yet, which is precisely what this map is for', because it is single-core, because interrupts are masked, and because no DMA engine is running. Every one of those is true today and none is a property of the region — they are properties of M1. T-0007 brings the allocator that may hand out the blob's own frames (tasks/open/T-0007.toml and RFC-0003 O-10 both name the question of whether they are released); SMP and DMA follow. `'static` is precisely the lifetime that lets the window be stored in a global, in `BootResources`, or anywhere else, with the compiler raising no objection at the moment the storing happens. Today it does not escape and I verified that rather than assuming it: `blob_at` is private, its result is consumed inside `memory_map`, `fdt::parse` copies into a `MemoryMap` by value and retains no reference (fdt.rs:207-217), and `_map` is dropped. So the containment is real — it is simply a property of the current call graph, stated in a comment, and checked by nothing. The structural alternative is cheap while there is one caller: give `blob_at` the shape `fn with_blob<R>(dtb: u64, f: impl FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R) -> Result<R, Reason>`, so the window cannot outlive the call and the containment stops being a sentence.
findings.why_it_matters: Fine once, wrong as precedent, and the precedent is the point: this is the only place in the kernel where a `&[u8]` exists over arbitrary physical memory the kernel did not write, and the shape chosen here is the shape the second such site will copy. A `'static` slice over foreign memory is the exact object that invariant 1 has no vocabulary for — it is reach without a handoff, and its only confinement is that nobody has yet written the line that stores it. That line will be one line, it will look like an optimisation ('parse it once, keep it for T-0007'), and no check in this tree would see it: `--check reach-around` says so itself, 'bounds the named route only — a raw address cast is not visible here, and needs M4'. Three lines now, a change to every holder later.

findings.issue: Invariant 4's mechanical check cannot see a regression, only a ceiling, and the prose claims otherwise. CONSTITUTION.md says 'They are measured on every contribution. A regression is a failure, not a discussion.' The check behind it is `ci/gate.sh --check budgets`, which is `cond_budgets` at ci/gate.sh:80, which is `ci/build.sh --size`, which computes `size <= budget` and a percentage and nothing else — `grep -n budget ci/gate.sh ci/build.sh` finds no comparison against any baseline, and nothing in the tree builds the merge-base. THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT RATHER THAN AN OPINION, which I ran: build the merge-base and the head the same way in two private clones, then diff the section table. `readelf -SW` on both ELFs gives .text 0x928 -> 0x198c (+4,196) and .rodata 0x2e4 -> 0x968 (+1,668) for an image delta of +5,860; `nm --print-size --size-sort` attributes 2,396 of the .text growth to `boot_rust` with `fdt::parse` inlined into it and 736 more to `Walk::close_node`; and the .rodata growth is within seven bytes of the diagnostic vocabulary computed independently from source (948 bytes of match-arm literals, ~201 of the four consts, and 32 sixteen-byte slice descriptors). The ratio is an artefact of a 7 KiB base holding a boot path and a fault path and no functionality; invariant 4 binds absolute bytes per profile, and 13,148 of 196,608 is 6.7% of the smallest profile in the tree. Roughly three quarters of the spend is a parser that objective 0002's second success criterion requires to exist, linked for the first time. The remaining quarter — about 1.66 KB, 12.6% of the whole nano image — buys thirty-three distinct strings for a path that stops the machine, which is the right trade for a kernel being brought up and is the first thing worth re-examining if nano ever gets tight.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a defect in an invariant's mechanical check rather than in this patch, which is why it is a note. It matters because invariant 4 is the one invariant whose prose promises a comparison and whose implementation performs a threshold, and the difference is invisible until it is expensive: a ceiling check gives an identical PASS to a necessary 5,860 bytes and to 5,860 bytes of waste, and gives it for as many contributions as fit under the ceiling. The remedy is not a new budget — it is that the number the gate already computes should be computed twice, once at the merge-base, and the delta printed beside the percentage. A growth that is defensible will read as defensible, and one that is not will have to be argued rather than absorbed.

findings.issue: The failure path this task scopes is clean, and the path that actually carries a firmware-supplied value to a console is the one nobody scoped. The task's criterion 5 asks that the failure path emit only compile-time constants, and `mem_fail` does — I checked the type, all three writes and all thirty-three strings. But on a bad x0 the outcome is frequently not `mem_fail` at all; it is `SKYNET_FAULT`, which prints ESR, FAR and ELR. FAR on that path is derived from x0: I measured `far 0x0000000009020004` with x0 forced to fw_cfg's base, and `far 0x0000000040880002` with x0 pointed at my crafted header, both of which are x0 plus an offset. Before this contribution x0 was accepted and ignored — `boot_rust(dtb: u64)` did not dereference it — so no value originating outside the kernel could reach a console at boot. After it, one can. This is not a violation and I am not asking for it to change: the console is the operator's own local channel rather than an outward one, invariant 5 binds emission outward, and invariant 2's first power is served by a stop that says where it faulted rather than one that does not. It is recorded because it is a threshold crossing that no criterion in the task file and no sentence in the submission notices, and because the reasoning that makes it acceptable — local channel, operator's own machine, no outward path — is exactly the reasoning that will need re-checking at M6, when there is an outward path, and at M5, when a console is a thing an agent might hold rather than a thing only the boot path holds.
findings.why_it_matters: Invariants 2 and 5 are both pending, so the record of what was considered at the crossing is the only enforcement there is. Criterion 5 was written against `mem_fail` and is satisfied; a reader at M6 checking 'when did an external value first reach a sink' would find that criterion, find it green, and stop. Naming the fault path here means the next person to widen what a console may carry starts from a true account of what it already carries.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
Approve. The code is right, the order is the argument and the order holds, and I broke it in the places it says it is safe rather than reading the places it says it is safe.

THE DOUBLE READ OF totalsize, which is the claim I was asked to test. The submission says the window's length is fixed by the first read so nothing the second read returns can widen it, and that the parser re-checks against the slice it was given. I did not accept that. I split the two reads with a hardware read-watchpoint on the totalsize field and changed the value in between, which is the only way to produce a genuine time-of-check/time-of-use gap on a single core with no DMA. One crafted header at 0x40700000, one binary, one instrument, three values, three different outcomes:

  first read 0x40 (64), unchanged   -> 'reservation block never terminates'
  first read 0x40, widened to 2 MiB -> 'totalsize is beyond the window x0 named'
  first read 0x40, shrunk to 40     -> 'structure block runs past totalsize'

The control is the load-bearing one: with the watchpoint in place and the value untouched the kernel walks past the header exactly as it would with no watchpoint at all, so the instrument is not producing the result. The widening case is TotalSizeBeyondBlob, which is precisely what the commit predicts, reached rather than argued. The shrinking case is the one nobody claimed and is the better news: the parser binds every subsequent bound to its OWN re-read, so a smaller second reading narrows the tree and the larger window is never used as authority. The claim holds in both directions.

WHAT I FOUND INSTEAD, by reaching for the thing the comment says is bounded. The disclosed residual is characterised as one bus read of one register at +4. `fdt::Header::read` opens with a forty-byte read at offset 0, and the window it reads inside is up to MAX_BLOB_LEN. I built a header that passes all twelve checks the commit tabulates and drove a real data abort to x0 + 0x180002 — 1.5 MiB from the address x0 named — with `far 0x0000000040880002` on the console. The four MMIO addresses I probed do stop after one read, and I reproduced the PL011 case exactly as reported, but that is what those particular QEMU registers happen to return at +4, not something the code enforces. That is the first major. The remedy is one sentence and my measurement is in the finding, so it needs no new work.

AND THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION UNDERNEATH IT: honest chicken-and-egg, not a constitutional problem. RFC-0003 section 1 states plainly that the kernel cannot check the window lies inside RAM because knowing where RAM is, is what the blob is for, and a range check against a constant is the rejected fallback in a different hat. What makes it survivable is that the authority is bounded in extent by a compile-time ceiling checked before the window exists, bounded in consequence by a fault path that works — seven garbage values of x0, five clean refusals and two clean faults, exit 0 every time, no hang, though I cannot prove no hanging x0 exists any more than the submission can — and bounded in lifetime by the fact that the window does not survive boot. The defect is not the residual; it is the sentence describing it.

ON THE 80%. Within the invariant's intent, and I decomposed it rather than opining: +4,196 .text, of which `boot_rust` carries 2,396 with `fdt::parse` inlined and `Walk::close_node` 736 more, and +1,668 .rodata, which is within seven bytes of the thirty-three reason strings and their descriptors computed independently from source. Three quarters is a parser the objective requires; the rest buys a boot that can say why it refused. 13,148 of 196,608 is 6.7% of the smallest profile. What is NOT within the intent is that nothing in this tree could have told the difference between this and 5,860 bytes of waste — `ci/build.sh --size` computes a ceiling, the prose promises a regression test, and the gate does run the check (the brief told me otherwise and the tree refutes it). The test that settles it is the two-clone section diff I ran, and it takes two minutes.

ON THE EMPTY RECORD, ruled here rather than passed forward. Two of the three are not defects and should stop being raised: `.gitignore:13` makes `/.forge/` untracked by design and says the ledger line is the permanent record, so an empty `evidence/` is an empty scratch directory and the digest that matters covers the record and embeds the verdicts; and an empty `signature` is explicitly exempted at ci/gate.sh:410, 'unsigned — permitted only for internal forge roles before G4', which is a decision rather than an omission. `prompt_hash` is the one that is live. It has no exemption anywhere — grep finds one line, the read — it was populated for C-0002 and C-0003 and has been empty for four merges since, and forge/prompts/README.md's third line asserts the opposite as fact. It does not block this contribution, because `.forge/` is untracked, is not in the diff, and `[task.scope]` bars both `ci/` and `.provenance/`, so no branch could repair it and rejecting a kernel patch would leave the fail-open untouched. The instrument is named, the line is named, and the fix already exists twelve lines further down the same file pointing the other way.

FOR THE M4 READER, because that is what this verdict is for. Invariant 1 was thought about here and the shape is deliberate. x0 is ambient authority in its purest form and irreducibly so — nothing can validate a pointer to the thing that tells you where memory is. What was chosen instead of validation is confinement, and the confinement is real: `blob_at` is private, the window is consumed inside `memory_map`, the parser copies by value and retains no reference, the map is dropped, `BootResources` is still two fields, and the minting-site count is still 4. Nothing here needs rewriting when capabilities arrive, because there is nothing left to mediate by the time `kernel_main` is entered. The one thing that is a comment rather than a structure is the `&'static` on the window — the lifetime that permits escape, justified by four facts about M1 that all expire, contained today only by a call graph nobody has written the storing line into yet. That is three lines to fix now and every holder later, and it is the minor finding.

WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR. I did not re-take criterion 1: verifying that the discovered region LENGTHS differ and match the machine needs temporary instrumentation, and adding it changes the image I would then be measuring. What I did instead is weaker and I am not dressing it up — one image, sha256 1e5a3204bc376c25…, booted at 8M, 64M, 128M and 512M, marker and clean PSCI exit at every size, which proves the parse succeeds against a real blob at four different addresses from one binary but says nothing about the lengths it computed. I did not boot the ELF for criterion 3; I forced `$x0 = 0` at the entry breakpoint, which exercises the same branch and produces the distinct string, but the ELF route itself is unverified by me. Whether the twelve checks correspond one-for-one to RFC-0003 section 1's list, and whether the Devicetree Specification citation at boot.rs:272 is right, are outside my lens and outside this tree — the specification is not in the repository, and tasks/active/T-0011.toml's routing rule says at length why a citation nobody in the tree can check is not something to rule on. The unit tests pass, 54 of them, and I ran them; I did not audit what they assert.

findings.how_established: nm on target/aarch64-unknown-none-softfloat/release/skynet-kernel from the private clone at 509db89, grep -iE 'stack|kernel_end|bss'; plus reading blob_at lines 315-393 and fdt.rs slice_at (line 224) and Header::read (line 289).
findings.issue: The aliasing clause of the from_raw_parts SAFETY comment is scoped to memory outside the kernel's own image ("The kernel writes nothing to physical memory outside its own image at M1"), but nothing in blob_at prevents the window from lying INSIDE it. An 8-byte-aligned x0 in the kernel's writable range, with a value <= MAX_BLOB_LEN at x0+4, constructs a &'static [u8] that overlaps the live stack fdt::parse is writing to while the borrow is held.
findings.why_it_matters: Measured layout of the submitted build (nm on the branch ELF): __bss_end 0x40083360, __kernel_end == __stack_top 0x40093360, STACK_SIZE 0x10000 — the image spans 0x40080000..0x40093360 and the stack grows down through 0x40083360..0x40093360. A window over that range is a shared reference to memory mutated during the borrow, which is UB in Rust's model and is the shape LLVM's noalias/readonly on a &[u8] parameter is entitled to exploit. No memory-safety consequence is reachable today, which is why this is not blocking: the slice length is the hard ceiling and every parser read goes through the three bounded functions, so the worst reachable outcome is a wrong MemoryMap that is immediately dropped, or a clean refusal. The clause is nonetheless not upheld on an input class the patch exists to defend against, and x0 is by construction the input the kernel cannot choose. The repair is cheap and does not touch what RFC-0003 section 1 forbids: rejecting a window that intersects [KERNEL_BASE, __kernel_end) tests the kernel's own link-time facts, not a board constant, so it is not the fallback constant the RFC refuses. This calculus changes the moment the map gains a consumer: if T-0007 lands a reader before this clause is closed, a window aliasing the kernel's own memory stops being inert. Routes to door 1 of [task.routing] as a new criterion on T-0011 while that file is open; if this contribution has merged, it is a new task.

findings.how_established: Read of kernel/src/fdt.rs lines 205-245 and 285-330 in the private clone at 509db89.
findings.issue: The double-read argument for totalsize is correct as stated, and it holds for a reason slightly stronger than the one given: it is not only that the first read fixes the length, but that the parser never indexes the blob except through three bounded functions, so no reading of totalsize — first, second, or a value that changes between them — can move a read outside the slice.
findings.why_it_matters: I attacked this specifically and it survived. fdt.rs:289 takes the whole 40-byte header in one slice_at(blob, 0, 40) before touching a field, so a truncated window is HeaderTruncated rather than an over-read; fdt.rs:317 rejects totalsize > blob.len() as TotalSizeBeyondBlob, so a second read larger than the first cannot widen anything; fdt.rs:224 bounds every other access with checked_add against blob.len(). A blob mutating under the parser therefore yields an inconsistent-but-in-bounds MemoryMap, never an over-read. At M1 that map is parsed and dropped, so the residual is inert. It stops being inert at T-0007, and it is worth writing down before someone relies on it: the map this path produces is not guaranteed self-consistent if the underlying memory is not stable, and nothing in the type says so.

findings.issue: The MMIO residual is disclosed accurately and its disclosure is adequate. The exposure is bounded to exactly one 4-byte volatile read at dtb+4, and the checks that make that read well-formed run before it rather than after.
findings.why_it_matters: The ordering the submission claims is the ordering in the file: dtb != 0 (line 316), 8-byte alignment (line 319), both ends of the field checked against the address space (lines 326-332), then the single read_volatile (line 344). Volatile is the right choice and the stated reason is the right reason — with the MMU off this is Device-nGnRnE, where gathering is architecturally prohibited, so a split or merged access is not merely a compiler liberty but an architectural violation. The read cannot be bounded further without knowing where memory is, which is the thing being discovered, so the disclosure is the correct disposition rather than a deferred fix. What the submission does not say, and what a later reader should know: because the offset is fixed at +4, the exposure does not grow with a hostile blob — a device with a read side effect at +4 suffers exactly one, and no sequence of inputs turns this into a sweep of a device's register file.

findings.issue: The optimiser residual the submission discloses but did not check — that discarding the work of filling an unread MemoryMap might take the error paths with it — does not occur in the submitted build. I checked it, since the author states they did not.
findings.why_it_matters: If the walk had been discarded as dead, the branches reaching its deepest diagnostics would be unreachable and their string data would not survive to the linked image. All eight sampled reason strings are present in the flat image, including three that are only reachable from deep inside the structure-block walk: 'structure block has no FDT_END', 'nesting is deeper than the bound', 'more memory regions than'. This is strong evidence rather than proof — string presence establishes the paths were not eliminated, not that every check executes — but it is the residual the author left open, and it resolves in the patch's favour. The disclosure was honest and the honesty was warranted.

findings.issue: Four unsafe blocks in the file, four SAFETY comments, and exactly one slice construction — the criterion 6 claim checks out by reading. Each comment states invariants rather than restating code, and each clause is separately checkable.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the part of the patch I would most want a reader in five years to be able to follow, and it is followable. The read_volatile comment names alignment, non-wrapping, the memory type, and why volatile is required, and each of those is a claim I could check against a line above it. The from_raw_parts comment separates non-nullness, the provenance of the length, non-wrapping, aliasing, and the 'static lifetime into clauses, and it says plainly what it does NOT claim — that the window is memory. That last sentence is the most valuable one in the patch: it names the residual the boot protocol leaves open instead of papering it with a constant, and the one clause I fault (aliasing, above) is legible enough to fault precisely because the rest is written this way. The single-core, interrupts-masked assumption underneath the aliasing argument is stated rather than assumed, which is what I check for; _start masks D, A, I and F at line 85 and nothing on the path to here unmasks.

findings.how_established: SKYNET_PROFILE=nano ./ci/build.sh then ./ci/build.sh --size, run twice in two independent private clones — 26db403 gave 7288 bytes (3%), 509db89 gave 13148 bytes (6%). Literal byte count by regex over boot.rs in the clone.
findings.issue: On the size question, which I was asked to form my own view on: +5,860 bytes, 7,288 to 13,148, +80%, 6% of nano's 196,608. I judge it proportionate, but the framing 'this is wiring' is the wrong frame and understates what was bought.
findings.why_it_matters: The growth is not glue. Roughly 1,717 bytes of it is the reason machinery (34 literals totalling 1,173 bytes plus 16 bytes of fat pointer each) and the remaining ~4,100 is the parser being linked into an image for the first time — a capability Objective 0002's second criterion requires, not overhead on top of one. Judged as 'the first real spend of this milestone's budget' rather than as wiring, 6% of budget for the kernel's entire understanding of physical memory is cheap. The 32 strings are the discretionary part, ~0.9% of budget, and they buy the property that a new fdt::Error variant cannot be added without someone deciding what the console says — the exhaustive match is the enumeration, which is worth more than the bytes cost. What would make it not proportionate, concretely: (a) if the per-variant strings became a standing pattern that grows without bound as the parser gains variants, since each one costs ~50 bytes forever and nano is the profile least able to pay for diagnostics it will rarely emit; (b) if nano and standard continue to carry byte-identical diagnostic text, when the profile split exists precisely so the frugal profile can carry a short code instead of prose — that is an RFC-level decision, not a diff-level one; (c) if the budget continues to be checked only at whole-image granularity, which hides that one feature consumed 80% of the image and that four more like it exhaust the profile. None of those is a defect in this patch. All three are the trajectory this patch is the first data point on, and invariant 4 makes the trajectory the thing to watch.

reviewer_verdicts.reasoning:
APPROVE. One major finding, no blocking finding, and the validation order survives the attack I was asked to press on it.

THE ORDER HOLDS. I tried to break the double-read argument and could not. The submission's own defence — that the window's length is fixed by the first read — is true but weaker than the property that actually protects this code. The real guarantee is that fdt.rs never indexes the blob except through three bounded functions, so no reading of totalsize can move an access outside the slice: fdt.rs:289 takes the entire 40-byte header in a single slice_at before touching any field, fdt.rs:317 turns a second reading larger than the first into TotalSizeBeyondBlob, and fdt.rs:224 bounds everything else with checked_add against blob.len(). A blob that mutates between the two reads produces an inconsistent MemoryMap, never an over-read. That is the correct shape for a TOCTOU on memory the kernel does not own: make the window immutable at construction and make every later read bounded by the window rather than by anything re-read from inside it. The order in blob_at is also the order claimed — dtb != 0, alignment, both ends of the field checked, the single volatile read, the MAX_BLOB_LEN bound, the wrap check, then one from_raw_parts at line 392, which is the only slice construction in the file.

WHY ONE MAJOR AND NOT A REJECT. The aliasing clause at line 392 argues that nothing else writes the window, and scopes that to memory outside the kernel's image. Nothing establishes the window is outside the kernel's image. With the measured layout (image 0x40080000..0x40093360, stack descending through 0x40083360..0x40093360) an 8-aligned x0 in the kernel's own writable range, carrying a plausible length at +4, yields a shared reference over memory that fdt::parse is actively mutating through its own frame — UB in Rust's model, and exactly the pattern noalias on a &[u8] parameter exists to exploit. I weighed blocking on it. I did not, because the consequence is contained by the property above: the slice length is the ceiling, every parser read is bounded by it, so no out-of-bounds access is reachable and the worst outcome is a wrong map that is dropped or a clean SKYNET_MEM_FAIL. The defect is in the completeness of a stated invariant on a reachable input class, not in reachable behaviour — which is the definition of major in my lens, and I would rather record it precisely than block on it imprecisely. It should not be left standing indefinitely: the repair costs a comparison against KERNEL_BASE and __kernel_end, which are the kernel's own link-time facts and not the board constant RFC-0003 section 1 refuses, and the finding's weight increases the moment the map acquires a reader.

THE DISCLOSED RESIDUALS. All three are disclosed rather than hidden and I judge each disclosure adequate. The MMIO read is bounded to one 4-byte access at a fixed offset, correctly volatile, correctly ordered after the alignment check, and genuinely unbounded-in-principle for the reason given — knowing where memory is, is what the blob is for. The optimiser residual the author left unchecked, I checked: all eight sampled reason strings survive into the linked flat image, including three reachable only from deep inside the structure-block walk, so the work was not discarded. Three sampled bad x0 values are not an enumeration and the submission says so; I did not enumerate either, and I did not find a hanging x0.

WHAT I CANNOT VOUCH FOR. I did not boot anything. Every figure I report is a build or a static measurement, and I have given the command behind each in the findings; the submission's runtime measurements — the three region lengths at three RAM sizes, the corrupted-magic boot, the ELF boot, the three garbage-x0 faults and their ESR and FAR values — I did not reproduce, and I do not vouch for them. My string-presence evidence establishes that the failure paths were not eliminated, not that every check executes; only a disassembly walk would establish the latter and I did not do one. I did not verify that the Devicetree Specification puts totalsize second at offset 4, and by the standard in this task's [task.routing] that is not a claim anyone can settle against this tree — the document is not in the repository, so I record it as unverified rather than swapping one unchecked citation for another.

ON MY OWN INSTRUMENT. I worked in a private clone of 509db89 with a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR, never in the shared worktree, and never in a bare extraction. That mattered and I can show it did: constitution-check in my clone reports 9 passed, 5 pending with no SKIP, so kernel-provenance — the check proving every kernel change on main arrived through a gate merge — actually ran and actually passed. An extraction would have skipped it and shown me a green summary that never asked the question. I took the before number in a second, separate clone of 26db403 rather than trusting the submission's, and both nano figures are mine. ./ci/build.sh prints PASS kernel built in my clone. No file in the shared tree was written by me except this verdict.
